title: Rwanda Senior Agronomist, Conservation Agriculture
raw_text: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli. About the Role We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Senior Agronomist with in-depth expertise and at least 6 years of experience in Conservation Agriculture and deploying farmer training in these practices in the field. Responsibilities Conservation Agriculture Strategy & Extension Development Develop and continuously improve scalable conservation agriculture advisory models in collaboration with farmer advisory and field teams. Design practical extension materials, training manuals, visual guides, and digital tools tailored to diverse farmer needs and contexts. Translate technical concepts including cover cropping, minimum tillage, agroforestry, and integrated pest management into practical field-based curricula. Adapt advisory approaches and materials based on climate, soil, socioeconomic conditions, farmer feedback, and field learning. Farmer Training, Field Deployment & Adoption Provide hands-on technical guidance to field teams delivering farmer trainings, workshops, Farmer Field Schools, and demonstration plots. Build the capacity of field staff and local extension agents to effectively promote and support conservation agriculture adoption. Provide timely agronomic troubleshooting to farmers and field teams addressing crop, soil, pest, and climate-related challenges. Work with MEL and field teams to develop and implement systems that track adoption, farmer outcomes, and opportunities for scaling. Agronomic Research, Practice Optimization & Impact Evaluate and refine conservation agriculture practices to improve soil health, water retention, biodiversity, productivity, and farmer profitability. Collaborate with R&D teams to design and oversee field assessments of soil health, crop performance, and environmental outcomes. Analyze field evidence and farmer feedback to identify high-impact practices and recommend improvements to conservation agriculture programming. Translate research findings and field learning into practical recommendations, extension content, and scalable implementation models. Partnership & Cross-Functional Project Leadership Build and manage strategic relationships with public, private, NGO, academic, and other technical partners supporting conservation agriculture initiatives. Coordinate project plans, timelines, deliverables, reporting, and data sharing across internal teams and external consortium partners. Represent the conservation agriculture program in technical discussions and ensure strong alignment between farmer needs, organizational priorities, and partner objectives. Identify opportunities for collaboration, innovation, and resource mobilization that strengthen program quality, scale, and long-term impact. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have: Master’s degree in Agronomy, Agroecology, Crop Science, Soil Science, or a closely related agricultural field. Minimum 6 years of relevant professional experience in agronomy, conservation agriculture, regenerative agriculture, or agroecological farming systems. Proven experience developing agricultural extension materials and leading farmer-facing training, capacity building, or advisory programs. Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-stakeholder projects involving government, NGOs, research institutions, academia, or private-sector partners. Strong hands-on experience working directly with smallholder farmers and field teams, with willingness to travel extensively and spend significant time in rural settings. Proficiency in English is required; additional regional or international languages are an advantage. Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Kigali, Rwanda Benefits Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits Contract Duration 2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance. Eligibility This role is open to all applicants; however, candidates with citizenship or permanent residency in Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, or Burundi are strongly preferred. Application Deadline 03 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis, which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. title: Young Economist Program
raw_text: MINECOFIN/BNR Young Economist Program with GIZ support 9th Cohort – 2026/2027 Background The Young Economist Program (YEP) provides an excellent opportunity for aspiring young Rwandan economists and helps create a strong “recruitment pool” of highly qualified Economists who can take up professional and leadership positions in the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN), the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR), and other government ministries and agencies. The program seeks to bridge the gap between academia, the workplace, and policy analysis, while equipping young economists with a strong understanding of the role of public policy in sustainably improving the well-being of the population. The program is implemented by MINECOFIN and BNR with the support of GIZ Rwanda. Since 2016, eight cohorts have graduated, contributing to a growing pool of young economists serving across key public institutions, including MINECOFIN, BNR, the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA), and the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR). Notably, approximately 90% of staff in MINECOFIN’s Office of the Chief Economist are graduates of the previous eight cohorts. The program is now preparing for its ninth cohort. The YEP combines practical experience with structured learning and mentorship. Participants gain hands-on experience at MINECOFIN and BNR, benefit from mentorship and seminars delivered by national and international experts, complete relevant online and in-person courses, and prepare and present analytical briefs. Their professional conduct and performance are assessed throughout the program. The program targets highly qualified Rwandan economists aged 30 years or below who hold at least a bachelor’s degree in Economics, Development Economics, Macro-Fiscal Economics, International Trade/Economics, Monetary Economics, Econometrics, Statistics, or a related field. A master’s degree in one of these fields is considered an asset. About the YEP 9 The 2026/27 YEP equips Young Professionals with the skills and experience required to work across different economic departments of MINECOFIN and other ministries and government agencies. The program combines three main components: (a) a continuous internship with on-the-job training and mentoring; (b) intermittent formal group training in applied economics, quantitative methods, and relevant software/s; and (c) continuous self-study, including a research project at a later stage of the program. Progress and performance are assessed throughout the program through performance evaluations and written tests. Learning outcomes By the end of the program, participants are expected to have strengthened their competencies in three core areas: Applied economic analysis and problem-solving: Critically assess economic and policy issues and apply economic concepts and analytical approaches to policy questions arising in the day-to-day work of MINECOFIN and other public Economic institutions. Quantitative and data analysis: Apply quantitative methods and relevant software/s for macroeconomic projections, policy analysis, and assessing the impacts of policies and external developments on the economy and citizens’ well-being. Communication and collaboration: Clearly communicate analytical findings and policy recommendations to different audiences, engage effectively with peers and supervisors, and contribute constructively to teamwork and institutional building. Location: Kigali, Rwanda Fixed Term: 6 months renewable once Positions: 20 Level: Trainees A. Responsibilities As part of the YEP training, participants will be assigned to MINECOFIN, BNR, and, where applicable, other government ministries and agencies for supervised on-the-job learning. During these assignments, participants will undertake the following training-related responsibilities: Young Economist – Key Responsibilities Conduct applied economic and policy analysis to support evidence-based decision-making, and policy formulation. Collect, manage, and analyze economic data using appropriate statistical, econometric, and quantitative methods and tools, including Excel, E-views, and STATA. Support macroeconomic monitoring, projection, and forecasting by analyzing key economic indicators, emerging trends, and development across the national economy. Analyze real, fiscal, monetary, external, and financial sectors developments and their implications for the economy. Apply macroeconomic and econometric models to assess policy options, economic scenarios, and effects of shocks on economic performance. Prepare analytical briefs, reports, and presentations to communicate economic findings to technical teams and policymakers. Support feasibility studies, project appraisal, economic and financial analysis, Cost-Benefit Analysis, and the implementation and follow-up of government programs and projects. Collaborate with government and development partners on economic research, policy analysis, and capacity-building activities. Participate in on-the-job learning, mentoring, teamwork, and continuous professional development, while undertaking assignments and receiving guidance and feedback from supervisors and mentors. B. Required qualifications, competences and experience. Qualifications Have an “A0” (3–4-year undergraduate) or master’s degree in one or a combination of the following: Economics, Development Economics, Macro-fiscal Economics, International Trade/Economics, Monetary Economics, Econometrics, Statistics. Comprehend public policy, and the relevance of economic analysis for public policy making affecting levels of living (poverty), environmental quality, and the distribution of access to health/education and economic opportunity. Be fluent in Kinyarwanda and English; knowledge of French is an advantage. Rwandan Nationals aged 30 years or below Practical Skills Proven research and (quantitative and qualitative) data analytical skills; Thorough understanding of Economic Models, Descriptive Statistics, Econometrics & Regression Analysis; Knowledge of Excel, Econometrics, Modelling, data management software/s; Proven solid English report writing skills; Ability to communicate well, work in teams, and prioritize tasks under deadlines. How to Apply Interested candidate should submit their application no later than October 23, 2026, at 5:00 PM. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application. Note: All attachments should be put together in one PDF file, not larger than 2 MB. Incomplete or late submissions (missing certain files) will result in automatic disqualification. An individual may participate in the Young Economist Program (YEP) only once. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for test and interviews. Apply

raw_text: VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT PHYSICAL and MENTAL WELLBEING SPECIALIST ABOUT FH FH Association Rwanda (Food for the Hungry) is an International Christian Relief and Development organization with a value proposition “We design, develop, and deliver catalytic solutions that build resilience so that children, families, and communities can flourish”. FH Rwanda has been implementing integrated relief and development projects in Rwanda since 1994. FH Rwanda operates in Ruhango, Muhanga, Gatsibo, Nyagatare, Ngororero, Karongi and Rulindo districts. Our Head Office is located at Umuyenzi Plazza, 2 nd Floor, Kisimenti – Remera. FH Rwanda has adopted an integrated programming model UNLOCK (Resilient Systems, Flourishing Communities) through various specializations: Asset creation, Productive learning, Mental Health & Physical Wellbeing and Disaster Risk Reduction. FH CULTURE All we do, and how we do it, seek to promote God’s beauty, goodness, and truth in a broken world. As such, we are defined by our ability to make people’s lives measurably better; our ability to deliver impact is the measure of our collective success. For we know that we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God has already prepared in advance for us to do. At Food for the Hungry, we operate under a set of values called Heartbeat Values. We are seeking to hire a qualified, dedicated and experienced “PHYSICAL and MENTAL WELLBEING SPECIALIST” to be based in Kigali headquarter. The jobholder reports to the Director of Programs. SUMMARY OF THE POSITION The Physical and Mental Wellbeing Specialist provides country-level technical support to strengthen the quality and integration of physical and mental wellbeing across FH Rwanda programs. The position provides technical guidance, coaching, training, and mentorship to program teams and partners in the design, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of culturally appropriate and evidence-informed interventions that promote holistic wellbeing among children, adolescents, families, and communities. The Specialist also contributes to program learning, innovation, evidence generation, partnership development, and resource mobilization, while ensuring alignment with FH's Re-IMAGINE journey, UNLOCK Program Model, PMWB Technical Programme Approach, Systems Practice framework, and relevant national priorities.MAIN KEY RESULTS Skills & Competencies Coaching and Mentorship skills - proven capacity to effectively manage and mentor staff with varying levels of experience. Systemic thinking - mastery of Systems Practice, Human Centered Design, and research methodology. Training and capacity building skills Interpersonal and Communication skills Strong organizational skills and attention to details. Proficiency in Google platforms, Microsoft Office products, and virtual technologies such as Skype and/or Zoom ResponsibilitiesDemand Driven Technical Leadership Support the design and planning of Physical and Mental Wellbeing programs and interventions in alignment with FH technical approaches and relevant national standards. Develop and adapt technical materials, tools, guidance, and knowledge products to support quality PMWB programming. Provide technical input to program teams to ensure interventions are evidence-informed, culturally appropriate, and responsive to community needs Support Program Delivery for Professional Excellence Provide technical guidance to program teams to ensure clear understanding and quality implementation of PMWB interventions at facility and community levels. Coach and mentor staff and partners to identify and address barriers to access, service delivery gaps, and community health system challenges. Support the development and implementation of appropriate facility- and community-based strategies to improve access to quality, responsive, and client-centered health and wellbeing services. Provide technical backstopping to program delivery manager to ensure activities are implemented effectively, on time, and in accordance with agreed quality standards. raw_text: Job Title: Fish Harvest ForemanLocation: KaganoReporting to: Harvest Supervisor / Farm ManagerContract Type: Full-time, on-site About Kivu Choice: Kivu Choice is Rwanda’s largest protein producer and one of the fastest-growing aquaculture companies in Africa. Founded in 2022, Kivu Choice is the sister company to Victory Farms, East Africa’s leading aquaculture platform based in Kenya. The company operates a fully vertically integrated aquaculture model, encompassing hatchery operations, cage-based grow-out, processing, distribution, and sales. Kivu Choice is also one of the country’s largest employers, with over 700 employees, and plans to grow to 1,200 employees within the next three years, reflecting its strong commitment to job creation and inclusive economic development. Over the next five years, Kivu Choice aims to scale into Africa’s largest and most sustainable protein producer, producing and distributing 30,000 tons of fish annually for the Rwandan market and for export across the region. Job Purpose: The Fish Harvest Foreman is responsible for supervising and coordinating all fish harvesting activities, ensuring that fish are harvested safely, efficiently, and according to the required quality, quantity, and production schedule. The role leads the harvest team and ensures proper handling of fish from the cage through crowding, netting, pumping, transfer, and delivery to the designated destination. Key Responsibilities: 1. Harvest Operations Supervise daily fish harvesting activities according to the production plan. Ensure the correct cages are harvested according to the schedule and instructions. Coordinate crowding, netting, and pumping activities. Ensure fish are handled carefully to minimize stress, damage, and mortality. Monitor harvest rates and ensure production targets are achieved. Ensure harvesting activities are carried out according to approved procedures. 2. Team Supervision Allocate duties to harvest team members and supervise their performance. Conduct daily checklists before harvesting activities. Ensure employees follow correct harvesting procedures and work instructions. Monitor attendance, discipline, productivity, and adherence to company procedures. Train new team members on safe and correct fish-handling and harvesting practices. Provide guidance and support to team members to ensure efficient harvesting operations. 3. Fish Quality & Handling Ensure fish are handled hygienically throughout the harvesting process. Monitor fish condition and report abnormal mortality, injuries, or quality concerns. Ensure harvested fish are properly sorted, weighed, counted, and transferred. Minimize physical damage, scale loss, and unnecessary stress during handling. Ensure fish quality is maintained throughout the harvesting and transfer process. 4. Equipment & Safety Inspect harvesting equipment before operations. Ensure nets, pumps, and other equipment are used correctly and safely. Report damaged or defective equipment immediately. Ensure all team members comply with health and safety requirements. Stop unsafe work and report incidents or near misses. Ensure harvesting equipment is properly maintained and available when required. 5. Records & Reporting Complete and maintain daily pump and cage inspection checklists. Report daily harvest performance to the supervisor or manager. Maintain accurate records of harvest quantity, fish numbers, biomass, and other relevant information. Communicate operational challenges or deviations immediately. Ensure all required harvest records are accurate and submitted on time. 6. Coordination Coordinate with Production, Cage Operations, Logistics, Quality, and Processing/Dispatch teams. Ensure harvested fish are transferred on time to the designated destination. Communicate changes to the harvest plan to the team. Support smooth coordination between harvesting and downstream operations. 7. Health, Safety & Compliance Ensure compliance with company health, safety, and environmental procedures. Identify and report workplace hazards and operational risks. Ensure team members follow safe working practices. Maintain a clean and safe working environment during harvesting activities. Perform any other duties related to fish production and harvesting as assigned. Key Performance Areas (KPIs) Harvest quantity and biomass accuracy. Fish mortality and handling losses minimized. Fish quality maintained. Compliance with harvest procedures and safety requirements. Equipment availability and proper utilization. Accurate and timely harvest reporting. Team productivity and discipline. Achievement of planned harvest targets. Qualifications & Experience: A degree in aquaculture, fisheries, agriculture, or a related field is advantageous. Minimum 1–2 years of experience in aquaculture, fisheries, fish harvesting, or a similar production environment. Previous supervisory or team-leader experience is preferred. Practical experience in cage farming, fish harvesting, handling, weighing, and counting is an advantage. Good knowledge of fish handling, welfare, safety, and harvesting procedures. Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills. Physically fit and comfortable working on or around water. Willingness to work flexible hours, including weekends and public holidays when required. How to Apply: If you are interested in this position, prepare the following: Job application letter Curriculum Vitae (CV) Copy of your degree and other academic qualifications Copy of your ID How to apply: Send all the required documents to our email address: recruiting@kivuchoice.com . Submission Deadline: 5th November 2026. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis as they are submitted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

raw_text: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili. title: Senior Creative Writer
raw_text: Description Job Title: Senior Creative Writer Reports to: Chief of Staff, UGHE, with a dotted reporting line to Cluster Lead of Evidence to Practice at LEAP center. Department: Marketing and Communications, Office of the Vice Chancellor Location: Kigali, Rwanda; occasional international travel required (20-30%) Position overview The Senior Creative Writer will play a key role in producing original, authored content that advances the external-facing communications and knowledge dissemination mission of the LEAP Centre, a new interdisciplinary center at the University of Global Health Equity (UGHE). The LEAP Centre aims to bridge academia and care delivery to advance global health equity through the demonstration of health systems innovations, capacity strengthening through training and collaboration, and the generation and dissemination of insights to inform policy and scale effective solutions. The Senior Creative Writer will serve as a skilled, self-directed author who can translate complex technical content into compelling written narratives for diverse audiences, who is experienced travelling independently to gather first-hand stories from program participants. S/he will develop and maintain a consistent editorial voice for the Centre, shaping the tone, style, and language through which LEAP communicates its work and impact in writing. In addition to supporting LEAP-specific priorities, the Writer will be a member of the broader UGHE Marketing and Communications team. Responsibilities Case Study Writing and Site-based Story Telling (Lead Responsibility) Independently plan and conduct site visits across Paul Fund project sites to gather documentation and material for case studies, including leading interviews with clinicians, patients, program staff, and community members. Lead the full case study development cycle from research to final publication: identifying compelling stories, securing access and consent, conducting on-the-ground reporting, and writing polished, publication-ready narratives. Build and maintain a growing portfolio of case studies that document health systems innovations and frontline impact, serving as LEAP’s primary evidentiary storytelling asset for funders, policymakers, and partners. Travel to remote or under-resourced sites as needed, adapting reporting approach to local context and constraints. Editorial Voice and Written Communications Own the development and implementation of LEAP's engagement and communications strategy, working closely with LEAP Leadership and the LEAP Program Manager. Define and uphold LEAP's editorial voice, the tone, style, and written language through which the Centre communicates its work, values, and impact, ensuring consistency across all written materials and channels. Develop engaging internal- and external-facing written communications materials that articulate LEAP's mission, activities, and impact for diverse audiences, including the OnePIH community, potential external collaborators, funders, and donors. Written products include newsletters, annual reports, briefs, op-eds, white papers, and other promotional or informational materials in addition to case studies. Manage and update written content across the LEAP Centre's web presence (including the LEAP landing page) and social media channels, ensuring consistency with PIH, UGHE and LEAP editorial standards. Translating Technical Content into Accessible Narrative Serve as the primary bridge between LEAP's technical and programmatic work and its public-facing communications, translating complex implementation findings, health systems data, and frontline insights into clear, compelling written narratives. Work closely with researchers, program leads, and implementing partners to extract key insights and develop written products that are accessible to non-specialist audiences, including policymakers, funders, and the broader global health community. Knowledge Product Writing and Packaging Lead writing and editorial support for LEAP knowledge products, including case studies, white papers, technical reports, op-eds, and learning briefs, ensuring content is authoritative, accessible, and written to a high standard. Provide communications and layout support for knowledge products, ensuring materials are visually consistent with LEAP and UGHE branding. Audiovisual Content: Scripting and Story Development Develop scripts, voice-over copy, and story treatments for LEAP video and multimedia productions, often drawing directly on material gathered during independent field visits, ensuring the narrative and messaging reflect LEAP's editorial voice and communications goals. Collaborate with LEAP leadership, the UGHE Marketing and Communications team, and site-based communications teams to develop content strategies for audiovisual storytelling. Events Planning, Communication, and Promotion Support planning, promotion, and communications for LEAP-hosted in-person and virtual events, including webinars, workshops, convenings, and launches, including travel to represent LEAP at sites as needed. Develop event-related written communications materials and coordinate with internal stakeholders to ensure timely dissemination and follow-up. Qualifications & Experience Education A degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Health, International Development, or a related field is required. A master's degree in Global Health Communications, Public Health, or a writing-intensive discipline is strongly preferred. A strong portfolio of published or distributed written work is required, including at least one or two long-form pieces (report, white paper, case study, or feature article). Experience Minimum of 5–10 years of demonstrated professional writing experience, with substantial experience in a global health, academic, or research-adjacent environment. Demonstrated track record of leading case study or long-form narrative projects independently, including field research, source identification, and interviewing, from concept through publication. Proven ability to work autonomously and manage complex writing projects with minimal supervision. Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality long-form and short-form written content, including reports, case studies, op-eds, and narrative briefs, for diverse audiences. Experience translating technical or scientific content into accessible, compelling narratives for non-specialist audiences. Demonstrated comfort and competence traveling frequently and independently, including to remote or resource-limited settings. Familiarity with global health, health systems strengthening, or international development contexts. Additional Assets Experience with web content management or social media writing. Experience scripting videos or developing story treatments for multimedia content. Benefits of Working at UGHE At the University of Global Health Equity, we invest in your well-being and professional growth from day one. Below is a range of our benefits; Medical Insurance (employee and legal dependents) Life Insurance (employee only) 13th Month pay cheque 23 vacation days Communications allowance including home internet Employee wellness program (Gym membership for employee only) Subsidised meal plan while in Butaro Shared housing while in Butaro Relocation allowance for employee and their legal dependents (where applicable) Work permit fees and processing (employee and dependents) Leave flights back home for employee and legal dependents (where applicable) Professional development opportunities to help you advance your career Choose UGHE for a benefits package designed to empower you—personally and professionally—so you can focus on what matters most: making a global impact in health equity. At UGHE, you will collaborate with a diverse team sourced from different corners of the world—gaining fresh perspectives, expanding your professional network, and accelerating both your personal and career growth through cross-cultural learning and diverse expertise. How to Apply Applicants should provide: (1) a resume, (2) a cover letter, (3) names and contact information of three professional references who can attest to work experience, and (4) copies of all degrees earned. Please upload your cover letter and copies of degrees as a single PDF file under "Additional Files" on the application page. University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Organizational Profile UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. raw_text: Job Title: Plant Manager(Processing)Location: Kigali, Processing PlantReporting to: Aquaculture Operations Manager Contract Type: Full-time, on-site (shift-based operations) About Kivu Choice: Kivu Choice is Rwanda’s largest protein producer and one of the fastest-growing aquaculture companies in Africa. Founded in 2022, Kivu Choice is the sister company to Victory Farms, East Africa’s leading aquaculture platform based in Kenya. The company operates a fully vertically integrated aquaculture model, encompassing hatchery operations, cage-based grow-out, processing, distribution, and sales. Kivu Choice is also one of the country’s largest employers with over 700 employees, and plans to grow to 1,200 employees within the next three years, reflecting its strong commitment to job creation and inclusive economic development. Over the next five years, Kivu Choice aims to scale into Africa’s largest and most sustainable protein producer, producing and distributing 30,000 tons of fish annually for the Rwandan market and for export across the region. Job Purpose: The Plant Manager leads the day-to-day running of Kivu Choice’s fish processing plant, ensuring that machinery-heavy production lines run safely, efficiently, and without unplanned stoppages. The role owns process control, preventive and corrective maintenance, and quality and food safety compliance across the plant, while leading shift teams and operators. As Kivu Choice scales volumes toward 30,000 tons a year, this position is critical to protecting throughput, yield, and product quality from intake through to cold storage and dispatch. Key Responsibilities: 1. Production & Process Control Plan and run daily production to meet volume, yield, and quality targets across all processing lines. Set, monitor, and adjust process parameters (line speeds, temperatures, and processing times) to keep output consistent. Develop and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) for every line and piece of equipment. Identify bottlenecks and lead continuous improvement to raise throughput and reduce waste. Coordinate with harvest, logistics, and sales teams so that raw material intake matches plant capacity and orders. 2. Preventive & Corrective Maintenance Build and run a preventive maintenance schedule for all plant machinery, refrigeration, and utilities. Lead fast troubleshooting and corrective repairs to keep unplanned downtime to a minimum. Maintain equipment history, maintenance logs, and a critical spare parts inventory. Manage external technicians and suppliers for specialized servicing and repairs. Advise on equipment upgrades, new installations, and capacity expansion. 3. Quality Control & Food Safety Implement and maintain food safety systems in line with HACCP, GMP, and ISO 22000 principles. Monitor critical control points and ensure corrective action is taken and documented when limits are breached. Enforce hygiene, sanitation, and cleaning-in-place standards across the plant. Prepare the plant for internal, customer, and regulatory audits (e.g. Rwanda FDA, RSB) and close out findings. Ensure full product traceability from raw material intake to finished goods. 4. Cold Chain & Product Integrity Oversee chilling, freezing, and cold storage operations to keep product within required temperature ranges. Monitor and record temperatures across processing, storage, and loading points. Work with logistics to protect cold chain integrity through dispatch and distribution. 5. Shift Leadership & People Management Lead, schedule, and supervise shift supervisors, machine operators, and line workers. Train operators on safe equipment use, SOPs, hygiene, and food safety practices. Set clear performance expectations, give regular feedback, and contribute to performance reviews. Enforce occupational health and safety standards and lead incident investigations. 6. Production Reporting & KPIs Track and report daily, weekly, and monthly KPIs, including throughput, downtime, yield, and waste. Analyze performance trends and present root causes and action plans to management. Maintain accurate production, maintenance, and quality records. Support budgeting for plant operations, maintenance, and spare parts. Qualifications & Experience: Bachelor’s degree or advanced diploma in mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, industrial, or food process engineering, food science, or a related field. At least 5 years of experience in a processing plant (food, beverage, dairy, meat, poultry, or fish processing preferred), including hands-on supervision of machinery-heavy production lines. Strong process control skills and proven experience running preventive and corrective maintenance programs. Working knowledge of quality control and food safety standards such as HACCP, GMP, or ISO 22000. Cold chain or perishable-product experience is a strong plus. Proven ability to lead shift teams and operators in a production environment. Comfortable with production reporting and KPIs such as throughput, downtime, and yield; good working knowledge of Excel. Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose equipment and process issues quickly under pressure. Rwandan national, or already holding the right to work in Rwanda (Kivu Choice is not able to sponsor work permits for this role). Fluency in English and Kinyarwanda; French or Swahili is an advantage. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis as they are submitted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

About FXB Rwanda FXB Rwanda is a registered Rwandan Local Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) rooted in Rwanda since 1995, and a member of FXB Global, carrying the legacy of François-Xavier Bagnoud into its fourth decade, across all four provinces and the City of Kigali. FXB Rwanda implements integrated development programs aimed at reducing poverty and vulnerability and promoting sustainable livelihoods, food and nutrition security, health, education, WASH, and economic empowerment. FXB Rwanda is currently seeking to recruit a qualified, motivated, and experienced Program Coordinator to support the implementation of the FXBVillage Project in Gisagara District. 2. Position details Job Title: Program Coordinator Reports to: Senior Programs Coordinator Direct Reports: Two (2) Unit Managers and one (1) Project Agronomist Number of Positions: One (1) Employment Category: Fixed-term contract of 12 months, renewable subject to performance and project requirements Duty Station: Huye District, with frequent field travel and supervision in Gisagara district Start Date: As soon as possible 3. Project background The FXBVillage program uses a holistic approach designed to addresses the multiple interconnected dimensions of poverty, including health, education, and income generation, to help the most vulnerable families become self-sufficient and graduate out of extreme poverty within a three-year period. From October 2026, FXB Rwanda is launching the implementation of the FXBVillage project in Kansi and Kibirizi sectors of Gisagara District in the Southern Province of Rwanda. 4. Purpose of the position Under the direct supervision of the Senior Programs Coordinator, the Program Coordinator will provide overall leadership, technical coordination, and operational oversight for the implementation of the FXBVillage Project in Gisagara District. The successful candidate will coordinate project planning and implementation, supervise two Unit Managers and one Project Agronomist, and provide guidance to the wider project team of approximately 14 staff. Monitor implementation progress, identify operational challenges and implementation gaps, and develop timely corrective measures in collaboration with the Senior Program Coordinator and relevant staff. Promote innovative, cost-effective, and context-appropriate approaches that strengthen household resilience and self-reliance. B. Identify staff capacity-development needs and facilitate appropriate coaching, technical support, and learning opportunities. Promote a positive, inclusive, and results-oriented working environment that encourages initiative, teamwork, innovation, and continuous improvement. C. Beneficiary management and sustainable graduation Oversee the identification, verification, registration, and follow-up of project beneficiaries in accordance with approved targeting criteria and project procedures. Ensure that beneficiary databases and household records are accurate, complete, regularly updated, securely maintained, and used appropriately for decision-making. Guide field teams in assessing household needs, monitoring progress, and adapting interventions to beneficiaries' evolving circumstances. Ensure that beneficiary capacity-building activities are relevant, participatory, and responsive to community needs, covering areas such as financial literacy, income-generating activities, nutrition, hygiene, family planning, sexual and reproductive health, HIV prevention, education, and child rights. Monitor household progress toward agreed graduation and self-reliance milestones, identify households requiring additional support, and promote sustainable livelihood strategies. Strengthen community participation, accountability, and ownership to ensure that project achievements are maintained beyond the project's completion. D. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Oversee the regular monitoring of project activities, outputs, outcomes, and performance indicators in line with the approved logical framework and monitoring plan. Ensure timely and accurate collection, verification, analysis, and reporting of project data. Work closely with MEAL staff and field teams to assess progress against targets, identify implementation bottlenecks, and recommend evidence-based corrective actions. Promote the use of monitoring data and beneficiary feedback to improve program quality, accountability, and implementation efficiency. Support the preparation and coordination of project evaluations, assessments, monitoring visits, and donor or partner field visits. E. Reporting, documentation and presentation development Consolidate and review high-quality narrative and quantitative reports, ensuring accuracy, consistency, timely submission, and compliance with donor and organizational reporting requirements. Prepare clear, evidence-based PowerPoint presentations for donor meetings, project review sessions, management meetings, stakeholder engagements, and field visits. Investigate recurring quality issues, identify root causes, and recommend preventive measures to improve construction quality and reduce rework. Track quality performance and use inspection and testing findings to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement. title: Operations & Logistics Manager
raw_text: Terms of Reference (TOR) – Operations & Logistics Manager Position: Operations & Logistics Manager Reports to: Academy Director Key Relationships: Academy Finance Manager, Educational Program Coordinator, Akagera National Park Management, appointed construction contractor and supervising architect Location: African Conservation Academy - Akagera National Park Contract: Fixed-term – 3 years. Start date: Estimated Mid-Late November 2026 Background The African Conservation Academy (hereafter referred to as the Academy) is a pioneering initiative that aims to address one of the most pressing challenges for conservation in Africa - the shortage of skilled, confident leaders to manage protected areas effectively. A purpose-built campus is to be developed for the Academy within Akagera National Park. Designed as a hands-on, applied training hub, the African Conservation Academy will deliver relevant, accessible training and development programmes for professionals from state, community, NGO, and privately managed protected areas from across the continent. Based in Akagera National Park, Rwanda, the Academy will immerse participants in the realities of conservation management - learning directly from a functioning yet evolving protected area. Position Purpose We are seeking an Operations and Logistics Manager who is committed to building Africa’s conservation talent. The role will ensure the smooth running of Academy operations and logistics by managing operational systems, resources, and personnel effectively in support of the Academy’s objectives. The role will also ensure a high degree of logistical and operational collaboration and alignment between the Academy and Akagera National Park. Additionally, during the construction of the campus, the Operations & Logistics Manager will oversee, with support of architectural supervision, the construction company contracted to carry out the build. Duties and responsibilities include: INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT AND MANAGEMENT Project manage the construction of the Academy campus, representing the Academy on site and serving as the principal point of contact between the Academy, the construction contractor and the architectural firm. Track construction progress, reviewing the programme, monitoring progress against it, assessing delay events and granting or refusing extensions of time. Manage the project budget, cash flow and payment of certified amounts within the periods set by the contract. Issue the Interim and Final Payment Certificates and the release of retention. Monitor the contractor’s staffing, working hours and labour records, and make recommendations to the supervising architect where consent to key personnel, or the removal of personnel, is required. Manage consent to subcontractors, including any nominated subcontractors, and confirm evidence of payments down the supply chain. Monitor health, safety, environmental protection and site security on the client’s behalf throughout construction, recognising that these remain the contractor’s obligations under the contract. Support the supervising engineer through any dispute arising under the construction contract, through final tests on completion of the construction, and manage the transition from construction into operation. Lead the planning, implementation, supervision and completion of infrastructure development and maintenance necessary post campus construction. LOGISTICS, STORES AND SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT Support the effective management, development, and operational readiness of the Academy and the day to day running of the facility, including but not limited to ensuring appropriate logistical support, equipment, and operational resources are available. Coordinate operations across the Academy and coordinate with Akagera Management Team to plan and implement those activities involving the park operations. Manage and supervise stores, procurement support functions, logistics operations and inventory systems, to ensure effective stock control procedures and uninterrupted availability of necessary supplies and equipment. Develop and manage systems that ensure accurate recording, accountability, transparency and efficiency in procurement and logistics processes. WORKSHOP, FLEET AND ASSET MANAGEMENT Supervise workshop operations, fleet management, maintenance personnel and vehicle drivers. Develop and implement maintenance schedules for vehicles and operational equipment, ensuring cost-effective practices are upheld. Maintain comprehensive maintenance records. Maintain accurate and up-to-date asset registers and management plans are in places for all vehicles, equipment, tools and operational assets. FACILITIES AND BUILDING MANAGEMENT Supervise facility operations and back of house personnel Develop and implement maintenance schedules for buildings, ensuring cost-effective practices are upheld. Maintain comprehensive maintenance records. Maintain accurate and up-to-date asset registers and management plans are in places for all infrastructure and associated assets. SYSTEMS IMPROVEMENT, COST MANAGEMENT AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY Develop and monitor operational budgets and ensure prudent utilization of resources. Identify and implement systems that improve operational efficiency, accountability and service delivery, without compromising operational effectiveness and safety. Establish performance monitoring systems for infrastructure, logistics and maintenance functions, Ensuring operational data, reports and records support informed decision-making. LANDSCAPE AND FIRE MANAGEMENT Work with Akagera Management Team to plan and implement a landscape restoration and ecological management plan for the Academy plot, integrating it into the park buffer zone. Lead the implementation of approved fire management plans and annual fire strategies for the Academy plot in partnership with Akagera Management Team, including fire prevention, preparedness, response and recovery activities. CONTRACTOR AND SERVICE PROVIDER MANAGEMENT Develop scopes of work, specifications and performance standards for contractors and service providers, with a focus on service delivery by local cooperatives where appropriate. Manage contractor performance to ensure compliance with contractual obligations, quality standards, safety requirements and project timelines, resolving any issues effectively. HEALTH, SAFETY AND RISK MANAGEMENT Promote and maintain a strong culture of occupational health and safety across all operational activities. Ensure compliance with the Academy’s policies, national legislation and industry safety standards. Conduct risk assessments and implement mitigation measures for all operations and logistics activities. Coordinate safety training, awareness programs and emergency preparedness initiatives. Ensure accidents, incidents and near misses are investigated, documented and corrective actions implemented. STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT AND COORDINATION Maintain effective working relationships with the Rwandan Development Board, local authorities, local communities, and other stakeholders in relation to operations and logistical activities for the Academy. Maintain close and effective relations with Akagera National Park in relation to operations and logistical activities for the Academy. REPORTING AND ADMINISTRATIVE RESPONSIBILITIES Prepare operations and logistics reports for submission to the Academy Director, as required. Monitor operational performance indicators and report on progress against agreed targets. Maintain accurate records, databases, plans, contracts, permits and operational documentation. Ensure compliance with the Academy’s policies, procedures, financial controls and reporting requirements. Perform any other duties assigned by the Academy Director that contribute to the effective management of the Academy. REQUIREMENTS A relevant tertiary qualification, or equivalent, in operations management, project management, logistics, conservation, natural resource management or a related field. Equivalent practical experience will also be considered. A minimum of 10 years' progressively responsible experience, preferably in large-scale project or operations and logistics management. Demonstrated client-side experience of building or infrastructure construction projects, working with contractors, architects and supervising engineers from design through to handover, is preferred. Proven ability to manage multiple complex projects involving multidisciplinary teams as well as contractors and service providers. Working knowledge of standard-form construction contracts and their administration, including programme and progress monitoring, payment certification, variations, claims and defects management. Sound financial management skills, including budgeting, cost control, resource planning, stock control, and procurement. Working knowledge of health and safety management, risk control and maintenance operations in demanding field environments. Excellent organisational, reporting, communication and stakeholder engagement skills. Demonstrated experience in engaging with government agencies, local communities, and a range of service providers. Strong computer literacy and the ability to maintain accurate operational, maintenance and inventory records. A valid driving licence and fluency in English are essential. Proven experience working effectively in remote, rural, and multicultural environments. Willingness to relocate to Akagera National Park. Demonstrated ability to work effectively under pressure in a dynamic and challenging environment. Excellent decision-making and tactical judgement in complex, and changeable situations with tight deadlines. High levels of integrity, professionalism, self-discipline and resilience. title: General Practitioner (GP)

raw_text: Job Description: General Practitioner (GP) Department/Unit: Ketamine Treatment & Research Center (KTRC)Duty Station: King Faisal Hospital Rwanda, KigaliReports to: Designated KTRC Clinical Lead / Head of DepartmentEmployment Terms: 1 year renewable Position Overview The General Practitioner (GP) will provide medical assessment, monitoring, and follow-up care for patients receiving ketamine-assisted treatment at the Ketamine Treatment & Research Center (KTRC). Working closely with psychiatrists, nurses, psychologists, and other healthcare professionals, the GP will identify and manage medical risks, respond to adverse events, and ensure safe, coordinated patient care in accordance with approved clinical protocols, hospital policies, and applicable professional and regulatory standards. Key Responsibilities Conduct medical histories and physical examinations, review medications and comorbidities, identify contraindications and drug interactions, and request appropriate investigations or specialist assessments. Assess patients' medical status before treatment and communicate relevant findings and recommendations to the treating psychiatrist and multidisciplinary team. Monitor patients during treatment sessions in collaboration with the nursing team and respond to medical complications within professional competence. Recognize clinical deterioration, adverse reactions, and emergencies, initiate appropriate interventions, and activate hospital emergency pathways when necessary. Assess medical stability and discharge readiness, provide post-treatment precautions, and coordinate referrals and follow-up care. Participate in multidisciplinary case discussions and collaborate with the clinical team to ensure continuity and quality of care. Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential clinical records, including assessments, monitoring observations, interventions, and adverse events. Contribute to clinical audits, quality improvement, safety protocol reviews, and approved research activities in accordance with ethics approvals and confidentiality requirements. Comply with hospital policies, infection prevention standards, medication safety requirements, professional ethics, and continuing professional development requirements. Authority and Accountability The GP shall perform medical assessments, monitoring, interventions, and follow-up within the limits of professional registration, demonstrated competence, hospital privileges, and approved KTRC protocols. The GP's responsibilities include: Medical assessment and monitoring: Identifying medical risks, assessing patient stability, and supporting safe treatment delivery. Emergency management: Providing initial medical care, recognizing complications, and escalating cases requiring specialist intervention. Patient follow-up: Providing discharge advice, coordinating referrals, and supporting continuity of care. Documentation and quality improvement: Maintaining clinical records and contributing to audits, incident reporting, and approved research activities. Multidisciplinary collaboration: Communicating effectively with the treating psychiatrist and other healthcare professionals. Psychiatric diagnosis, psychiatric risk assessment, complex psychotropic medication decisions, and psychiatric treatment planning remain the responsibility of the treating psychiatrist. The GP shall not independently initiate or modify ketamine treatment outside approved protocols and the established authorization framework. Decisions regarding treatment eligibility, continuation, postponement, or discontinuation shall follow the designated clinical decision-making process. Qualifications and Experience Essential Bachelor's degree in Medicine or an equivalent recognized medical qualification. At least two (2) years of clinical experience as a medical practitioner. Valid registration and current practicing license from the relevant Rwandan medical regulatory authority. Demonstrated competence in medical assessment, clinical decision-making, and recognition of medical emergencies. Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification, or willingness to obtain it within the timeframe specified by the hospital. Strong communication, clinical documentation, and teamwork skills. Commitment to patient safety, confidentiality, professional ethics, and adherence to clinical protocols. Preferred Additional training in general practice, family medicine, internal medicine, or emergency medicine. Advanced Life Support (ALS) or equivalent emergency-care training. Experience in outpatient, day-care, or procedural services involving patient monitoring. Experience in mental health, substance use disorders, or psychiatric comorbidities. Training or experience in ketamine treatment or ketamine-assisted psychotherapy. Experience in clinical research, clinical audit, quality improvement, or electronic medical records. Required Technical and Clinical Skills Medical assessment and clinical decision-making. Identification of medical risks, contraindications, and drug interactions. Patient monitoring and initial management of medical emergencies. Medication safety and clinical documentation. Emergency response, referral, and escalation procedures. Multidisciplinary teamwork and patient communication. Patient safety, confidentiality, and infection prevention. Basic computer literacy and electronic medical record management. The role requires a mature and confident individual who can work well with people from different backgrounds and personalities, including senior leaders, international visitors, donors, and other important guests. raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCES FOR RECRUITING THE PROJECT MANAGER(PM ) IN THE NYUNGWE AGROFORESTRY FOR COMMUNITIES AND CONSERVATION (NAP) 1. Background Initiative pour la Promotion de la Famille et du Genre (IPFG) is a women led organization established in 2002 and legally registered by the ministerial Order N0 17/11 of 31 January 2006 which was published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Rwanda O.G N0 10 bis of 15 May 2006. It is based in Gasaka Sector-Nyamagabe District- Southern Province. IPFG has a vision is to aspire a democratic society where both women and men are aware of their problems, complement one another and actively participate in the actions of the entire development. The mission of IPFG is to promote and reinforce complementarity between man and woman as well as their participation in the actions which aim to achieve social and economic development based on fairness. To achieve this mission, IPFG focuses its interventions across 4 main areas: i) Climate Resilience and Environment Conservation, ii) Sustainable Livelihoods and Economic Empowerment ; iii) Social Mobilization and Community Transformation and iv) Institutional Capacity Development and Sustainability. 2. Context From January 2024, IPFG in partnership with Livelihoods funds is implementing “The Nyungwe Agroforestry Project”, a 20 years’ Carbon project aiming to make a positive impact on 13,000 hectares of farmland, involving 23,000 smallholder farmers across the eastern border of the Nyungwe National Park in Nyamagabe and Nyaruguru Districts. The Nyungwe Agroforestry Project wants to improve the resilience of the farmers through rehabilitation of ecosystem services and increasing their adaptation capacities to climate change. Specifically, the project will help implementing communities: To grow agroforestry trees for various advantage, promote and improve good agricultural practices (GAP), reduce soil erosion, avail forest products such as timber and fuelwood at farm level, to improve soil fertility; and to increase income opportunities within implementing communities. In this regard, IPFG is seeking applications from competent, dynamic and self-motivated individuals to fill the following positions: 2.1 Project manager (1) He/she will lead a team of field officers and be based in Nyamagabe District. He/She will passionate, motivated, and driven individuals with an assertive attitude and good command in Kinyarwanda and English Language. Task and responsibilities Planning & Strategy Design work plans and follow up on them to ensure proper implementation. Ensure achievement of project targets within the specified timeframe (e.g. trainings, quality seedling production before onset of the rainy season, land preparation and distribution of seedlings). Team Leadership & Management Lead field teams and ensure field ethics are followed. Motivate and drive the team towards the shared mission of the project. Recruit farmers according to the project's ramp-up. Train field teams for effective project implementation. Communicate targets and operational procedures to field teams and project support staff. Ensure adherence to organizational policies and safeguards by project staff. Ensure the health and safety of project staff. Monitoring, Evaluation & Reporting Monitor the project through field visits and use of the Monitoring Information System (MIS). Report on implementation status and project performance. Ensure achievement of project impacts on farmers through monitoring. In close collaboration with the M&E Officer, provide regular field reports and ensure monitoring and recording of progress against the project's indicators. Stakeholder Engagement & Events Support the organization of trainings, meetings, workshops and other events for partners and stakeholders in line with project implementation. Manage and implement MOUs with different project stakeholders (e.g. tea cooperatives, farmers, RAB, etc.). Finance & Administration Ensure proper documentation of project budget and expenditure. Approve payments to Environmental Committees. Requirements Having a bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields: Agriculture, Agroecology, Forestry, Agroforestry,Development Studies, Project Management or any related field. Minimum 5 years of experience in managing projects related to agro-ecology, forestry &Agroforestry, carbon sequestration, natural resources management and/or environment protection or other development projects. Good knowledge of good agricultural practices (GAP) falling in the context of Rwanda, specifically in regions around Nyungwe National Park (NNP) High proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) and knowledge of GIS and MIS(Monitoring Information System) tools will be a benefit A good level of report writing, networking, facilitation and communication skills; Possess energy, drive, enthusiasm, commitment and passion for good quality work benefiting communities and environment. Strong verbal/written communication skills Strong leadership skills Strong problem-solving skills, creativity in decision making Having a driving license, cat A 3. title: Rwanda Quantity Surveyor Lead (Fixed-term)
raw_text: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. title: Regional Human Rights Specialist
raw_text: Regional Human Rights Specialist, Africa Rwanda Full-Time GLOBAL CONSERVATION Job Description Reports To: Director, Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) Location: Kigali, Rwanda (or another WCS Africa hub location) Country Program/Sector: APAMU /Africa Program Position Type: Full-time Scope/Capacity: Africa-wide Coordinates with: APAMU Team, Rights & Communities, Rights & Communities Regional and National Staff, Regional Leadership Teams, Country Directors, Landscape Leads, Protected Area Managers, Law Enforcement Advisors, Program Development Teams, and Technical Working Groups About Us The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a private, nonprofit U.S. organization founded in 1895. Its mission is to preserve wildlife and wild places by understanding critical issues, developing science-based solutions, and taking conservation action that benefits nature and humanity. With more than a century of experience, long-term commitments in dozens of landscapes, a presence in more than 60 countries, and experience creating more than 150 protected areas worldwide, WCS has accumulated the biological knowledge, cultural understanding, and partnerships necessary to ensure that wildlife and wild places thrive alongside local communities. WCS recognizes that nature and people are intrinsically linked, and that biological and cultural diversity are interdependent, mutually reinforcing and often co-evolved. Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities frequently represent the most active defenders of nature, and we believe that respecting and protecting the rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities reflects our global commitment to equity and justice and is our best pathway to achieving durable conservation. About the Africa Program WCS manages one of the largest conservation portfolios in Africa, supporting protected and conserved areas, community-led conservation, key biodiversity landscapes, species conservation initiatives, and wildlife law enforcement efforts across multiple countries. Globally, WCS also supports Indigenous and Traditional Territories, a growing opportunity to center guardians of nature and to secure their rights. The Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) seeks to ensure that conservation outcomes are achieved in a manner that applies WCS policies, principles and commitments. The Global Rights and Communities (R&C) unit provides guidance and tools across WCS countries to promote community conservation, ensure social safeguards and promote respect for human rights and positive relationships with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and other rights holders. This position will play an important role in coordinating and contributing to a standardized approach to human rights protection in Africa, with the guidance of APAMU, Global R&C and close collaboration with regional and country teams. Job Purpose The Regional Human Rights Specialist will lead and support the standardization of human rights integration and rights-based approaches across WCS conservation programs throughout Africa. The position will provide strategic and technical guidance to country programs and field sites to support human rights integration in conservation law enforcement, conduct human rights impact analyses, assist in investigation or fact-finding around human rights issues as requested, develop recommendations for country programs or landscapes to address human rights issues and risks, and oversee the review of rights-respecting Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for field operations. This position reports to the Director of Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU), and will play a critical role in the APAMU team in fulfilling the needs of a human rights based approach. The position will maintain a dotted line of reporting to the Senior Human Rights Specialist in Rights & Communities Global, for final approval and review of substantive human rights products and in order to coordinate with broader WCS policy and approaches outside of Africa. The position will also coordinate closely with regional and country level human rights, law enforcement, safeguards and communities staff. This position will require significant travel to remote field locations and sites where WCS works, and working with diverse teams from different country programs. The candidate will be expected to undertake planning and coordination as necessary with global, regional and country or site-level counterparts. Major Responsibilities 1. Human Rights Strategy and Integration Work with Senior Human Rights Specialist to ensure the implementation of WCS's rights-based conservation approach across all Africa programs. Coordinate with Regional Social Safeguards leads to support country programs and landscapes to integrate human rights into conservation planning, project design, budgets, monitoring, and reporting. Provide technical guidance on international human rights standards applicable to conservation programming. Promote alignment between WCS sites, country and regional level management, APAMU, and Rights & Communities. Support the development and review of organizational guidance, tools, frameworks, and operational procedures related to human rights. 2. Human Rights Impact Analysis and Risk Management Conduct human rights impact assessments and analyses for new sites and other situations as needed. Identify actual and potential human rights risks associated with conservation interventions and recommend practical mitigation and management measures. Contribute to the development and maintenance of systems for tracking human rights risks, corrective actions, lessons learned, and emerging trends across Africa programs. 3. Human Rights and Conservation Law Enforcement Work closely with the APAMU Law Enforcement Strategist and Senior Human Rights Specialist to provide strategic guidance on the integration of human rights principles into conservation law enforcement operations. Support law enforcement teams, site managers, and country programs to ensure that internationally recognized human rights standards are observed, and protocols are adequate for monitoring, and training. Support the development, review, and implementation of rights-respecting law enforcement policies, protocols, and operational guidance. 4. Development of Rights-Respecting SOPs Review Africa-level Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that embed human rights principles into field operations as needed together with regional safeguards leads, based on WCS institutional policies. 5. Training and capacity building Design and deliver human rights trainings with a focus on practical application of human rights protection and human rights-based approaches in the context of field implementation, community conservation and conservation law enforcement (or equivalent) 6. Other tasks as needed Review protocols and process relating to mainstreaming of gender equity, respect for the rights of Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and underrepresented groups in program design and management. Contribute technical content for donor reports and organizational reporting related to human rights commitments and achievements. Qualification Requirements Advanced degree in Law or other relevant field with a specialization in human rights; a first degree with relevant experience and certificates can be accepted in lieu of an advanced degree. Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in human rights advocacy, research, policy or monitoring and reporting. Proven experience working directly with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, civil society organizations, and/or government stakeholders in the context of Africa. Fluency in English and ability to work professionally in French. Desirable Qualifications Experience in conservation programs or issues relating to conservation. Experience with grassroots advocacy or human rights defenders. Fluency in Portuguese or African languages relevant to program areas. Core Competencies and Skills Technical Competencies Strong knowledge of international human rights standards and frameworks, and regional African frameworks Knowledge of both civil law and common law based systems for law enforcement. Understanding of human rights-based approaches to conservation and development including institutional due diligence practices. Demonstrated experience conducting human rights assessments and risk assessments and to develop appropriate methodologies. Understanding of gender integration, Indigenous Peoples rights. Experience developing policies, guidance documents, and operational procedures. Professional Skills Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills. Effective at organization, time-management, and self-directed field work. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Strong stakeholder engagement and interview skills. Ability to work effectively across cultures and multidisciplinary teams. Ability to influence and support change across diverse country programs. raw_text: JOB DESCRIPTION: TERRITORY LEAD Company: EarthEnable Reports to: District Operations Lead Location: Different districts in Rwanda Compensation: 320,000 - 350,000 RWF (Rwandan Franc) / month gross, depending on experience Who We Are At EarthEnable, we believe that our clients deserve our very best, that work should be fun, and that the best ideas could come from any part of the company. We celebrate each other’s wins, learn from our setbacks, and are deeply proud of the impact we make every day. We believe a home that doesn’t make you sick means more than living disease-free. It means pride and dignity in the place our customers most treasure: their homes. Being a part of our team means more than building housing products: it means building an organization and building a better future for rural families. What We Do EarthEnable is transforming the way people live, by making homes healthier for families across rural Rwanda, Uganda, and Kenya. 80% of Rwandans live in homes with dirt floors which are dusty, unsanitary, and fertile breeding grounds for parasites and germs. While replacing a dirt floor with concrete has significant health benefits (e.g. reducing diarrhea by 50% and parasitic infections by 80%), concrete is unaffordable for many who need it, and is also responsible for 8% of global carbon emissions. EarthEnable addresses this pressing and ubiquitous problem by selling high-quality, earthen housing products like our flagship floor that is 80% cheaper than concrete with 90% less embedded energy. Earthen floors, plasters, and blocks are composed of natural materials (gravel, clay, sand, and laterite) and sealed with a proprietary drying oil that makes them waterproof, strong, and polished. In our first decade of operations, EarthEnable has installed ~60,000 products for over 300,000 individuals and created livelihoods for over 1,300 people. See our new product - a full house - here! Position Overview The Territory Lead is responsible for the overall performance, growth, and operational excellence of their assigned territory. This role combines commercial leadership, operational oversight, and people management to ensure sales targets are met, construction projects are executed efficiently, and customers receive an exceptional experience. The ideal candidate is a proactive and results-driven leader who can translate strategy into execution, build high-performing teams, and operate with strong business acumen in dynamic field environments. Drive achievement of assigned sales and build targets while maintaining strong quality and customer satisfaction standards. Monitor territory performance through data and KPIs, proactively identifying risks and implementing corrective actions. 2. Equip teams with the tools, messaging, and support needed to effectively engage customers and convert leads. Champion customer-centric practices, ensuring a seamless journey from initial engagement through project completion. Strengthen relationships with cooperatives, institutions, local leaders, and community stakeholders to expand market reach and reinforce EarthEnable’s mission. Oversee territory-level marketing and activation initiatives to drive demand and brand visibility. 3. Operational and Construction Excellence Oversee all construction activities within the territory, ensuring adherence to quality standards, timelines, and safety practices. Align construction capacity with sales volume to prevent project delays and backlog. Partner closely with operations teams to coordinate material forecasting, ordering, and delivery. Track project progress and ensure timely follow-up on active builds, addressing bottlenecks before they escalate. Continuously identify opportunities to improve construction efficiency and reduce cycle times. 4. Financial Stewardship and Data Integrity Ensure customer payments are collected in accordance with company policies while maintaining the highest standards of financial accountability. Monitor territory-level financial indicators, including revenue, cost drivers, and operational efficiency. Promote accurate and timely data capture to support reporting, forecasting, and informed decision-making. Safeguard company resources by reinforcing compliance with internal controls. 5. Team Leadership and Culture Building Build, lead, and retain a high-performing territory team across sales and construction functions. Provide regular coaching, mentorship, and structured performance feedback to strengthen capability and accountability. Foster a culture grounded in professionalism, collaboration, continuous learning, and results. Model EarthEnable’s values and cultivate an environment where team members feel motivated, supported, and empowered to succeed. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Business, Sales, Operations, or a related field. Minimum of 3+ years of progressive experience in field operations, sales leadership, or territory management. Demonstrated success managing teams and delivering measurable business results. Strong operational mindset with the ability to balance commercial growth and execution quality. Experience working in fast-paced or growth-oriented organizations is highly desirable. Proficiency in data-driven decision-making and performance management.
