title: Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE EXECUTIVE COORDINATOR - ACE-AJ SECRETARIAT Position Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat Host institution Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda Scope Pan-African / multi-country Reporting ACE-AJ Founding Members, through the governance and hosting arrangements of ACE-AJ and LAF Duty station Kigali,Rwanda,withregularregionaland international engagement Contract Full-time; terms to be specified in the employment contract 1. Institutional Background and Rationale The African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice (ACE-AJ) is a Pan-African platform established to strengthen access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights and people-centred justice across Africa. Its origins lie in a continentally grounded feasibility process undertaken in 2016 through consultations with access-to-justice organisations in Kenya, Sierra Leone, Rwanda, Malawi and South Africa. The feasibility work examined the relevance, scope, sustainability, institutional form and operational requirements of a continental centre and identified the need for a stronger African voice, systematic knowledge exchange, research, learning, capacity development and collaboration among organisations working closest to communities. The feasibility process envisaged the Centre as more than a conventional project or secretariat. It was conceived as a galvanising space for access-to-justice and legal-empowerment actors; a repository of African practice and evidence; a platform for peer learning and exchange; a mechanism for strengthening community-based justice; and a vehicle through which African organisations could develop collective positions and speak with greater coherence on continental and global justice questions. ACE-AJ was officially launched in Kigali, Rwanda, in 2017. Since its establishment, it has evolved into a multi-country network bringing together civil society organisations and justice actors committed to expanding access to justice for poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities. The Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda, is a founding member and hosts the ACE-AJ Secretariat. ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 provides the current institutional roadmap. It organises the Centre’s work around five mutually reinforcing priorities: promoting holistic justice delivery; strengthening capacity building; research and knowledge generation; advocacy and communication; and strengthening the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The Strategy also places substantial emphasis on monitoring, learning, institutional visibility, membership growth, strategic partnerships and diversified resource mobilisation. 2. Purpose and Strategic Character of the Position The Executive Coordinator is the principal executive and operational lead of the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The purpose of the position is to provide disciplined continental coordination and executive leadership for the implementation of ACE-AJ’s Constitution, Strategic Framework 2024–2030, decisions of the General Assembly and Board, approved programmes and institutional commitments. The Executive Coordinator will move ACE-AJ from strategy to implementation. The office holder will connect a geographically dispersed membership, translate strategic priorities into annual and multi-year plans, mobilise resources, coordinate multi-country programmes, strengthen governance and institutional systems, generate and communicate evidence, develop strategic partnerships and position ACE-AJ as a credible African platform on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. The position therefore requires a network builder and institutional entrepreneur, not only a programme administrator. The Executive Coordinator must combine continental vision with implementation discipline; diplomacy with accountability; strong member relations with external representation; and programme leadership with fundraising, knowledge generation and organisational development. 3. Overall Accountability Serve as the principal executive focal point for implementation of ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 and approved annual priorities. Ensure that decisions of the General Assembly and Board are translated into clear workstreams, responsibilities, timelines, budgets, deliverables and measurable results. Lead the day-to-day work of the Secretariat and coordinate Secretariat personnel, consultants, technical advisers and designated support from member organisations. Maintain effective operational coordination with LAF as host institution while safeguarding ACE-AJ’s distinct continental identity, governance and member ownership. Provide timely, evidence-based advice to the Board on institutional development, programme performance, partnerships, funding, risks and emerging access-to-justice trends. 4. Key Responsibilities 4.1 Continental Network Coordination, Membership and Movement Building Provide proactive day-to-day coordination of ACE-AJ as a Pan-African network and maintain substantive engagement with members across countries, regions, legal traditions and languages. Develop an annual member-engagement architecture covering consultations, focal-person meetings, peer exchanges, communities of practice, thematic working groups, institutional visits and regional or continental convenings. Maintain structured two-way communication between the Secretariat, Board, General Assembly, founding members, and strategic partners. Map and continuously update member expertise, innovations, community-justice models, research, policy experience, institutional capacities and support needs. Strengthen member ownership by creating practical opportunities for members to lead research, training, advocacy, convening and cross-country initiatives. Lead strategic membership growth, with particular attention to geographic balance and stronger representation from underrepresented parts of the continent. Coordinate membership admission, onboarding, orientation, retention and an accurate, functional membership database. Identify common challenges across jurisdictions and convert them into collective learning, research, advocacy and programme initiatives. 4.2 Strategy Implementation and Institutional Performance Translate the 2024–2030 Strategic Framework into costed annual work plans, implementation matrices, institutional calendars and measurable performance commitments. Coordinate implementation across all five strategic priorities and ensure that programme choices remain connected to ACE-AJ’s mission, comparative advantage and member experience. Develop a Secretariat performance dashboard showing progress against strategic outcomes, programme commitments, membership engagement, partnerships, fundraising, visibility and governance decisions. Institute quarterly implementation reviews and prepare concise performance briefs for the Board. Identify implementation bottlenecks, emerging risks and opportunities and recommend corrective measures. Coordinate periodic strategy reviews and contribute evidence for the development of ACE-AJ’s post-2030 strategic direction. 4.3 Holistic and People-Centred Justice Advance ACE-AJ’s agenda on holistic justice delivery by connecting formal, informal and community-based justice actors and approaches. Promote recognition of community-based justice practitioners and strengthen their contribution to accessible, affordable and responsive justice systems. Support member initiatives that demonstrate how legal empowerment, mediation, community justice, legal aid and other people-centred approaches can complement formal justice institutions. Facilitate cross-country learning on enabling policy and regulatory environments for community-based justice and paralegal practice. Ensure that the perspectives of poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities remain central to ACE-AJ’s programmes, research, advocacy and institutional narrative. 4.4 Capacity Building and Peer Learning Develop and coordinate a continental capacity-building programme informed by member needs and the Strategy. Organise practical peer-to-peer learning, mentorship, technical exchanges and cross-country exposure among members. Develop partnerships with universities, legal aid clinics, professional bodies, judiciaries and specialist institutions for training, research and professional development. Promote learning models that draw systematically on the experience of ACE-AJ members rather than relying exclusively on external expertise. Support development of scalable training resources and, where feasible, longer and more intensive learning programmes for community-based justice practitioners. 4.5 Research, Evidence and Knowledge Management Lead implementation of ACE-AJ’s research and knowledge-generation agenda, including practitioner-driven and comparative research with continental policy relevance. Coordinate documentation of best practices, innovations, impact case studies and lessons from member organisations. Develop and maintain an accessible knowledge-sharing platform or e-repository for research, laws, policies, tools, case studies and member resources. Promote common or compatible data-collection approaches across members to strengthen the African evidence base on access to justice. Coordinate research partnerships with universities, research institutions and practitioners and ensure appropriate ethical, data-protection and quality standards. Translate research into policy briefs, position papers, learning products, advocacy messages and practical tools for members and decision-makers. 4.6 Continental Advocacy, Policy Influence and Representation Develop and coordinate ACE-AJ’s continental advocacy agenda, drawing on member evidence and experience. Support development of coherent African positions on legal empowerment, community justice, legal aid, people-centred justice and related emerging issues. Build structured engagement with the African Union, African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights, regional economic communities, United Nations mechanisms and other relevant regional and global institutions. Identify opportunities for ACE-AJ and its members to contribute to justice-sector reform, policy processes, legislative discussions and international forums. Represent ACE-AJ at authorised regional, continental and international engagements and prepare high-quality briefs, statements and speaking points. Ensure that ACE-AJ’s advocacy elevates member expertise and community experience rather than substituting for them. 4.7 Strategic Communication, Visibility and African Narrative Lead implementation of an institutional communication and visibility plan that establishes ACE-AJ as a recognised source of African expertise on access to justice and legal empowerment. Oversee regular member updates, newsletters, website content, social media, publications and other institutional communication. Develop a compelling evidence-based continental narrative demonstrating ACE-AJ’s added value and the contribution of its members. Increase dissemination and citation of ACE-AJ research, policy products and member-generated knowledge. Coordinate media engagement and ensure consistent branding, messaging and recognition of member organisations. 4.8 Resource Mobilisation and Financial Sustainability Develop, maintain and drive a diversified resource-mobilisation strategy and funding pipeline aligned with ACE-AJ’s strategic priorities. Map foundations, bilateral and multilateral partners, international organisations, corporate and philanthropic actors and other potential supporters. Lead or coordinate high-quality concept notes, proposals, budgets, partnership submissions and donor presentations. Build and maintain long-term donor and strategic-partner relationships and coordinate due diligence, negotiations, stewardship and reporting. Explore sustainable non-grant income approaches consistent with ACE-AJ’s mandate, governance and applicable legal requirements. Work with the host institution and relevant governance structures to ensure sound grant management, financial controls, compliance and transparent reporting. Strengthen ACE-AJ’s ability to demonstrate impact as a central element of fundraising and partnership development. 4.9 Programme Development, Multi-country Implementation and Accountability Design and coordinate multi-country and network-wide initiatives from concept development through implementation, monitoring, learning and reporting. Develop clear implementation arrangements with participating members, including roles, deliverables, budgets, timelines, reporting requirements and decision-making arrangements. Track delivery across countries and intervene early where implementation is delayed or quality is at risk. Coordinate narrative and management reporting to the Board, members, partners and donors. Ensure programmes demonstrate clear value to participating members and contribute to ACE-AJ’s strategic outcomes rather than operating as isolated projects. 4.10 Governance and Institutional Development Provide high-quality technical and administrative support to the Board and General Assembly. Coordinate AGMs, Board meetings and other governance processes, including agendas, briefing papers, minutes, decision registers and systematic follow-up. Maintain constitutional, governance, membership, programme and institutional records. Support development, review and implementation of policies, manuals, procedures and internal systems required for a credible continental institution. Ensure Secretariat operations comply with the ACE-AJ Constitution, approved policies, governance decisions and relevant legal and contractual obligations. Support the establishment and effective operation of thematic working groups, committees, patrons or other mechanisms provided for in ACE-AJ’s strategic and governance framework. 5. Expected Results and Performance Indicators ACE-AJ functions as an active, connected and member-owned continental network with demonstrably regular and substantive member participation. Annual strategic priorities and governance decisions are implemented, tracked and reported systematically. Membership expands strategically and becomes more geographically and linguistically representative. Regional and continental exchanges, working groups and joint initiatives produce documented learning and collaborative action. ACE-AJ generates and disseminates credible African evidence, research, best practices and policy products. ACE-AJ’s visibility and participation in relevant African and international justice platforms increases. A credible and diversified funding pipeline is maintained, with stronger donor stewardship and institutional sustainability. Multi-country programmes demonstrate timely delivery, accountability, learning and clear value to participating members. Governance, programme, financial, membership, partnership and communication records are accurate, current and accessible. ACE-AJ increasingly contributes an identifiable African voice to debates and policy processes on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. 6. Qualifications and Experience Master’s degree in law, Human Rights, Development Studies, Public Policy, International Relations, Governance, Programme Management or a closely related field. A strong bachelor’s degree combined with substantial relevant senior experience may be considered. At least 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights, governance, civil society strengthening, international development, network leadership or a closely related field. Demonstrated experience coordinating a network, coalition, secretariat, regional platform or multi-country partnership. Substantial experience working across several African countries is strongly preferred. Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into implementation plans, budgets, partnerships, programmes and measurable results. Strong experience in programme design and management, monitoring and learning, budgeting, reporting and institutional planning. Proven experience in resource mobilisation, proposal development and donor or strategic-partner relationship management. Experience supporting governance bodies and organisational/institutional development. Experience in research, policy engagement, advocacy, knowledge management or capacity development relevant to access to justice is highly desirable. Excellent written and spoken English. Working knowledge of French is a strong advantage; knowledge of other widely used African languages is an asset. 7. Core Competencies and Leadership Profile Continental network leadership and movement building. Strategic execution and disciplined follow-through. Member engagement, coalition management and cross-cultural diplomacy. Resource mobilisation, partnership development and donor stewardship. Programme leadership and multi-country coordination. Governance, institutional development and accountability. Research literacy, evidence use and knowledge translation. High-level writing, communication, advocacy and representation. Sound judgement, political and institutional sensitivity, integrity and independence. Ability to work effectively across borders, time zones, institutions and professional cultures with limited supervision. 8. Particular Profile Sought ACE-AJ is seeking an Executive Coordinator who can build an institution and a continental network at the same time. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging organisational leaders, practitioners, community-justice actors, academics, donors, governments, regional institutions and international partners. The person must be able to create trust among members while maintaining delivery discipline and accountability. Candidates should demonstrate through concrete examples how they have coordinated networks or multi-country partnerships; converted strategy into implementation; maintained active member participation; handled competing institutional interests; mobilised resources; built strategic partnerships; convened diverse actors; generated or used evidence for policy influence; and contributed to institutional growth, visibility and sustainability. 9. Reporting, Supervision and Working Relationships The Executive Coordinator shall report to the ACE-AJ Founding Members in accordance with the Constitution and shall operate within the agreed hosting arrangements with LAF. The Executive Coordinator will work closely with the Chairperson and other Board members, the General Assembly, member organisations and designated focal persons. For hosted administrative functions, the Executive Coordinator will maintain close operational coordination with the Executive Director and relevant departments of LAF. The Executive Coordinator will supervise ACE-AJ Secretariat personnel and coordinate consultants, technical advisers, interns, service providers and staff designated by member organisations to support ACE-AJ activities, subject to approved structures and budgets. 10. Eligibility and Right to Work in Rwanda This recruitment is primarily intended for Rwandan nationals and non-Rwandan nationals who are already legally resident in Rwanda and authorised to work in Rwanda. Due to the resources available for this position, ACE-AJ/LAF will not provide international relocation, expatriate benefits, or sponsorship for relocation to Rwanda. Applicants must therefore be able to take up the position in Kigali under an existing lawful right to reside and work in Rwanda. 11. Application Requirements Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae, a letter of motivation, copies of relevant degree(s) and certificate(s), and two professional references. The motivation letter should specifically demonstrate experience in coordinating networks, coalitions or multi-country partnerships and provide concrete examples of continental or cross-country coordination, strategy implementation, convening, membership engagement, partnership development and resource mobilisation. Applications should be addressed to the Executive Director of LAF, as host of the ACE-AJ Secretariat, and submitted by email to legalaidrwanda@gmail.com with a copy (cc) to ace.a2j@gmail.com The deadline for submission of applications is 30 October 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

title: Infection Prevention and Control / Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (IPC/MNCH) Specialist
raw_text: JOB ANNOUNCEMENT Introduction DUHAMIC-ADRI (Duharanira AMajyambere y’Icyaro) is a local non-profit organization legally operating in Rwanda since 1985 and based in Kigali, Rwanda. In the framework with ACHIEVE/PACT, the organization will be implementing the ACHIEVE Rwanda EVD MNCH Activity for Strengthening community and facility infection prevention and control to protect women and child in Burera, Musanze and Rubavu Districts. Project Goal: ACHIEVE Rwanda EVD/MNCHActivity will strengthen preparedness for Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease while safeguarding continuity of essential maternal, newborn and child health services. The activity builds on Rwanda's existing MNCH community-to-facility platform to strengthen three linked functions during an outbreak: prevention, early detection and referral, and continuity of essential care. Substantial investment already supports surveillance, laboratory systems, clinical preparedness, points of entry, infection prevention and control, and risk communication. An important gap remains in sustained last mile community preparedness and in the community-to-facility linkage. With the above background, DUHAMIC-ADRI is looking for suitable, proactive, and self-driven professionals to fill vacant positions in the mentioned districts of Northern and Western Provinces. GENERAL INFORMATION Employer: DUHAMIC-ADRI Vacant positions: 1 Project: ACHIEVE Project (Ebola Prevention & MNCH Integration) Contract Duration: 10 Months (Fixed-term) Start Date: Immediate effect before end of October 2026 Position: IPC/MNCH Specialist Job Title: Infection Prevention and Control / Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (IPC/MNCH) Specialist Vacancy Slot: 1 Duty Station: Musanze District (with regular oversight and travel to Burera and Rubavu Districts) Reporting to: Project Manager Job Summary: The IPC/MNCH Specialist will provide high-level clinical guidance, oversight, and technical mentorship for the ACHIEVE Project across Musanze, Burera, and Rubavu. The incumbent will be responsible for standardizing Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures specifically focusing on Bundibugyo Ebola prevention and surveillance networks and maximizing MNCH outcomes within targeted cross-border health facilities and community structures. Key Responsibilities: Lead the strategy, implementation, and quality assurance of integrated Bundibugyo Ebola prevention and MNCH clinical protocols across the three target districts. Conduct clinical mentorship and technical training for healthcare workers on Ebola case definitions, standard precautions, and safe MNCH delivery practices during outbreak threats. Collaborate with District Hospitals, Ministry of Health (MoH) emergency preparedness teams, and border-control stakeholders to align actions with national epidemic response guidelines. Monitor project indicators related to cross-border disease surveillance, IPC compliance, and maternal/child healthcare statistics. Draft operational risk-assessment reports and present project milestones to the project management unit and partners. Requirements & Qualifications: Education background: Bachelors’ degree in General Medicine ((MD) or Bachelor’s Degree in Nursing from a recognized institution. Registration with the Rwanda Medical and Dental Council (RMDC) with a valid license to practice is required. Working Experience: At least five (5) years of proven experience in clinical practice and IPC/MNCH Community health system, or healthcare program management, with a strong emphasis on infectious disease prevention, epidemic preparedness. Having an experience of working with NGOs will be an added value. Skills: Strong clinical mentoring, crisis management, reporting, and interpersonal communication skills. Languages: Proficiency in English and Kinyarwanda. The applicant must not be older than 45 years. How to Apply Interested candidates who meet the specified profiles should submit their application files in a single PDF document to the below indicated channel. The application file must include: A motivation letter addressed to the DUHAMIC-ADRI Executive Secretary. A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) highlighting relevant experiences and 3 professional references. A copy of ID, academic degrees and professional registration licenses/certificates. A copy of Driving license with Cat. A (to those applying on the Project Field Officer Positions). Application Deadline: October 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM.Submission Email:recruitment@duhamic.org.rw Notes: The candidate should specify the job title applied in the subject line Female and Persons with Disabilities candidates fulfilling the requirements and qualifications are encouraged to apply Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for written exams and interviews. Safeguarding Responsibilities: DUHAMIC-ADRI is committed to preventing all unwanted behavior at work. The organization has a zero-tolerance approach to any harm, fraud or exploitation of any person or child by any of our staff, or partners. DUHAMIC-ADRI reserves the right to seek information/investigation from job applicants’ current and/or previous employers about incidents of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment the applicant may have been found guilty to have committed or about which an investigation was in the process of being carried out at the time of the termination of the applicant’s employment with that employer. At any time, DUHAMIC-ADRI has the rights to check whether your previous organization complies with the safeguarding and protection procedures and take appropriate actions including contract termination.” By submitting the application, the job applicants confirm that they have no objection to DUHAMIC-ADRI requesting the information specified above. Done at Kigali, October 12, 2026 MUHIGIRWA Benjamin Executive Secretary Apply

title: Plant Shift Supervisor
experience_raw: Mid career (3 to 5 years of experience)
raw_text: JOB ADVERT – PLANT SHIFT SUPERVISOR Trinity Musha Mines Ltd is a Mining company focused on the production and exploration of Tin, Tantalum, and Lithium in Rwanda. Trinity Musha is currently inviting suitable candidates to apply for the following position: 1. Position/Job Title: Plant Shift Supervisor 2. Job Grade: C4 3. Department: Metallurgy 4. Report To: Metallurgist 5. Job Brief: Supervise and coordinate all daily operations of the gravity processing ensuring that production targets, recovery and grade requirements are achieved safely, efficiently and in compliance with company and environmental standards. 6. Responsibilities: The Plant Supervisor has the following responsibilities and duties: Operational Supervision Oversee daily operation of the gravity circuits including crushing, screening, jigging, spirals and shaking tables. Monitor feed rates, water balance and recovery performance to optimize plant efficiency. Ensure proper handling and collection of concentrate, middlings and tailings. Coordinate with the maintenance team for timely servicing and repair of plant equipment. Production and Process control Record and report daily throughput, recovery and concentrate grades. Assist in troubleshooting process problems and recommend improvements. Work closely with the Metallurgist to implement process control parameters and plant optimization. Ensure sampling, density and moisture checks are performed accurately. Team Supervision and Training Supervise plant operators and samplers. Conduct shift handovers and ensure clear communication of production goals and issues. Provide on the job training for operators on gravity separation principles, safety and equipment handling. Safety and Compliance Enforce company safety standards, LOTO procedures and PPE use. Conduct safety toolbox meetings and ensure incident reports are properly documented. Ensure environmental compliance (e.g. tailings disposal and water management. Reporting and Administration Submit Daily production and performance report to the metallurgist. Maintain accurate shift logs, downtime reports and maintenance requests. 7. Job Requirements: The Plant Supervisor should have the following education, experience and Skills: Diploma or Degree in Metallurgical Engineering/Material Science Engineering/Mining Engineering. 3-5 years of experience in a gravity processing plant (tin, tungsten, tantalum) Strong understanding of gravity separation principles and plant flowsheets. Experience in supervision, safety leadership and production reporting. Basic computer literacy (MS Excel, Word etc.) Trustworthy and have sober habits Basic mathematical and writing skills Supervisory skills Be able to work within a Team environment Professionalism, Positive Attitude and Excellent communication skills at least in English. Equal Opportunity Employer Trinity Musha Mines Ltd values diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, ethnicity, disability, or background. HOW TO APPLY: Applications should be submitted no later than Tuesday 27th October 2026 at 4 PM. Please click on Apply Here. Applications sent through other channels will be rejected. Indicating which position, you are applying for and addressed to the General Managerof Trinity Musha Mines Ltd. For other inquiries please contact the HR office on 0788525141/0788361758. Only applicants fulfilling the requirements will be contacted. Done at Musha, on 14/10/2026. Missionnaire Mbanza General Manager Trinity Musha Mines Ltd Apply

title: Avis De Recrutement D’un (e) Assistant (e) Comptable
experience_raw: Mid career (3 to 5 years of experience)
raw_text: Kigali, 06 octobre, 2026 Réf. : 2026- /BD/br/IFR AVIS DE RECRUTEMENT D’UN (E) ASSISTANT (E) COMPTABLE Brève présentation d’INADES-Formation Rwanda INADES-Formation Rwanda est une organisation nationale membre du réseau international INADES-Formation, Centre Africain de Formation. Présente au Rwanda depuis 1975 et constituée en association nationale en 1976, elle dispose d’un Bureau National à Kigali et intervient sur l’ensemble du territoire, sous la supervision d’un Conseil d’Administration. Son siège est situé à Kigali, dans le District de Gasabo, Secteur Remera, et elle dispose de bureaux régionaux dans les Provinces du Sud, de l’Est et de l’Ouest. Sa mission est de promouvoir le développement économique et social des populations, en favorisant leur participation libre et responsable à la transformation de leur société. INADES-Formation Rwanda accompagne principalement les agriculteurs et leurs organisations, les femmes, les jeunes et les communautés locales, en partenariat avec les autorités publiques, les organisations de la société civile et les institutions de développement. Pour réaliser sa mission, l’organisation met en œuvre des programmes et projets de développement avec des partenaires nationaux et internationaux, tout en assurant une gestion rigoureuse de ses ressources. Dans le cadre du renforcement de ses capacités institutionnelles, INADES-Formation Rwanda souhaite recruter un(e) Assistant(e) Comptable sous contrat à durée déterminée (CDD) pour appuyer son service administratif et financier. Intitulé du poste Assistant (e) Comptable(01 poste) 3. Objectif du poste Sous la supervision du Directeur Administratif et Financier (DAF), l’Assistant(e) Comptable contribue à la gestion comptable, financière et administrative de l’organisation. Il/elle assure notamment la tenue de la comptabilité, le suivi budgétaire et financier des projets, la préparation des paiements et rapports financiers, ainsi que le respect des procédures internes, des exigences des bailleurs et de la réglementation en vigueur. 4. Position hiérarchique Supérieur hiérarchique : Directeur Administratif et Financier (DAF) Relations fonctionnelles : Direction du Bureau National, comptables, responsables de projets, personnel d’INADES-Formation Rwanda et du Réseau INADES, auditeurs internes et externes. 5. Principales missions et responsabilités Comptabilité et trésorerie Enregistrer et imputer correctement les opérations comptables dans SAGE 100 ou tout autre logiciel utilisé par l’organisation Vérifier la conformité et l’exhaustivité des pièces justificatives Préparer les journaux et participer aux clôtures comptables et à l’élaboration des états financiers Effectuer les rapprochements bancaires et assurer le suivi de la trésorerie. Paiements Contrôler les demandes de paiement et les pièces justificatives conformément aux procédures, budgets et exigences des bailleurs Préparer et suivre les paiements des fournisseurs, prestataires, consultants, partenaires, salaires, impôts, taxes et autres dépenses autorisées Assurer le suivi des soldes fournisseurs, avances et liquidations. Gestion financière des projets Assurer le suivi comptable et budgétaire des projets financés par les bailleurs Veiller au respect des budgets, conventions et procédures de financement Préparer les données et éléments nécessaires aux rapports financiers et au suivi des dépenses. Digitalisation et gestion documentaire Participer à la digitalisation des processus comptables et financiers Assurer le classement, la numérisation et l’archivage des documents physiques et électroniques Mettre à jour les plateformes de gestion documentaire et veiller à la qualité, la traçabilité et la sécurité des données. Contrôle interne et audits Veiller au respect des procédures administratives, financières et comptables Signaler les anomalies et contribuer à l’amélioration des contrôles internes Préparer les documents nécessaires aux audits et contribuer au suivi des recommandations. Immobilisations et rapports Participer à la tenue du registre des immobilisations et aux inventaires physiques Préparer les tableaux de bord, états de suivi budgétaire et rapports financiers demandés par la hiérarchie. Autres responsabilités Respecter les politiques de confidentialité et de protection des données Participer aux formations, missions de terrain et autres activités liées à la fonction Exécuter toute autre tâche confiée par le DAF en lien avec ses responsabilités. 6. Profil recherché Le/la candidat(e) doit : Être de nationalité rwandaise Être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire (A0) en Comptabilité, Finance, Gestion Financière, Audit ou domaine connexe Justifier d’au moins 3 ans d’expérience en comptabilité, de préférence au sein d’une ONG ou d’une organisation similaire. Avoir une expérience en gestion financière de projets financés par des bailleurs et en préparation de rapports financiers Maîtriser SAGE 100 ou un logiciel comptable similaire ainsi que Microsoft Excel, Word et PowerPoint Maîtriser la comptabilité générale, analytique et budgétaire ainsi que le suivi des comptes de tiers et des projets Avoir une bonne connaissance des procédures financières et comptables des ONG. Une certification CPA ou ACCA constitue un atout. 7. Qualités personnelles et valeurs professionnelles Le/la candidat(e) doit faire preuve de : Intégrité, honnêteté, discrétion, rigueur et sens des responsabilités Esprit d’équipe, respect, courtoisie et sens du service Organisation, capacité à travailler sous pression et à respecter les délais Initiative, adaptabilité et ouverture à la digitalisation et à l’innovation Engagement envers le développement rural, l’inclusion, la justice sociale, la transparence et la bonne gouvernance Adhésion aux valeurs, au Code d’éthique et aux politiques d’INADES-Formation Rwanda. Bonne maîtrise du français et de l’anglais ; le kinyarwanda est indispensable. Le permis de conduire catégorie B constitue un atout. 8. Durée et lieu d’affectation Contrat : CDD de 12 mois, renouvelable selon les performances et les besoins de l’organisation, avec période d’essai conformément à la législation en vigueur Lieu : Bureau National d’INADES-Formation Rwanda, Kigali. 9. Dossier de candidature Le dossier doit comprendre : Une lettre de motivation adressée au Directeur du Bureau National Un CV détaillé, actualisé et signé, avec trois références professionnelles vérifiables Une copie certifiée/notifiée du diplôme requis Les certificats ou attestations de travail justifiant l’expérience professionnelle Une copie d’une pièce d’identité valide Les certificats de formation ou certifications professionnelles pertinentes, notamment CPA/ACCA le cas échéant Une copie du permis de conduire catégorie B, le cas échéant NB : INADES-Formation Rwanda se réserve le droit de vérifier l’authenticité des informations fournies et de contacter les références indiquées. 10. Modalités de candidature Les candidatures doivent être envoyées par e-mail à inadesformation.rwanda@inadesfo.net, avec pour objet : « Candidature au poste d’Assistant(e) Comptable ». Date limite : 21 octobre 2026 à 14h00. Seuls les candidats présélectionnés seront contactés. 11. Égalité des chances, diversité et inclusion INADES-Formation Rwanda encourage particulièrement les candidatures féminines et celles des personnes vivant avec un handicap. L’organisation s’engage à promouvoir un environnement de travail fondé sur le respect, la diversité et l’inclusion. Fait à Kigali, le 06 Octobre 2026 BIMENYIMANA Désiré Directeur du Bureau National INADES-Formation Rwanda

title: Procurement and Contracting Specialist
raw_text: Vacancy Announcement Procurement and Contracting Specialist For Country Office A. About GIZ The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH is a federally owned international cooperation enterprise for sustainable development with worldwide operations. The GIZ Office in Kigali covers GIZ’s portfolio in Rwanda and Burundi. GIZ Rwanda/Burundi implements projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Union and other commissioning authorities in the following priority areas: Sustainable Economic Development; Good Governance; Climate, Energy and Sustainable Urban Development; Digital Transformation and Digital Economy; and regional projects in the Great Lakes Region. GIZ Rwanda/Burundi would like to recruit a candidate for the position of Procurement and Contracting Specialist for the GIZ Rwanda Country Office. Location: Kigali Fixed Term: 12 months (renewable upon review) Position: one (1) Start date: 01 January 2027 The Procurement and Contracting Specialist performs the following responsibilities and tasks: B. Responsibilities The Procurement and Contracting Specialist Advises Head of Procurement and Logistics Unit on questions relating to his responsibility. Coordinates all queries received and ensures that they are dealt with promptly and competently, advises on legal and technical matters related to procurement and contracting Shares opinion before processing a decision inside or outside GIZ Provides a roadmap of upcoming operations falling under his responsibilities. Advises projects regarding procurement issues, informing them on time about the status of procurement, particularly in the event of delays Makes available expertise in the context of knowledge management and advises parties on issues relating to his responsibility C. Main activities 1. Dialogue with Head of Procurement and Logistics The Procurement and Contracting Specialist Contributes in effective and efficient operation and service delivery of the procurement and logistics unit in compliance with GIZ’s Process and Rules (P+R) and according to service level agreements Contributes to the achievement of the annual targets of the unit Cooperates effectively and efficiently with projects on ongoing supports Monitors closely procurement planning and provides regular updates on ongoing activities Handles procurement requests for local subsidies, financing agreements & Development Partneships Handles procurement requests for local consultants and consulting firm contract Handles procurement requests related to acquisititions of goods locally and from Germany Maintains the professional relationship between CO and projects as well as within the team 2. Dialogue with program managers (AV) and Program team The Procurement and Contracting Specialist Advises program managers/project team on questions relating to procurements and contracts. 3. Update the Market Situation The Procurement and Contracting Specialist Expert Updates local market situations to program manager and Unit Head 4. Other duties/additional tasks The Procurement and Contracting Specialist Expert Performs other duties and tasks at the request of management D. Required Qualifications, Competences and Experience Qualifications Masters Degree in Law or in Procurement or in similar field, recognised commercial Masters degree in business administration Professional experience At least 5 years’ professional experience in a comparable position Strong knowledge and sensitivity to compliance related topics, proven record of procurement experience with an international organisation Other knowledge, additional competences Outstanding knowledge of Contracting and purchasing Very good working knowledge of ITC technologies (related software, email, the internet) and computer applications (e.g. MS Office) Proficient in English, written and oral Excellent communication and organisational skills, distinctive social sensitivity Fully confidential and trustful, highly service oriented, accurate and attentive to detail, strong analytical skills Ability to deliver high quality work under pressure Willingness to upskill as required by the tasks to be performed – corresponding measures are agreed with management E. How to apply Interested candidates should submit their application (motivation letter, updated CV, certificates and references), via our electronic job portal by using the button “apply”; until 1st November 2026 at 4:00 PM. All attachments should be put together in one PDF file not larger than 2 MB. GIZ is a signatory of the Diversity Charter. Recognition, appreciation and inclusion of diversity in the company are important to us. All employees shall be valued - regardless of gender and gender identity, nationality, ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, social background, age or sexual orientation. We support equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities. This includes the provision of reasonable accommodation, if needed, in order to participate in the job application and interview process and to perform essential job functions. Please let us know if you have any particular requirements, should you be invited for assessment/interview or that you wish us to consider when revewing your application. Women and persons with disabilities are particularly encouraged to apply. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the test and interview. GIZ Office Rwanda KN 41 St. / Nr.17, Kiyovu P.O. Box 59, Kigali, Rwanda Apply

title: Impact Division Chief of Staff
raw_text: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. About the Role We are looking for an exceptional strategist and communicator to improve coordination between all of the Impact Division's workstreams. You will support the CIO in advancing One Acre Fund's Global Impact Strategy. Responsibilities The Impact Division supports all One Acre Fund programs to generate more impact, wherever we work. We help the organization keep three core aspects of impact at the forefront of our work: Improving farmer livelihoods in the short-term Ensuring long-term viability through sustainable agricultural practices (soil health, crop diversity, etc.) Addressing non-agricultural needs of farming households (energy, nutrition, etc.) The role of the Impact Chief of Staff is to support the Chief Impact Officer (CIO) in advancing our organization’s Impact Strategy. Three critical components of this role are to: Improve coordination of many different actors to implement our Impact Strategy. Increase the reach and effectiveness of Impact Division leadership. Lead strategic research, communications, or operational initiatives. Specific responsibilities include: Improving Impact Division communication & coordination around achieving goals Goal setting and tracking. Lead the annual development of OKRs aligned to organizational impact strategy; monitor progress against the strategic plan, OKRs, and other organizational indicators. Coordination across the Impact Division. Ensure fluid collaboration between technical support teams and operational teams through clear work planning and frequent, transparent communication. Increasing the reach of Impact leadership Conduct regular prioritization reviews with division leadership to ensure we’re tackling the most important problems. Serve as the Chief Impact Officer’s “whip” by moving complex projects forward. Represent the Division externally by pursuing early stage opportunities with partners. Take on direct or indirect management responsibilities from division leadership, as appropriate. Leading strategic Initiatives Lead strategic research or operational initiatives that: Are highly important to One Acre Fund and organizational leadership Sit outside the day-to-day purview of the current team Specific projects will depend on the candidate's background and interests, organizational priorities, bandwidth of implicated teams, and timing. Examples could include: Impact-focused internal campaigns Researching a new technology or partnership Team-building and culture initiatives Improving impact communications & Q&A forums Temporarily filling critical leadership gaps and recruitment of high priority roles. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. raw_text: We are hiring for Senior Systems Architect! Inviting interested candidates to apply by reading the job description below and sending applications to https://career.qtsoftwareltd.comstarting October 15th, 2026. JOB ADVERTISEMENT Duty Station: Kigali – Rwanda Deadline for applicants: 15th November 2026 Contract type: Fixed Term Renewable Submit CV, Cover letter, National ID and copy of Academic Degree to:https://career.qtsoftwareltd.com About the Company QT Global Software Ltd is a private company, engaged in web and mobile application development, information security consultancy, and network security services, providing secure solutions to esteemed clients. We collaborate with government agencies, companies, and organizations to create outstanding user experiences, secure solutions, and support and maintenance across the product/solution lifecycle. At QT Global Software Ltd, we continuously transform our operations to ensure that we provide reliable and cost-effective client-oriented IT services. We achieve this by assembling the best resources in software development, IT infrastructure, and security, as well as the best project leads. We are proud of our past accomplishments and excited about our future prospects. Our management philosophy and objectives revolve around two key principles: Firstly, we strive to become the preferred employer for the brightest and most talented minds in the region. Secondly, we prioritize the development, recognition, and rewarding of performance that we deem crucial to our long-term success and sustainability. Company Values All staff at QT Global Software Ltd are connected to a shared set of organizational values: Quality Customer Service Professional Business Conduct Client-Oriented and Secure Solutions 1.Position purpose Reporting directly to the Enterprise architecture Lead as part of the central architecture function, the Senior Systems Architect coordinates the design and governance of end-to-end enterprise and project systems, ensuring that applications, integration services, data platforms, infrastructure, networks, identity and cybersecurity controls operate as a coherent, secure, reliable, interoperable and sustainable whole. The role translates business and non-functional requirements into implementable architectures and provides cross-project technical assurance from solution selection through deployment and evolution. 2. Scope and interfaces The position serves architecture function across multiple technology projects and platforms, including new development, legacy modernization and third-party integrations. Collaborate with senior software developers and technical leads (application design), infrastructure and DevOps teams (hosting and operations), cybersecurity (controls and risk), data teams (information architecture), project managers and business analysts (scope and requirements), QA (quality attributes), vendors and relevant client technical representatives. 3. Key responsibilities / Terms of Reference A. Enterprise and end-to-end systems architecture Own solution-context and end-to-end system blueprints covering applications, interfaces, integration/middleware, data, compute, storage, networks, identity, security and operations. Define current-state, target-state and transition architectures; maintain architecture principles, reference patterns, technology standards and multi-project roadmaps. Lead technical discovery and assess functional and non-functional requirements, constraints, dependencies, capacity assumptions and technology options with stakeholders. Evaluate build-versus-buy, cloud versus on-premises/hybrid deployment, monolith versus service decomposition, and interoperability choices based on demonstrable requirements and total cost of ownership. B. Integration, interoperability and data architecture Design integration approaches using APIs, messaging/event streaming, service gateways, integration platforms, batch pipelines and appropriate interface contracts. Specify authentication, authorization, API lifecycle, versioning, throttling, retries, idempotency, error handling, auditability and service-level expectations across systems. Partner with data specialists on data flows, data ownership, master/reference data, databases, data security, retention, quality, backup and recovery. Assess interoperability standards and third-party systems, avoiding unnecessary duplication of platforms and vendor lock-in where practicable. C. Infrastructure, reliability and performance architecture Architect deployment topologies for data centers, private/public cloud and hybrid environments, including compute, container platforms, storage, networking, DNS, load balancing and connectivity. Define measurable capacity, latency, throughput, availability, resilience, scalability, recoverability and observability requirements; lead high-level sizing and validate through testing. Design high availability, failover, disaster recovery and backup strategies with agreed RTO/RPO targets and documented operational responsibilities. Work with infrastructure/DevOps teams on IaC, release architecture, configuration management, monitoring, logging, tracing and production readiness; do not assume ownership of routine operations. D. Security, privacy and compliance by design Incorporate identity federation, IAM/RBAC, least privilege, network segmentation, encryption and secrets management into architecture decisions. Coordinate threat modeling, security architecture review, privacy/data classification and risk treatments with cybersecurity stakeholders. Map relevant legal, contractual and sector-specific security obligations to system controls; apply frameworks such as ISO 27001 and others where appropriate, without assuming every listed regulation applies. E. Architecture governance and delivery assurance Chair or contribute to architecture review forums; maintain Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), exceptions, design-review findings and remediation actions. Review HLDs, integration specifications, deployment models, SDDs and major technology changes for interoperability, feasibility, security and operational readiness. Support solution estimations, technical proposals, vendor evaluations, procurement specifications, proofs of concept and acceptance of third-party solutions. Escalate architecture risks, incompatible product choices, technology duplication, unsupported assumptions and material deviations early; present decision options to management. F. Leadership and knowledge transfer Mentor software developers, engineers, technical leads and infrastructure specialists on system thinking, trade-offs and architecture documentation. Facilitate cross-functional design workshops, knowledge transfer and architecture handovers to delivery and operations teams. Advise leadership on emerging technologies such as AI/ML platforms, analytics, event-driven systems and cloud-native design where justified by business value. 4. Expected deliverables Architecture principles, standards and reusable reference architectures. As-is/to-be architecture diagrams and phased system modernization roadmaps. Project high-level design packages: context/container/deployment views, interfaces and trust boundaries. Architecture Decision Records, review checklists, technical risk/dependency registers and approved exceptions. Integration architecture, interface inventory and non-functional requirements with measurable acceptance criteria. Capacity and resilience plans (including HA/DR, backup, RTO/RPO) and production-readiness recommendations. Technology/vendor evaluation reports, proof-of-concept findings and technical inputs to procurement/proposals. Architecture reviews, design assurance reports and knowledge-transfer materials. 5. Required qualifications and experience Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems or related discipline; a relevant Master’s degree is an advantage. At least 10 years of progressive professional experience in software, systems or infrastructure engineering, including at least 3 years leading end-to-end systems/solution architecture for complex enterprise environments. Demonstrated experience designing, delivering or modernizing multi-system solutions involving applications, APIs, integration, data, infrastructure and cybersecurity controls. Proven capability to explain architecture decisions, evaluate alternatives, document trade-offs and guide cross-functional engineering teams. Practical experience in Linux/server platforms, networking fundamentals, cloud or on-premises infrastructure, containers/orchestration, distributed services and databases. Solid understanding of IAM, security-by-design, availability, recovery, monitoring, performance testing and reliability engineering. Experience preparing clear architecture diagrams (e.g. deployment/network/data-flow diagrams) and structured architecture documentation. 6. Technical competencies Architecture frameworks and modeling. Integration: REST APIs, API gateways, asynchronous messaging, Kafka/RabbitMQ or equivalents, event-driven and service-oriented patterns. Platforms: Docker, Kubernetes or equivalent orchestration; virtual machines, load balancers, storage and network design. Data: relational and NoSQL systems (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB), caching, replication, backup and data integration. Automation/operations: CI/CD, IaC (e.g., Terraform, Ansible), logging, metrics, tracing, incident and change management concepts. Security: IAM/SSO, OAuth 2.0/OIDC, TLS, mTLS, HSMs, Keys management systems (KMS), PKI, digital certificates, zero trust architecture, encryption algorithms/standards, secrets management, network zoning, threat modeling and risk assessment. 7. Desirable qualifications Experience with public-sector or regulated enterprise information systems and complex stakeholder/vendor environments. Certification such as cloud solutions architecture, Kubernetes, ITIL or information security (beneficial but not a substitute for demonstrated experience). Experience with high-scale distributed systems, platform migrations and multi-site disaster recovery. Strong expertise in designing highly secure systems, including cryptographic algorithms and encryption standards (AES, RSA, ECC), data encryption at rest and in transit, secure communication protocols (TLS/ mTLS), Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), digital certificates, key management systems (KMS/HSM), Identity and Access Management (IAM), OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, Zero Trust Architecture, secrets management. 8. Core behavioral competencies Systems thinking; strategic judgment; practical problem solving; strong technical writing and communication; constructive challenge; collaboration; stakeholder facilitation; mentoring; ownership of decisions and risk transparency. N.B: Only shortlisted will be contacted. Apply

raw_text: ITORERO ANGLICAN RY’URWANDA DIOCESE YA KIBUNGO AKARERE : Kirehe UMURENGE: GATORE UMUSHINGA RW0631EAR GATORE PHONES :0788552884/0788967578/0783297188 Email: rw631eargatore@gmail.com ITANGAZO RY’ AKAZI Ubuyobozi bw’Itorero Anglican ry’u Rwanda Paruwasi ya Gatore, riherereye mu mudugudu wa Gashanga, Akagari ka Nyamiryango,Umurenge wa Gatore mu Karere ka Kirehe, intara y’ i Burasirazuba riterwa inkunga na Compassion international mu Rwanda binyuze mu mushinga RW0631 EAR Gatore, ririfuza gutanga akazi ku mwanya wa: Umukozi ushinzwe ubuzima bw’abana n’ iterambere ry’umuryango (HCDSW) I. IBISABWA KURI UWO MUKOZI MURI RUSANGE NI: Upiganira akazi kuri uyu mwanya agomba kuba yujuje ibi bikurikira: Kuba ari umunyarwanda Kuba afite impamyabumenyi y’icyiciro cya kabiri (Bachelor’s degree) mu mashami akurikira: Ubuforumo (Advanced diploma); Ubuzima rusange (Public Health); Ububyaza (Mid-wives); Ubuvuzi (Clinical Medecine); Ubuzima bwo mumutwe (Mental Health) n’andi masomo ajyanye n’Ubumenyi mu mibereho y’abantu n’Iterambere Rusange (Social works and Development Studies) Kuba afite equivalence igihe yize hanze, Kuba azi neza kwandika no kuvuga ikinyarwanda n’icyongereza azi n’igifaransa ni akarushyo. Kuba ari mu kigero cy’imyaka 21-40 (21-40 years). Kuba azi gukoresha mudasobwa (Computer). Kuba afite icyemezo cyo kuba atarigeze akatirwa n’ inkiko igifungo kirengeje amezi atandatu. Kuba afite ibyemezo by’ abantu 3 bamuzi bamutangira ubuhamya ariko badafitanye isano, Kuba adafite andi masezerano y’akazi. Kuba atuye cyangwa yemera kuba hafi y’akazi mugihe yamaze gutsindira uwo mwanya. Kuba yiteguye guhita atangira akazi mu gihe yatsinze ikizamini. Kuba afite ibihamya by’ uko akunda abana byaba ari akarushyo. II. DOSIYE Y’USABA AKAZI IGOMBA KUBA IGIZWE N’IBI BIKURIKIRA : - Ibaruwa isaba akazi yandikiwe umuyobozi w’itorero rya EAR Paruwasi Gatore. - Inyandiko y’umwirondoro w’ usaba akazi ( C.V). - Fotocopi y’ indangamuntu . - Fotokopi y’impamyabumenyi iriho umukono wa Noteri. - Icyemezo kigaragazako washyingiwe mu gihe usaba akazi yubatse. - Icyemezo kigaragazako ari ingaragu mu gihe usaba akazi atubatse. Ku bazaba bujuje ibisabwa ikizamini cy’ijonjora kizakorwa kuwa 22 /10/2026 bikazakorerwa ku biro by’itorero rya EAR Gatore. title: Product Operations Lead (Fixed-Term)
raw_text: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. About the Role You will own the way the Product team works, including discovering and driving efficiencies through AI adoption, administering the product toolkit, process design and adoption, and use of data. If our ways of working aren't maximizing Product value add, it is up to you to fix it. Responsibilities Tooling & Infrastructure Administration (40%) Stack Ownership: Act as the primary administrator for the Product Department’s software stack (e.g., Dragonboat, Figma, Matomo, Notion). Manage configurations, user permissions, licenses, and vendor relationships. AI Adoption: Drive smart adoption of AI tools/agents to improve Product’s confidence in the value add of new features and to automate workflows. Workflow Configuration: Build and maintain standardized approaches to roadmaps, workflows, and automations to ensure all Domain teams (Field, HQ, CorpTech) operate with consistent visibility. Troubleshooting: Serve as the first line of support for PMs facing technical blockers with internal tools. Data Governance & SROI Tracking (30%) Troubleshooting: Serve as the first line of support for PMs facing technical blockers with internal tools. Impact measurement: Work with PMs to refine their product metrics to ensure they’re strategically aligned, automated, and accurate. Data Integrity: Audit analytics tools (e.g., Matomo) to ensure new features are launched with correct event tracking. Flag data quality issues to Engineering. Reporting: Own comprehensive reporting, surfacing critical insights on Product impact (e.g., BVMs) and processes (e.g., Roadmap Hygiene) to track progress against targets. Process Enablement & Logistics (30%) KPI Tracking: Assist the Dir. of Product with capturing and sharing Product team KPIs, working with Product Managers to ensure accuracy and help drive overall team performance towards targets Onboarding: Lead the technical onboarding for new Product hires, ensuring they are trained on our specific templates, tool stack, and "Way of Working." Knowledge Management: Maintain the department's internal documentation library (Wiki/Drive) to ensure the "Standard" defined by the Principal is accessible and up-to-date. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have: Soft Skills Service Mindset: Finds satisfaction in "unblocking" others and building the stage for other PMs to shine. Hyper-Organized: Loves checklists, documentation, and bringing order to chaos. Influence without Authority: Can drive adoption and compliance with Senior PMs without being their direct manager. Hard Skills Tool Administration: Advanced proficiency in configuring PDLC tools (Dragonboat) and documentation platforms (Notion/Confluence). Data Fluency: Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills (Pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, cross-sheet formulas) for SROI modeling. Familiarity with web analytics (Matomo/GA). Knowledge Product Lifecycle: Understanding of how software is built (Agile/Scrum basics) to effectively support the PM workflow. Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Nairobi, Kenya or Kigali, Rwanda Benefits Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits Contract Duration 2 Years Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya, Rwanda, Burundi, Malawi, Zambia, Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, Uganda Ethiopia and Nigeria. Application Deadline 03 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Apply

Based in Rugazi agglomeration, Ruyenzi Cell, Runda Sector, Kamonyi District, Southern Province. As the organization grows, we are committed to become a strong, financially sustainable, membership-based organization. To strengthen our long-term sustainability, we seek a Fundraising Officer to establish and lead our fundraising function. The position is responsible for developing and implementing the organization's first fundraising and resource mobilization strategy, diversifying funding sources, strengthening public visibility, and building long-term partnerships that contribute to a financially independent and sustainable organization. Build and maintain relationships with donors, partners, and sponsors. Coordinate donor reporting with program and finance teams. Maintain a donor database and fundraising pipeline. Creativity in developing fundraising campaigns. Knowledge of digital fundraising and marketing is an advantage. High integrity, initiative, and results orientation.
