title: Head Chef
experience_raw: Mid career (3 to 5 years of experience)
raw_text: Akagera Management Company HEAD CHEF – AP MOBILE CAMP VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT Akagera Management Company Ltd (AMC) was created through a partnership between African Parks and Rwanda Development Board (RDB) to manage Akagera National Park. African Parks will host the AP Mobile Camp at Akagera National Park to support various African Parks programmes and events including Leadership Workshops, the African Parks General Management Meeting, and other conservation-related workshops and trainings. Therefore, Akagera Management Company Ltd (AMC) is seeking dynamic, motivated, reliable, and experienced candidate to fill the Head Chef Position to support the AP Mobile Camp operations on a Full-time contract. Job Title Head Chef Reporting To Mobile Camp Manager/AP-X F&B Manager Location AP Mobile Camp, Akagera National Park, Rwanda Employment Type Full-Time Residential Posi Position Summary The Head Chef is responsible for the overall management and operation of the camp kitchen, ensuring the consistent delivery of high-quality, safe, and nutritious meals for guests, staff, and special events. The role requires strong culinary skills, leadership ability, cost control, menu planning expertise, and the ability to work in a remote wilderness environment with limited resources. The Head Chef will lead the kitchen team, maintain food safety standards, manage stock and purchasing requirements, and ensure an exceptional dining experience that reflects the standards of the Mobile Camp operation. Key Responsibilities Culinary Operations Plan and prepare high-quality meals for guests, staff, and special functions. Develop varied and balanced menus suitable for international visitors and diverse dietary requirements. Maintain consistently high standards of food presentation and quality. Ensure meals are prepared and served according to scheduled meal times. Accommodate dietary restrictions, allergies, and special guest requests. Monitor portion control and food wastage. Kitchen Management Supervise and coordinate all kitchen staff. Train and mentor cooks, assistants, and kitchen stewards. Develop staff duty rosters in coordination with camp operations. Maintain discipline, teamwork, and professional conduct within the kitchen. Ensure proper handover procedures between shifts. Food Safety and Hygiene Ensure compliance with all food safety, hygiene, and sanitation standards. Maintain clean and organized kitchen, storage, and food preparation areas. Monitor food temperatures and safe storage practices. Ensure correct handling of perishable goods. Conduct regular cleaning inspections of kitchen facilities and equipment. Stock Control and Procurement Manage food inventory and stock levels. Prepare accurate food orders and forecast requirements. Conduct regular stock counts and inventory reconciliations. Minimize spoilage, losses, and wastage. Monitor food costs and report significant variances. Budget Control Operate within approved food cost budgets. Identify opportunities for cost savings without compromising quality. Maintain records of kitchen expenditure and stock consumption. Equipment and Maintenance Ensure kitchen equipment is used correctly and maintained in good working order. Report equipment faults promptly. Monitor fuel, gas, refrigeration, and generator-dependent kitchen systems. Guest Experience Maintain a positive and professional presence around guests. Engage with guests where appropriate regarding menu preferences and dietary needs. Ensure meals contribute positively to the overall guest experience. Assist with special events, bush dinners, braais, and VIP functions when required. Minimum Requirements Education Formal culinary qualification or recognized chef certification preferred. Experience Minimum 5 years' experience in professional food service operations. Minimum 2 years in a senior chef or kitchen management role. Experience in remote camps, lodges, safari camps, field operations, or hospitality environments is highly advantageous. Skills and Competencies Strong leadership and supervisory skills. Excellent culinary and menu-planning abilities. Strong food safety and hygiene knowledge. Inventory and cost-control experience. Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines. Good organizational and communication skills. Ability to adapt to changing guest numbers and operational requirements. Physically fit and capable of working in a remote camp environment. Good level of spoken and written English French language skills are a plus. Use and knowledge of local ingredients and preparations. Working Conditions The Head Chef position is based in a remote mobile camp located within Akagera National Park. The successful candidate must be willing and able to work under the following conditions: Accommodation is provided in a canvas safari tent. Ablution facilities are shared with camp staff. The camp is located in an unfenced wilderness area with free-roaming wildlife. Staff must comply with all camp safety and wildlife protocols. Daily interaction with environmental conditions such as dust, heat, rain, insects, and wildlife should be expected. Electricity and communications may be limited or dependent on generators and solar systems. Working hours are operationally driven and may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and public holidays. Days off are scheduled according to guest occupancy levels, camp operational requirements, and activity schedules, rather than traditional fixed weekly off-days. Extended periods in camp may be required during peak operational periods. Staff are expected to maintain professional conduct and contribute positively to camp life while living and working in close proximity to colleagues. Performance Indicators The Head Chef will be evaluated against: Guest satisfaction with food quality and presentation. Food safety and hygiene compliance. Kitchen cleanliness and organization. Food cost management. Stock accuracy and inventory control. Staff development and kitchen team performance. Ability to deliver meals efficiently during varying occupancy levels. Compliance with operational and safety procedures. HOW TO APPLY Interested candidate should submit their application no later than 20th October 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application. Interested candidates should also submit the following documents in a single PDF file: Application letter addressed to the AP Mobile Camp Manager specifying the position applied for Updated Curriculum Vitae (CV) including three (3) professional references with their contact details Academic certificates and certificates of competence Copy of ID Criminal record Medical certificate Any additional supporting documents Ps: The recruited candidate will start with immediate effect All documents should be submitted in scanned soft copies in PDF format (preferably as one document) and named after your name and position applied for. Example: Name – Head Chef – AP Mobile Camp 2026 Please note that only candidates with the needed qualifications and relevant experience will be shortlisted. If you do not hear from us within one week after the submission deadline, know that you have not been shortlisted. Note: Due to the remote and demanding nature of a mobile safari camp operation, flexibility, resilience, self-motivation, and a positive attitude are considered essential requirements for this position. Apply

title: Executive Director
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToR) FOR THE RECRUITMENT OF THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR Position: Executive DirectorDuty Station: Kigali, Rwanda, Reports to: Chairperson of the Board of DirectorsSupervisory Authority: Board of Directors 1. BACKGROUND AND JUSTIFICATION Association Rwandaise des Conseillers en Traumatisme (ARCT-RUHUKA) is a national non-governmental organisation of professional trauma counsellors established in 1998. The organization evolved from a trauma counselling programme implemented with the support of Trócaire, an Irish charity organisation, in response to the need for trauma counselling and psychosocial support in Rwanda. ARCT-RUHUKA was subsequently formally established and obtained legal recognition as a non-governmental organisation under Ministerial Decree No. 97/11 of 28 July 2007. The organization was later legally registered with the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB) under Legal Personality No. 97/11 dated 12 September 2013. In accordance with the applicable legal and regulatory framework, ARCT-RUHUKA has continued to maintain its legal compliance and institutional standing. Its most recent certificate, issued by the Rwanda Governance Board on 30 September 2026, certifies that Association Rwandaise des Conseillers en Traumatisme (ARCT-RUHUKA), a national non-governmental organization with Legal Personality No. 97/11 of 12 September 2013, complies with Law No. 058/2024 of 20 June 2024 and the related regulations. Over the years, ARCT-RUHUKA has evolved into an established national organisation dedicated to trauma counselling, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), professional capacity development, advocacy, institutional strengthening, and child rights and protection. Through its qualified and committed staff, the organisation works across various sectors and communities in Rwanda, providing technical expertise, professional support, and integrated services that promote mental well-being, strengthen resilience, protect vulnerable populations, and improve the overall well-being of individuals, families, and communities To strengthen its governance, operational efficiency, institutional sustainability, and impact on target populations, ARCT-RUHUKA seeks to recruit a qualified and experienced Executive Director with strong leadership, strategic management, program coordination, resource mobilization, and organizational development skills. The Executive Director will be responsible for the overall day-to-day management of the organization, implementation of decisions made by statutory organs, coordination of staff and programs, development of strategic partnerships, and achievement of institutional objectives in accordance with the organization's mission, vision, statutes, policies, and procedures. 2. OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION Under the direct supervision of the Chairperson of the Board of Directors and in accordance with the guidance and decisions of the General Assembly and the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will provide strategic leadership and operational management of ARCT-RUHUKA. The Executive Director will ensure effective governance, institutional performance, program quality, resource mobilization, sound human and financial resource management, and the long-term sustainability of the organization. 3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES 3.1. Strategic Leadership and Institutional Governance The Executive Director shall: Provide overall leadership and management to ensure that ARCT-RUHUKA remains an efficient, effective, transparent, and accountable institution; Translate the strategic directions and decisions of the General Assembly and Board of Directors into operational plans and actionable activities; Coordinate the development, review, and implementation of the organization's strategic plan and operational plans, involving all relevant departments and institutional organs; Submit strategic plans, operational plans, budgets, and institutional reports to the Board of Directors for review and approval; Ensure compliance with the organization's statutes, internal regulations, administrative and financial procedures manual, and other institutional policies; Ensure the effective functioning of the organizational structure and propose improvements to strengthen institutional efficiency; Coordinate the preparation of Board of Directors and General Assembly meetings in collaboration with the Chairperson, including agendas, supporting documents, and reports; Ensure timely implementation and follow-up of resolutions, directives, and recommendations from the organization's statutory organs; Propose amendments and improvements to institutional policies, procedures, internal regulations, and other governance documents whenever necessary; Advise the Board of Directors on strategic priorities, institutional risks, development opportunities, and organizational sustainability. 3.2. Administrative and Operational Management The Executive Director shall: Plan, organize, coordinate, supervise, and monitor the day-to-day operations of the Executive Secretariat; Ensure the effective implementation of administrative procedures and internal control systems; Define staff responsibilities and duties in accordance with the approved organizational structure and guidance from the Board of Directors; Ensure effective coordination between departments, decentralized offices, project teams, and operational units; Ensure the availability and efficient utilization of human, material, logistical, and other resources required for the organization's operations; Oversee the management, maintenance, and proper utilization of the organization's assets, infrastructure, equipment, and other property; Strengthen administrative systems, management tools, and internal communication mechanisms; Maintain effective administrative relations with relevant public, private institutions, regulatory authorities, and partners. Identify operational challenges and implement appropriate corrective measures; Ensure business continuity and take immediate action in emergencies within delegated authority, in collaboration with the Board of Directors. 3.3. Program and Project Management The Executive Director shall: Provide overall coordination and supervision of all programs and projects in line with the organization's mission, strategic plan, and contractual obligations; Oversee the development of project proposals, work plans, results frameworks, and budgets in collaboration with program managers and relevant departments; Ensure the technical quality, relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, and sustainability of the organization's interventions; Ensure that programs respond to the needs of beneficiaries and uphold the principles of dignity, confidentiality, safeguarding, and non-discrimination; Coordinate the implementation of training, trauma counselling, clinical supervision, psychosocial support, awareness-raising, and advocacy activities; Ensure that project activities are implemented according to approved timelines, budgets, performance indicators, and expected results; Promote complementarity and synergies among the organization's programs and projects; Organize regular coordination and performance review meetings with staff. Ensure that recommendations from evaluations, audits, monitoring visits, and partner reviews are addressed and implemented; Promote innovation, institutional learning, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement in program quality. 3.4. Financial Management, Budgeting, and Internal Controls In collaboration with the Director of Finance and Administration (DAF), the Executive Director shall: Coordinate the preparation of the organization's consolidated budget and submit it to the Board of Directors for approval; Ensure budget implementation in accordance with approved allocations, donor agreements, and the organization's administrative and financial procedures manual; Regularly monitor budget execution and implement corrective measures to address significant variances; Review and approve financial reports prepared by the Finance and Administration Department before submission to the Board of Directors or partners; Ensure the establishment, maintenance, and effective implementation of internal control systems, risk management mechanisms, and fraud prevention measures; Authorize expenditures, financial commitments, and staff mission orders within the limits of delegated authority; Ensure that financial reports are accurate, reliable, timely, and compliant with statutory, accounting, and donor requirements; Ensure compliance with applicable tax, social security, accounting, and financial regulations; Oversee the preparation and implementation of internal and external audits and ensure timely follow-up of audit recommendations; Promote transparency, accountability, and the efficient utilization of financial and material resources; Ensure compliance with donor-specific financial procedures, grant conditions, and contractual obligations; Support the development of resource diversification and long-term financial sustainability strategies. The Executive Director shall exercise financial authority in accordance with the principles of segregation of duties, dual control, and the organization's approved delegation of authority framework. 3.5. Human Resource Management and Staff Development The Executive Director shall: Implement the organization's human resource management policies in accordance with its statutes, staff regulations, and procedures manual; Identify and plan staffing needs in line with strategic priorities, program requirements, and available resources; Recruit, assign, and supervise permanent and temporary support staff within the limits of delegated authority; Submit proposals for the recruitment of senior management staff and staff termination decisions to the Board of Directors where such decisions fall within its authority; Establish staff performance objectives and conduct regular, transparent, and objective performance appraisals; Promote a professional, inclusive, respectful, and harassment-free working environment; Identify staff capacity-building needs and develop appropriate training and professional development plans; Promote staff motivation, teamwork, accountability, and professional growth; Ensure compliance with applicable labor laws, staff protection policies, and internal procedures; Address workplace conflicts and propose appropriate solutions; Promote succession planning, leadership development, and knowledge transfer within the organization. 3.6. Resource Mobilization, Partnerships, and Institutional Development The Executive Director shall: Develop and submit a resource mobilization and partnership development strategy to the Board of Directors for approval; Identify funding opportunities from bilateral and multilateral donors, United Nations agencies, international NGOs, foundations, and private sector partners; Coordinate the development and submission of project proposals, concept notes, funding applications, and partnership initiatives; Establish, maintain, and strengthen relationships with technical and financial partners, public institutions, civil society organizations, and professional networks; Represent the organization in coordination meetings, forums, platforms, and partnership engagements as delegated; Negotiate partnership opportunities in accordance with the organization's strategic priorities and authorized signing powers; Develop income-generating and self-financing initiatives that are consistent with the organization's mission and statutes; Enhance the visibility, credibility, and institutional positioning of ARCT-RUHUKA; Ensure compliance with funding agreements, contractual commitments, and accountability requirements; Diversify funding sources to reduce dependence on a limited number of donors and strengthen institutional sustainability. 3.7. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning The Executive Director shall: Establish and maintain an integrated system for institutional planning, monitoring, evaluation, reporting, and performance management; Define institutional, programmatic, financial, and administrative performance indicators in collaboration with relevant managers; Supervise the preparation and timely submission of narrative, technical, financial, and institutional reports; Periodically assess progress against operational plans, budgets, and expected results; Organize performance review meetings and ensure follow-up on agreed recommendations; Promote the collection, analysis, and use of reliable data to support evidence-based decision-making; Ensure effective accountability mechanisms for beneficiaries, communities, governance organs, and development partners; Promote knowledge sharing, documentation of good practices, and institutional learning; Oversee the implementation of improvement plans arising from evaluations, audits, and performance reviews. 3.8. Legal Compliance, Ethics, and Risk Management The Executive Director shall: Ensure compliance with the organization's statutes, internal regulations, and applicable laws and regulations governing non-profit organizations in Rwanda; Ensure that the organization meets its legal, administrative, and regulatory obligations to relevant authorities; Coordinate the preparation, maintenance, and updating of legal, administrative, and institutional documents; Ensure the implementation of policies on fraud prevention, anti-corruption, safeguarding, and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse; Identify institutional, financial, operational, legal, and reputational risks and propose appropriate mitigation measures; 0Ensure the protection of personal data, confidentiality of information, and adherence to professional standards in trauma counselling; Coordinate the management of legal matters and disputes in collaboration with the Board of Directors and, where necessary, a legal advisor; Ensure that legal representation and judicial proceedings are conducted in accordance with statutory requirements and the authority delegated by the Board of Directors. 3.9. Institutional Communication and Representation The Executive Director shall: Ensure effective institutional communication within the organization and with external stakeholders; Represent ARCT-RUHUKA in civil, administrative, and partnership matters within the limits of the authority granted; Maintain professional relationships with government authorities, development partners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders; Oversee the preparation and dissemination of institutional reports, publications, and communication materials; Promote the organization's image, visibility, and reputation in line with its mission, vision, and ethical principles; Submit significant matters requiring strategic decisions or specific representation to the Board of Directors 4. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND PROFILE 4.1. Academic Qualifications The candidate shall: Hold at least a Master's degree or equivalent in Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Mental Health, Psychosocial Support, Social Work, Public Health, Administration, Management, Sociology, Community Development, Development Studies, Project Management, or another relevant field aligned with ARCT-RUHUKA's programmes and strategic objectives. Possess relevant professional experience in trauma counselling, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), child protection, community development, advocacy, institutional capacity building, or the management of non-governmental organisations. Demonstrate proven experience in strategic leadership, organisational management, programme planning, project implementation, resource mobilisation, and donor relations. Have a strong understanding of NGO governance, financial management, human resource management, partnership development, and institutional sustainability. 4.2. Professional Experience The candidate shall demonstrate: At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience in organizational, program, or project management; At least five (5) years of experience in a managerial, leadership, or supervisory position; Practical experience in program coordination, administrative and financial management, strategic planning, and human resource management; Experience managing projects funded by national or international development partners; Experience in the design, development, or implementation of trauma counselling, mental health, or psychosocial support programs shall be a significant advantage; Experience in resource mobilization, partnership development, and institutional management shall be an added advantage. Demonstrate experience working with Community on special attention to vulnerable people , including survivors of trauma, women, children, adolescents, and other at-risk groups. 4.3. Technical Competencies The candidate shall demonstrate: Strong knowledge of strategic and operational planning; Solid skills in program and project management, budgeting, and financial oversight; Good understanding of internal control systems, risk management, and compliance; Strong competencies in human resource management, leadership, and organizational development; Ability to develop funding proposals and negotiate partnerships; Good knowledge of monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning systems; Familiarity with donor requirements and grant management procedures; Knowledge of laws and regulations applicable to non-profit organizations in Rwanda; Proficiency in computer applications and administrative, financial, and reporting systems. 4.4. Language Requirements Excellent command of English and Kinyarwanda, both written and spoken; Good command of French, written and spoken; 4.5. Personal and Behavioral Competencies The candidate shall demonstrate: Strategic leadership and sound decision-making skills; Integrity, honesty, transparency, and high ethical standards; Excellent communication, negotiation, and representation skills; Teamwork and the ability to work in multicultural environments; Strong organizational skills, initiative, and the ability to manage competing priorities; Problem-solving and conflict management abilities; Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines; Sensitivity to mental health, safeguarding, confidentiality, and human dignity; Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of ARCT-RUHUKA. 4.6. Other Requirements Rwandan nationality, if required by the organization's statutes and applicable regulations; Maximum age 45 years, subject to confirmation of compliance with the organization's statutes and applicable laws; Availability for domestic and occasional international travel; A valid Category B driving license shall be an advantage or a requirement if confirmed by the organization's internal regulations. 5. APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS. Interested candidates shall submit an application dossier comprising: A motivation letter addressed to the Chairperson of the Board of Directors of ARCT-RUHUKA; An updated and detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV); Copies of academic qualifications and relevant training certificates; Employment certificates or other evidence of relevant professional experience; Contact details of three professional referees; A copy of a valid national identity card; Criminal records. Any other relevant supporting documents demonstrating the candidate's qualifications and experience. The application submission procedure, receiving address, and deadline shall be communicated in the official vacancy announcement. The recruitment process shall uphold the principles of transparency, fairness, confidentiality, equal opportunity, merit, and prevention of conflicts of interest. 6. Submission Details Interested and eligible candidates are invited to submit their application documents to the email: arct.recruitment@gmail.com The submission deadline is 22nd October 2026. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. ONLY shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information or clarification, interested candidates may contact ARCT-RUHUKA during official working hours at +250 796 894 484. Done at Kigali, on 04th October 2026. Annonciata KALIGIRWA Chairperson of the Board of Directors Attachment attachment_file_5f44b321265b6c328ce9 Apply

title: GIS Systems Developer
raw_text: We are hiring for GIS Systems Developer! Inviting interested candidates to apply by reading the job description below and sending applications to https://career.qtsoftwareltd.com starting October 15th, 2026. JOB ADVERTISEMENT Duty Station: Kigali – Rwanda Deadline for applicants: 15th November 2026 Contract type: Fixed Term Renewable Submit CV, Cover letter, National ID and copy of Academic Degree to: https://career.qtsoftwareltd.com About the Company QT Global Software Ltd is a private company, engaged in web and mobile application development, information security consultancy, and network security services, providing secure solutions to esteemed clients. We collaborate with government agencies, companies, and organizations to create outstanding user experiences, secure solutions, and support and maintenance across the product/solution lifecycle. At QT Global Software Ltd, we continuously transform our operations to ensure that we provide reliable and cost-effective client-oriented IT services. We achieve this by assembling the best resources in software development, IT infrastructure, and security, as well as the best project leads. We are proud of our past accomplishments and excited about our future prospects. Our management philosophy and objectives revolve around two key principles: Firstly, we strive to become the preferred employer for the brightest and most talented minds in the region. Secondly, we prioritize the development, recognition, and rewarding of performance that we deem crucial to our long-term success and sustainability. Company Values All staff at QT Global Software Ltd are connected to a shared set of organizational values: Quality Customer Service Professional Business Conduct Client-Oriented and Secure Solutions 1. Position Summary The GIS Systems Developer shall design at the application/component level, develop, configure, integrate, test, deploy, document, and maintain GIS-enabled software solutions. The role is primarily hands-on and combines GIS technology proficiency with full-stack software development to implement web and, where required, mobile GIS applications; geospatial data workflows; GIS services; and integrations with enterprise information systems. The developer shall work with project technical leads, software architects, business analysts, GIS specialists, DevOps engineers, and other project team members to translate approved business and technical requirements into reliable, secure, maintainable software. Responsibility for enterprise-wide architecture, overall technology strategy, and solution-level governance remains with the designated architect or technical lead. 2. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Geoinformatics, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, ICT, Geography, or a related discipline. At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience, including substantial hands-on development or customization of GIS-based software applications. Demonstrated implementation contribution to at least two (2) GIS software development or enterprise GIS integration projects. Evidence of completed software deliverables such as GIS web applications, APIs, geospatial database components, or GIS integrations. Relevant ArcGIS, software development, cloud, or database certifications are an added advantage, not mandatory. 3. Required Technical Experience 3.1 GIS Platforms and Development Practical experience configuring, extending, and consuming services from ArcGIS Enterprise (including ArcGIS Server and Portal for ArcGIS) and/or ArcGIS Online. Hands-on development of interactive web maps, geospatial user interfaces, feature editing, layer visualization, pop-ups, search, filtering, and spatial queries using ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript (formerly ArcGIS API for JavaScript). Experience with ArcGIS REST APIs, feature services, map services, geoprocessing services, authentication, and service consumption or publishing. Ability to use ArcGIS Pro for preparing and validating geospatial datasets, maps, layers, and services, as required. Experience implementing location-based workflows, spatial analysis, GIS dashboards, and geospatial reporting. 3.2 Frontend and Mobile Development Proficiency in JavaScript or TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, and modern frontend development. Hands-on experience with React and/or Next.js, including API integration, state management, reusable components, responsive layouts, and form validation. Experience integrating GIS mapping components into enterprise web applications. Experience with mobile GIS applications, responsive field-data-collection workflows, or mobile frameworks is an added advantage. 3.3 Backend Development and Integrations Ability to implement backend services using at least one relevant stack, such as Node.js/NestJS, Java/Spring Boot, or ASP.NET. Experience developing and consuming REST APIs, handling JSON data, authentication/authorization, validation, error handling, and API documentation. Experience integrating GIS with enterprise applications such as land information systems, ERP, health information systems, environmental systems, document management systems, and external data services. Understanding of asynchronous processing, data import/export, and integration error recovery; SOAP integration experience is an added advantage where legacy systems require it. 3.4 Spatial Databases and Data Processing Strong SQL skills and practical experience with geospatial data storage and querying, preferably PostgreSQL/PostGIS and/or enterprise geodatabases backed by supported relational databases. Ability to create, query, update, validate, and optimize spatial datasets and relevant indexes in collaboration with database/GIS administrators. Experience with coordinate reference systems, projections, common GIS data formats, spatial joins, and geometry operations. Ability to implement data import, transformation, cleansing, validation, and synchronization routines. 3.5 Engineering Practices, Security, and Delivery Use of Git and collaborative development workflows, including code review and version control. Ability to write automated/unit/integration tests, troubleshoot defects, profile slow services or spatial queries, and improve application performance. Understanding of secure coding practices, secrets handling, access control, and integration with organizational identity services. Practical experience supporting CI/CD pipelines, environment configuration, logging, release packaging, and deployments in collaboration with DevOps or infrastructure teams. Ability to prepare developer-facing technical documentation, installation notes, API documentation, and handover materials. 4. Key Responsibilities Develop, enhance, and maintain web-based GIS applications, geospatial modules, and related software components based on approved requirements and technical designs. Build interactive maps, data-editing tools, spatial search/filtering, GIS dashboards, and other geospatial user-interface components. Configure, extend, publish (where authorized), and consume GIS map, feature, and geoprocessing services on ArcGIS Enterprise or ArcGIS Online. Design and implement application-level APIs, backend logic, and integration adapters connecting GIS services with other business systems. Implement and maintain spatial data models, geospatial queries, ETL/data import routines, and data validation processes under agreed data standards. Write maintainable, secure, reusable code; perform unit and integration testing; participate in peer reviews and resolve identified defects. Investigate and fix functional, integration, geospatial-data, and performance issues; assist with monitoring and production support. Work with technical leads, architects, business analysts, QA, database administrators, and DevOps staff to clarify requirements and deliver features within project plans. Support deployment, configuration, release validation, and maintenance of GIS applications across development, test, and production environments. Maintain source code, API specifications, technical setup guides, configuration records, release notes, and relevant implementation documentation. Participate in sprint planning, technical discussions, demonstrations, code reviews, and project progress reporting. Provide technical knowledge transfer to internal development and support teams; support user training only where hands-on technical input is required. 5. Preferred Experience GIS implementations in government, land administration, utilities, environment, or natural-resource management. Parcel Fabric and cadastral/land information workflows within the ArcGIS Enterprise ecosystem. Field data collection, offline/mobile workflows, GPS-based data capture, and synchronization. ArcGIS Experience Builder, ArcGIS Dashboards, or configurable GIS applications, including custom widgets where applicable. Python/ArcPy or other scripting for GIS data processing and workflow automation. Open geospatial technologies and standards, including OGC services, GeoJSON, and PostGIS. Real-time GIS data feeds, event-driven integrations, remote-sensing datasets, or advanced spatial analytics. 6. Soft Skills Strong analytical thinking, debugging, and practical problem-solving. Ability to translate technical specifications and requirements into working software. Clear communication with technical and non-technical colleagues. Teamwork, code-review participation, and willingness to receive and apply technical feedback. Good time management, attention to detail, and accountability for assigned deliverables. Ability to work independently on assigned development tasks and within multidisciplinary project teams. 7. Expected Deliverables Functional GIS web application features, modules, and, where assigned, mobile GIS components. Version-controlled, reviewed, and maintainable source code with relevant build and deployment configuration. Implemented GIS service configurations, maps, layers, and application integrations. Documented REST APIs, integration services, and backend components. Geospatial database scripts, data-processing routines, and validated datasets as applicable. Unit/integration test artifacts, defect resolutions, and evidence of release verification. Technical documentation, installation/configuration instructions, API references, release notes, and handover records. Knowledge transfer and technical support notes for maintenance teams. 8. Performance and Acceptance Criteria Assignments and deliverables shall be reviewed against the approved project scope, specifications, and applicable organizational development standards. Acceptance considerations include: Functional requirements implemented and demonstrated to the project team. Code reviewed, version controlled, and accompanied by appropriate tests and documentation. GIS services, integrations, data processing, and access permissions function as specified. Material defects and security findings addressed before acceptance according to agreed severity thresholds. Deployable artifacts and technical handover materials provided for supported environments. N.B: Only shortlisted will be contacted. Apply

raw_text: ITANGAZO RY'AKAZI Trinity Musha Mines Ltd ni ikigo cy'ubucukuzi gishinzwe gutunganya no gushakisha Tin, Tantalum na Lithium mu Rwanda. Trinity Musha irimo gutumira abakandida bujuje ibisabwa gusaba akazi ku myanya ikurikira: A. Imyanya y’ akazi: # Umwanya (Saba umwe muri iyi myanya ikurikira) 1 Underground Dump Truck Operator 2 Continuous Miner Operator 3 LHD/ Scoop Tram Operator B. Ishami: Ubucukuzi (Mining) C. Atanga raporo kuri: Umugenzuzi w'Ubucukuzi (Mine Supervisor) D. Aho akorera: Trinity Musha Mine / Agace cyangwa ahantu hemewe ho gukorera munsi y'ubutaka E. Intego y'akazi: Gukoresha mu mutekano, neza kandi hakurikijwe amategeko imashini yemewe mu gukata, gukusanya no gusuka amabuye y'agaciro, mu gihe hubahirizwa ingamba z'umutekano zijyanye no guhumeka, kurwanya ivumbi, gukurikirana imyuka, gufata ubutaka, kubuza abantu kwegera imashini, gutandukanya amashanyarazi (isolation) n'aho imashini zihurira n'ubwikorezi. 1. Inshingano: Kwitabira ikiganiro cyo mbere y'akazi (pre-shift briefing) no kwemeza uburyo bwemewe bwo gukata, intera ntarengwa yo kwinjira, uburyo bwo gushyigikira ubutaka, uburyo bwo guhumeka, gahunda yo kurwanya ivumbi, uburyo bwo gutwara amabuye, ibimenyetso by'itumanaho, agace kabuzanyijwe n'inzira yo guhunga. Gukora gusa igihe washyizweho, ufite ubuzima bwiza, wahawe amahugurwa, wasuzumwe mu bikorwa kandi wemerewe gukoresha imashini yihariye (ubwoko n'icyitegererezo), sisitemu ya remote-control n'agace uhabwa gukoreramo munsi y'ubutaka. Kutinjira cyangwa gukata mbere y'uko umugenzuzi w'inzobere atangaza ko aho bakorera hatekanye; kugenzura igisenge, inkuta, aho bacukura, hasi, ibishyigikira ubutaka, amazi, guhumeka, ibikoresho by'ingoboka, kugaragara, ingano y'imyuka n'aho amabuye atwarirwa. Kuzuza no gushyira umukono ku rutonde rw'igenzura mbere yo gutangira rukubiyemo: igice gikata n'ibyuma bikata, boom, umutwe ukusanya, ibipakira, convoyeur (conveyor), umutwe wo gusuka (tailpiece), iminyururu, imiyoboro, insinga, ibirinda, scrubber, ibitera amazi, igikoresho gipima imyuka, impuruza, amatara, ibyuma bihagarika byihutirwa, ibizimya umuriro aho bikenewe, igikoresho kimenya abantu begereye na remote-control. Kudakoresha imashini ifite inenge ikomeye ku mutekano; kuyihagarika, kuyitandukanya n'amashanyarazi, kuyifunga (lock out), kuyishyiraho ikarita y'icyitonderwa (tag) no kuyibuza kugenda, gushyigikira ibice byazamuwe, gutanga raporo y'inenge no gutegereza uruhushya rwanditse rwo kuyikoresha nyuma yo gusanwa no kugeragezwa n'inzobere. Kugerageza no kurinda sisitemu ya remote-control, kwemeza ko imashini ihuye na yo, kugumana igenzura ry'icyuma cyohereza ibimenyetso (transmitter) no gukumira ko imashini yatangira gukora ku buryo butateganyijwe cyangwa butemewe. Gushyiraho no gukurikirana agace kabuzanyijwe ku mpande z'aho imashini ihindukirira, inzira z'iminyururu, ahashobora gufatirwa, imitwe ikata n'ikusanya, convoyeur na tailpiece; guhagarara ako kanya igihe umuntu yinjiye mu gace kabuzanyijwe. Gukorera ku ruhande rwagenewe umutekano ahari ubutaka bushyigikiwe, ureba neza imashini, aho bacukura n'aho amabuye atwarirwa; ntuzahagarare iruhande rw'imashini igenda cyangwa munsi y'igisenge kidashyigikiwe. Kwemeza ko umwuka ukenewe, imyenda ihumeka (curtains), imiyoboro, scrubber n'ibitera amazi biri mu mwanya ukwiye kandi bikora neza; gukora ibipimo by'imyuka bisabwa, ugahagarara, ukazimya imashini ukavamo igihe guhumeka kwanze cyangwa imyuka igeze ku rwego rusaba gufata ingamba. Kudakata hatariho umuvuduko w'amazi ukwiye, ibitera amazi, scrubber n'ibikusanya ivumbi; kugenzura umwuka usubira inyuma no kubuza abantu kwegera ivumbi n'umwuka usubira inyuma. Gutanga impuruza, kugenzura inzira no kugenda buhoro; kurinda insinga, ibigenzura guhumeka, ibishyigikira ubutaka n'abantu, kwita ku hasi habi no guhuza umutwe ukata n'umurongo wo gukata wemewe. Gukata (slumping na shearing) mu byiciro bigenzurwa, mu bujyakuzimu bwa sump, ishusho n'urwego byemewe, mu gihe ukurikirana umutwaro, ihindagurika, ivumbi, imyuka, ibishashi n'ihinduka ry'ubutaka. Gukoresha amaboko akusanya na convoyeur mu buryo bworoshye kugira ngo hatabaho kwifunga cyangwa kunyanyagiza amabuye; ntuzigere ugenzura, ushyiramo ikiganza cyangwa ukuraho ikibuza igihe imashini ifite amashanyarazi; banza wemeze ko nta mbaraga zisigaye mbere yo gukuraho ikibuza. Guhuza gusuka n'imodoka zitwara (shuttle cars), amakamyo cyangwa ubundi bwikorezi ukoresheje ibimenyetso byemewe; kugumana intera, kubuza umuntu kwinjira hagati y'imashini no guhagarara igihe kugaragara, itumanaho cyangwa guhuza bibuze. Kutarenza intera ntarengwa yemewe idashyigikiwe cyangwa ubujyakuzimu bwo gukata; igihe ugeze ku mupaka, uhagarare, umanure ukingire umutwe, uhave, utegereze ko hashyirwaho ibishyigikira kandi ko guhumeka kwiyongera mbere yo gutangira. Gukata ibice bigufi mu butaka bubi, ntuzigere ukora cyangwa unyure munsi y'igisenge kidashyigikiwe, kandi wemeze ko igisenge n'inkuta bitekanye mbere yo gukuramo imashini yapfuye cyangwa gusana. Gukurikirana insinga, moteri, hydraulics n'ubushyuhe buturuka ku guterana; guhagarara iyo hari umwotsi, umuriro, ibishashi, insinga yangiritse cyangwa ubushyuhe bukabije, ukazimya amashanyarazi ugakurikiza gahunda y'ubutabazi bw'ikirombe. Ibisabwa ku Kazi, Ubushobozi n'Imyitwarire: Kuba ufite uruhushya rwo gutwara ibinyabiziga rwa category B na F Uburambe bw' imyaka nibura itatu(3) muri uyu mwuga. Icyitonderwa: Usaba ku mwanya wa LHD/ Scoop Tram Operator, agomba kuba azi gukoresha Wheel loader Usaba ku mwanya wa Continuous Miner, agomba kuba azi gukoresha Excavator Kurangiza neza amahugurwa y'ikigo (induction) n'amahugurwa yemewe y'inyigisho n'ay'ibikorwa ya Machine Operator. Isuzuma ry'ubushobozi mu bikorwa no kwemererwa ku mugaragaro gukoresha ubwoko n'icyitegererezo cy'imashini, sisitemu ya remote-control n'agace ahabwa gukoreramo. Icyemezo cy'ubuzima gifite agaciro gikwiriye gukoresha ibikoresho bigendanwa munsi y'ubutaka n'imbaraga z'umubiri uyu murimo usaba. Kugaragaza ubumenyi ku buryo bwo gukata, gahunda zo guhumeka no gufata ubutaka, kurwanya ivumbi, gupima imyuka, gutandukanya no gufunga amashanyarazi, umutekano wa remote-control, uduce tubuzanyijwe, aho imashini zihurira n'ubwikorezi n'uburyo bwo gutabara. Ubushobozi bwo kumenya ibikoresho bifite inenge, ubutaka budashyigikiwe, guhumeka kwanze, imyuka irenze igipimo, ihindagurika ridasanzwe, ubushyuhe bukabije, ibyago by'amashanyarazi n'imikoranire idatekanye y'abantu cyangwa ubwikorezi. Ubushobozi bwo kugumana umwanya utekanye wo gukoreramo, kwita ku kazi igihe kirekire, kugumana remote-control no gutumanaho neza mu gihe cyose cyo gukata. Kuzuza neza inyandiko z'igenzura, umusaruro, imyuka, guhumeka, inenge, gusana n'ubushobozi. Kuza ku kazi neza, gukurikiza amabwiriza mu budahemuka no kwemera gukoresha ububasha bwo guhagarika akazi igihe cyose ikintu gikomeye cy'ingenzi cyabuze. Gukora gusa igihe washyizweho, ufite ubuzima bwiza, wahawe amahugurwa, wasuzumwe mu bikorwa kandi wemerewe gukoresha imashini yihariye (ubwoko n'icyitegererezo), sisitemu ya remote-control n'agace uhabwa gukoreramo munsi y'ubutaka. title: Logistics Officer
experience_raw: Mid career (3 to 5 years of experience)
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE (TOR) Hiring of Logistics Officer October 8th 2026 1. Background Ngali Holdings “The Company” is an investment company located at Kimihurura, Kigali, Rwanda. The organization seeks to recruit a competent and experienced Logistics Officer to lead and oversee Company’s logistics operation. 2. Position Title Logistics Officer 3.Reporting Line Job Details Department People and Culture Job Title Logistics Officer Supervisor HR & Admin Manager Job Purpose: To manage and coordinate the company’s logistics operations, including procurement, transportation, inventory management, and distribution of materials and equipment, ensuring timely, cost-effective, and compliant support for mining operations. Primary Responsibilities Coordinate procurement and delivery of materials, supplies, and equipment. Manage transportation of goods and materials to and from mining sites. Monitor inventory levels and maintain accurate stock records. Ensure timely distribution of materials and supplies to operational units. Liaise with suppliers, transporters, and service providers. Track deliveries and confirm receipt of goods. Ensure compliance with procurement and logistics policies. Prepare logistics and inventory reports for management. Organize storage of equipment and materials in warehouses or depots. Monitor and control logistics costs and optimize resource utilization. Support planning for operational needs and resource allocation. Maintain accurate records of issued and received items. Conduct regular stock counts and reconcile discrepancies. Ensure safe handling, storage, and transport of hazardous materials. Support emergency logistics needs for operations or field projects. Assist in supplier evaluation and selection processes. Coordinate with finance on invoices, payments, and procurement documentation. Maintain updated logistics policies, procedures, and SOPs. Support compliance audits and inspections related to logistics. Recommend improvements to logistics processes and operational efficiency. Use SAP Business One for inventory management, including receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments, reconciliation, and reporting Maintain and regularly update the Company Asset Register. Person specification Academic qualification Bachelor’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or related field. Professional qualification Certifications such as CIPS, CPSM, or equivalent are an advantage. Experience Minimum 3 years of experience in logistics, supply chain, or operational support. Key Performance Indicators Measures Ensure timely, cost-effective, and compliant management of logistics operations, including procurement, transportation, and inventory management. On-time delivery of materials, accurate inventory records, minimized logistics costs, Compliance with procurement policies, and successful support for operational activities without delays or shortages. Accurate inventory records and SAP Business One transactions. Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities: Strong logistics and supply chain management skills. Strong practical knowledge of SAP Business One inventory management. Warehouse, stores, and inventory control skills. Asset management and reconciliation skills. Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Strong judgment, integrity, accountability, and attention to detail. Ability to work under pressure and meet operational deadlines. 4. Application Requirements Interested candidates shall submit: Application letter Updated Curriculum Vitae (CV) Certified academic and professional certificates Copies of identification documents Contacts of at least three professional referees 5. Selection Method Selection shall be conducted through: Shortlisting of qualified candidates Written assessment SAP Business one practical test is mandatory (Candidate who do not attain required pass mark may not proceed to the next stage Interview Reference and background checks 6. Submission Deadline Date,23rd October,2026, Email: nh.recruitment@ngali.com Contact: 0785387870 Signed: Nadine Uwera HR &Admin Manager Attachment attachment_file_a68483b23b22d6660fd5 Apply

title: Tender Notice for Transportation of Rubis Petroleum Products (White Oils, LPG, and Lubricants)
raw_text: Date: 28th September 2026 Subject: Invitation to Tender: Transportation of Rubis Petroleum Products (White Oils, LPG, and Lubricants) Dear Prospective Transporter, Rubis is inviting qualified local transport companies to submit tenders for the transportation of our petroleum products. Please note that a mandatory minimum requirement for this tender is a fleet of at least two (2) trucks. Scope of Work The tender covers three specific categories of transport: White oil fuel distribution LPG distribution (Bulk and Cylinders) Lubricant distribution Summary of HSE & Technical Requirements As part of the onboarding and pre-qualification process, bidders must demonstrate adequate Health, Safety, Environment, and Quality (HSE) systems. The detailed requirements will be formally presented but the core minimum requirements include: General Compliance & Management: Valid operating licenses, comprehensive HSE management systems, adequate insurance cover, and strict adherence to all national and transit-country hazardous goods regulations. Personnel & Fleet Standards: Competent, medically fit, and product-trained drivers subject to a zero-tolerance alcohol and drug policy, alongside strict fatigue and journey management. Vehicles must be roadworthy, legally compliant (axle limits, speed governors, ABS), and equipped with GPS, firefighting, and spill response gear. Category-Specific Vehicle Vetting: White Oils: Verified tanker integrity, calibrated compartments, leak/pressure tests, and spill/fire prevention equipment. LPG: Technical integrity and emergency shutdowns (for bulk); or secure decking, ventilation, and strict cylinder stacking limits (for cylinders). Lubricants: Proper product segregation, secure packaging, and contamination prevention controls. Operational Controls: Acceptance of mandatory "safe-to-load/offload" inspections, strict adherence to Rubis site and traffic rules, and the provision of periodic HSE and operational performance reports. Note: Tender-stage requirements are for pre-qualification only. Shortlisted transporters will undergo further rigorous HSE, technical, and product-specific vetting before final award and depot access. Next Steps Interested transporters meeting the minimum criteria are requested to submit their Expression of Interest (EOI) along with preliminary compliance documents (company registration, transport licenses, HSE policies, and fleet details) latest 26th October 2026 at Rubis Head Office KABC 4th Floor in sealed envelop, tender opening will be same date at 3:00 PM. Upon review of the initial submissions, qualified bidders will be scheduled for a comprehensive HSE briefing and vetting session. We look forward to receiving your proposal and potentially partnering with you. For more information reach out to Email: grace.karibori@rubisrwanda.com Phone: +250788507340/ +250728507340

raw_text: Effective date: October 1st, 2026 Request for Proposal [Tender for Provision of Crisis Modifier Supplies] RFP DOCUMENT :19/2026 RFP ISSUE DATE: [October 6, 2026] PROPOSAL SUBMISSION DEADLINE: [October 22,2026, 17:00 Kigali Time] Confidential Document Prepared by CARE RWANDA ABOUT CARE At CARE, we seek a world of hope, inclusion, and social justice, where poverty has been overcome and people live with dignity and security. This has been our vision since 1945, when we were founded to send lifesaving CARE Packages to survivors of World War II. Today, CARE is a leader in the global movement to end poverty. CONTENTS PART A — INVITATION TO QUOTE PART B — INSTRUCTIONS TO QUOTERS PART C — SCHEDULE OF REQUIREMENTS PART D — EVALUATION AND AWARD PART E — TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF AWARD FORM 1 — QUOTATION SUBMISSION FORM FORM 2 — PRICE SCHEDULE FORM 3 — CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND ELIGIBILITY DECLARATION PART A — INVITATION TO QUOTE The African Wildlife Foundation (AWF), Rwanda Country Office, invites eligible and qualified companies to submit quotations for Consultancy for an Integrated Protected-Area Monitoring and Control-Room Information System – RDB (AWF-RW/RFP/FY27/033). The African Wildlife Foundation (AWF) Rwanda Country Office invites qualified firms to submit technical and financial proposals for a consultancy to develop a national biodiversity-monitoring framework and data-governance protocol for Rwanda's protected areas, and to select, set up and pilot the information platform for the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) control-room network, starting with Volcanoes National Park. The assignment must be completed by 30 April 2027. The platform is not prescribed: bidders are invited to propose how they will assess the current systems and recommend the most suitable platform based on interoperability, cost of maintenance and ease of use. The quality of the proposed methodology carries the largest weight in the evaluation. Hardware and room fit-out are procured under separate contracts (AWF-RW/RFQ/FY27/020 and AWF-RW/RFQ/FY27/025). How to submit Online, through the AWF bid form (scan the QR code at the end of Part A, or open): https://wkf.ms/4rY7RzK . If the tender reference is not filled in, type AWF-RW/RFP/FY27/033. Concerns can be reported confidentially to the Country Coordinator or to the AWF ethics hotline. PART C — SCHEDULE OF REQUIREMENTS C.1 Background The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) is building an integrated protected-area monitoring and control-room network: a national control room at RDB headquarters in Kigali that brings together information from Rwanda's four national parks, and new site-level control rooms at Volcanoes National Park (VNP) and Gishwati-Mukura National Park (GMNP). Nyungwe and Akagera National Parks are managed by African Parks and already use their own operational platform (EarthRanger). Monitoring and operational data are currently spread across several tools – SMART patrol data, ArcGIS layers and services, sensor and telemetry feeds, community-monitoring tools and the African Parks systems – with no common national framework for biodiversity monitoring indicators, data standards, data sharing or data governance. AWF supports RDB, under the Volcanoes Conservation and Development Programme, to put in place both the national framework and the information system that makes it operational, starting with a park-level pilot at VNP. The VNP control room is delivered through three separate contracts: ICT and audio-visual equipment (AWF-RW/RFQ/FY27/020), room partitioning, fit-out and furniture (AWF-RW/RFQ/FY27/025), and this consultancy. This consultancy covers services only; no hardware, works or furniture. C.2 Scope of work Inception and assessment: review the current systems, data sources, data quality, interoperability, hosting, connectivity and staff capacity at RDB HQ, VNP and GMNP, and the platforms used in Nyungwe and Akagera; consult RDB, African Parks and other data holders. Platform options analysis and recommendation: compare realistic platform options (for example EarthRanger, SMART Connect, ArcGIS-based solutions, or a combination) and recommend one, using at least these criteria: (i) fit with the current status of systems and data and interoperability with SMART, ArcGIS, sensor/telemetry feeds and the African Parks systems; (ii) total cost of ownership over five years, including licences, hosting, maintenance and support; (iii) ease of use for operators, rangers and administrators; (iv) data sovereignty, hosting and security; (v) local support capacity and sustainability; (vi) scalability to all parks. The recommendation is presented to RDB and AWF and must be approved in writing before implementation starts. National biodiversity-monitoring framework and data-governance protocol: propose core monitoring indicators and protocols across the parks, data standards and a data dictionary, roles and responsibilities, data flows, access rights, data sharing and confidentiality rules (including sensitive species data), quality assurance and archiving; validate with RDB and stakeholders in a workshop. Implementation of the approved platform: configure the platform for RDB HQ, VNP and GMNP; integrate SMART, ArcGIS, sensor/telemetry and community-monitoring data; arrange data exchange with the Nyungwe and Akagera systems, subject to agreement with African Parks. Park-level operational pilot at VNP and control-room dashboards: design and deploy the operational dashboards, including the four live dashboards for the VNP display wall and the national views for RDB HQ; configure alerts and reports; test end-to-end and support go-live once the equipment from tender 020 is installed. Capacity building: train RDB control-room operators, rangers using field apps, and system administrators; provide user and administrator guides and short video tutorials. Handover and sustainability: integration architecture, configuration records, credentials and documentation handed to RDB; a costed operation and maintenance plan; post-go-live support for one month. title: Request for Proposal for Audit Services
raw_text: REF:117/CEO/KRK/26 Date: 15th October 2026 Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Request for proposal for Audit Services Kinazi Cassava Plant (KCP) Ltd is a cassava-processing factory located in Ruhango District, Southern Province of Rwanda; the factory produces fine cassava flour for human consumption and industrial use. Under this year of 2026, KCP is seeking to hire an audit firm to provide financial, compliance and value for money audit services for a year ending 31st December 2026, renewable for other 2 years subject to satisfactory performance of the assignment. KCP is now soliciting proposals (both technical and financial to be submitted separately in sealed envelopes) from qualified/Listed audit firms by both (iCPAR and RRA) for “Assurance Services to Provide Financial Audit Services to Kinazi Cassava Plant Ltd”. An acceptance of the best offer will be based on evaluation results of your proposals consistent with the criteria set out in this RFP, and in accordance with procurement regulations. Interested and qualified bidder should submit their proposals at the following address: Kinazi Cassava Plant, Chic building, 2nd floor. Attn. to: Chief Executive Officer, cc: Procurement Officer The successful Audit firm shall be endorsed and supervised by Office of Auditor General of State Finances. Kris R. KABALIRA Chief Executive Officer Kinazi Cassava Plant Ltd TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToR) Recruitment of an External Auditor Background Kinazi Cassava Plant ltd is a company operating in Rwanda. The organisation is seeking to recruit an independent and qualified external audit firm to conduct an annual audit of its financial statements and provide assurance on the accuracy, completeness and reliability of its financial reporting. Under the supervision of Auditor General of State Finances, the engagement will be undertaken in accordance with applicable laws and regulations of the Republic of Rwanda, International Standards on Auditing (ISA), the applicable financial reporting framework, and relevant requirements of the Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Rwanda (ICPAR). Objective of the Assignment The overall objective is to appoint an independent external auditor to: Audit the organisation's annual financial statements. Express an independent professional opinion on whether the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position and financial performance of the organisation. Assess compliance with applicable accounting, tax and statutory requirements. Value for money Audit Review the adequacy of internal controls and financial management systems. Identify significant weaknesses, risks and areas requiring improvement. Provide practical recommendations to strengthen governance, financial management and internal controls. Scope of Work The external auditor shall conduct the audit in accordance with International Standards on Auditing and applicable Rwandan laws and regulations. The assignment shall include, but not be limited to: Financial Statements The auditor shall audit: Statement of financial position; Statement of income/expenditure or profit and loss; Statement of changes in equity; Statement of cash flows; Notes to the financial statements; and Supporting accounting records and schedules. Accounting and Internal Controls The auditor shall: Review the accounting systems and procedures; Assess key internal controls over income, expenditure, assets and liabilities; Review segregation of duties and authorisation procedures; Assess the adequacy of supporting documentation; Identify material control weaknesses and associated risks; and Recommend improvements where necessary. Compliance The auditor shall assess compliance, as applicable, with: Rwanda tax laws and regulations; Rwanda company and accounting legislation; Applicable employment and statutory requirements; The organisation's financial policies and procedures; and Other relevant laws and regulations. Verification The auditor shall undertake appropriate audit procedures, including: Examination of accounting records and supporting documents; Bank and cash verification; Review of assets and liabilities; Review of payroll and statutory deductions; Review of procurement and expenditure transactions; Verification of selected income and expenditure transactions; Review of related-party transactions, where applicable; and Other procedures considered necessary to form an audit opinion. Specific Responsibilities of the Auditor The appointed audit firm shall: Develop an appropriate audit plan and timetable. Conduct the audit objectively and independently. Obtain sufficient and appropriate audit evidence. Maintain appropriate audit working papers. Communicate significant audit findings promptly to management and/or the Board. Discuss identified weaknesses and proposed corrective actions with management. Issue an independent audit opinion. Prepare a management letter highlighting significant internal-control and financial-management issues. Follow up on recommendations from the previous audit Maintain confidentiality of all information obtained during the assignment. Deliverables The auditor shall provide the following deliverables: Audit planning memorandum/audit plan; Independent Auditor's Reports: Financial report Compliance report Value for money report Audited annual financial statements; Management Letter identifying significant findings and recommendations; Summary of internal-control weaknesses and recommended corrective actions; Any other report required by management, the Board or applicable legislation. Draft audit findings should be discussed with management before finalization of the audit report. Duration of the Assignment The audit is expected to cover the financial year ending 31 December 2026. The audit fieldwork is expected to commence in February 1st, 2027 and be completed by March 5th 2027, with the final audit report submitted no later than March 15th 2027. The engagement may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance, organisational requirements and applicable laws and regulations. Qualifications and Experience of the Audit Firm Interested audit firms should meet the following minimum requirements: Be legally registered and authorised to provide audit services in Rwanda. Be registered with the Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Rwanda (ICPAR) & RRA and hold valid practising credentials as required by applicable law. Demonstrate relevant experience in external/statutory audits. Have qualified and experienced audit personnel. Demonstrate experience auditing organisations of similar size and complexity. Demonstrate knowledge of Rwandan accounting, taxation and regulatory requirements. Have appropriate quality-control and audit procedures. Demonstrate independence and absence of conflicts of interest. Have adequate capacity and resources to complete the assignment within the required timeframe. Independence and Conflict of Interest The audit firm must be independent of the organization and must disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest. The auditor shall not undertake activities that compromise its independence or result in auditing its own work. The selected firm shall sign an independence and conflict-of-interest declaration before commencement of the assignment. Required Team The proposed team should include, at minimum: Engagement Partner/Lead Auditor; Audit Manager/Supervisor; and Qualified audit staff appropriate to the size and complexity of the assignment. The proposal should provide the names, qualifications, professional certifications and relevant experience of the proposed key personnel. Proposal Requirements Interested firms should submit a technical and financial proposal containing: Technical Proposal Company/firm profile; Certificate of registration and relevant licences; ICPAR registration/practising credentials; Understanding of the assignment; Proposed audit methodology and approach; Proposed work plan and timetable; Relevant experience and references; CVs of key personnel; Evidence of similar assignments undertaken; Independence and conflict-of-interest declaration; and At least three relevant client references, where available. Financial Proposal The financial proposal should clearly indicate: Professional audit fees; Applicable taxes; Any reimbursable expenses; Any other costs; and Total proposed cost. Financial proposal must be VAT inclusive All costs must be expressed in Rwandan currency Administrative required documents Valid tax clearance certificate Valid Social security clearance certificate audited financial statements Business licence Anti-fraud, corruption and conflicts of interest Confidentiality All information, documents and data obtained by the auditor during the assignment shall be treated as confidential and shall not be disclosed to third parties without prior written authorisation, except where disclosure is required by law or professional obligations. Additional Requirements Bids must be prepared in English language No blacklisted company allowed to bid Kinazi cassava plant has rights to cancel tender in case there is clear reasons Bid validity period 120 days Evaluation Criteria KCP Ltd will evaluate all proposals based on the following criteria. To ensure consideration for this Request for Proposal, your proposal should be complete and include all of the following criteria: Administrative documents required: as highlighted here in Technical expertise and Overall Proposal Suitability: proposed solution(s) must meet the scope and needs included herein and be presented in a clear and organized manner, Bidders must provide audit plan and methodology, descriptions and documentation of staff technical expertise and experience. Bidders also need to provide their experiences as an organization which include but not limited to years of experiences, financial stability, expertise, and edge to other competitors. Technical proposal is evaluated at 70 % of total marks. Previous Work and Awards: Bidders will be evaluated on examples of their work pertaining to the requirement as well as client testimonials and references Value and Cost: Bidders will be evaluated on the cost of their solution(s) based on the work to be performed in accordance with the scope of this project. The financial proposal is evaluated at 30 % of total marks. Application Procedure Interested and eligible audit firms should submit their proposals to KCP Ltd office physical address at CHIC building, 2nd floor or on emails below not later than 9th, November/ 2026, 10:30 AM. Bids opening will take place at the same location on Monday 9th, November 2026, 11 AM. If you have any questions or require additional information, please do not hesitate to contact our procurement officer on Telephone: +250787833634 or by E-mail: jn.nitabaje@kcp.rw and info@kcp.rw.Late submissions will not be considered. Thank you for your time and consideration. We look forward to receiving your bids. Sincerely, Kris R. Kabalira Chief Executive Officer Kinazi Cassava Plant Ltd Attachment attachment_file_6d2e405135e389355805

title: Tender for the Supply and Implementation of Network Security Firewall and Sd-wan Leo Connectivity Solutions
raw_text: TENDER FOR THE SUPPLY AND IMPLEMENTATION OF NETWORK SECURITY FIREWALL AND SD-WAN LEO CONNECTIVITY SOLUTIONS UMUTANGUHA Finance Company (UFC) Plc, a company duly registered in the Office of the Registrar General under company code number 101310843, licensed by National Bank of Rwanda to operate as Micro Finance Institution. Umutanguha Microfinance operates a Headquarters and multiple geographically distributed branch locations that require secure, reliable and highly available connectivity to support its financial services, internal business applications, cloud services, voice, collaboration and other business operations. As part of its network modernization program, Umutanguha Finance intends to implement a solution for a resilient Wide Area Network incorporating Peplink SD-WAN and bonding technology together with Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite connectivity, to improve branch connectivity and security, centralized visibility and management of WAN performance, support business continuity. The solution will be executed under two components structured as the supply and installation of a SD-WAN, WAN bonding and LEO connectivity and Supply and installation of the Network security Equipment. title: Request for Quotation (RFQ) _Supply and Delivery of Pigs for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project
raw_text: Project/Activity Name Heifer International Rwanda Agresso Work order: RW1338 Country: Rwanda Advertisement for Procurement Request for Quotation (RFQ) Supply and Delivery of Pigs for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project. Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a Nonprofit and International Non-governmental Organization with the mission to alleviate hunger and poverty, while caring for the environment through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become theflagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. Heifer International Rwanda partners with smallholder farmers to build sustainable livelihoods by empowering them to use their own energy, ingenuity, and dreams to fuel their success out of hunger and poverty. Heifer programs mobilize communities and foster the organization of associations, cooperatives and social networks while strengthening their capacity to address development challenges. Purpose and Objective The objective of this procurement is to obtain the required quantities of livestock, meeting the prescribed technical and quality standards, and to deliver them to the designated locations in Rwanda’s Northern, Southern, and Western Provinces. How to Apply Detailed request for Quotation (RFQ) is attached below. All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their proposals, marked with clear subject line: “Supply and Delivery of Pigs for PRISM Project” to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 29th October2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time. Done on October 5th, 2026. Heifer International Rwanda Management Attachment attachment_file_54dcbc98cf6302b75330

Concerns can be reported confidentially to the Country Coordinator or to the AWF ethics hotline. PART C — SCHEDULE OF REQUIREMENTS C.1 Background AWF and the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) are establishing an integrated protected-area control room network so that patrol, ranger, sensor and monitoring data can be viewed in real time. VNP will host one of the new site-level control rooms. The VNP control room will be staffed by three operators and will display four live online dashboards on a four-screen display wall, with one additional large display in the adjacent briefing room. This RFQ covers equipment only. Room partition, interior fit-out, cable containment and furniture are procured under a separate tender (AWF-RW/RFQ/FY27/025), and the monitoring framework, information-system integration and dashboard design under a separate consultancy (AWF-RW/RFP/FY27/033). The supplier will coordinate with both contractors on site. C.2 Scope of work Supply new, genuine, manufacturer-warranted equipment meeting or exceeding the minimum specifications in Part C, with brand, model and datasheet stated for every item. Deliver all equipment to VNP Park Headquarters, Kinigi, and bear all transport, insurance, customs and handling costs to site. Install and connect all equipment, including wall-mounting of displays, power protection and Cat6 data connections, in coordination with the fit-out contractor. Configure the display controller PC to show four web dashboards (URLs provided by AWF/RDB) in full-screen kiosk mode, auto-starting and auto-logging in after a power interruption. Test and commission the complete system in the presence of AWF and RDB representatives and provide a 1-day hands-on training for control-room operators. Provide warranty registration in the name of RDB/AWF, as-built notes and a list of serial numbers, and warranty support for the period offered. title: Request for Proposal for Upgrade and Improvement of Lightning Protection System
raw_text: Title: Request for Proposal for Upgrade and Improvement of Lightning Protection System Ref No: KC/KGL/RFP/04/2026 Tender Method: Request for Proposal (RFP) Kepler College invites qualified and eligible companies to submit bids for the upgrade and improvement of the lightning protection system at Kepler College, located at KG 29 Avenue No. 16, Rusenyi Village, Murama Cell, Kinyinya Sector, Gasabo District, Kigali City, Rwanda. Interested bidders may request the tender documents by emailing: procurement@keplercollege.ac.rw . Any queries or requests for clarification regarding this tender shall be addressed to: procurement@keplercollege.ac.rw . The site visit is mandatory and shall be conducted by appointment, Monday to Friday, from the date of publication until November 16, 2026, between 9:00 AM and 4:00 PM. A maximum of two (2) representatives per bidder may attend the site visit. Bids must be securely sealed, clearly marked with the tender title and reference number, and submitted in two (2) hard copies: one marked “ORIGINAL” and the other “COPY.” Bids must be delivered to the Reception Office of Kepler College, located at KG 29 Avenue No. 16, Kinyinya Sector, Kigali City, no later than Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 2:30 PM local time. Bids will be opened on the same day, Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 3:00 PM local time, in the Kepler College Boardroom, in the presence of bidders or their representatives who choose to attend.
