title: Request for Proposal for Contract for the Supply and Maintenance of the Lightning Alert System
raw_text: RWANDA ULTIMATE GOLF COURSE LTD Company Code: 109031590 Request for Proposal for Contract for the Supply and Maintenance of the Lightning Alert System Procurement Method: National Open Competitive Bidding Procurement Reference Number: 2026/NCB/LAS /RUGC/07 October 2026 Invitation No: 2026/NCB/LAS/RUGC/07 The Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course requests for a proposal for Tender; Supply and Maintenance of the Lightning Alert System, More details on the scope of work are provided in the technical specifications. The Best selected Bidder will be selected based on the lowest-priced quotation, which is eligible and technically compliant with the procedures described in this RFP. The RFP includes the following documents: Section1 - Letter of Invitation. Section 2 - Instructions to Bidders. Section 3 - Technical Proposal and Financial Proposal. Section 4 - Technical Specifications. The RWANDA ULTIMATE GOLF COURSE LTD(RUGC) requests a proposal for the tender of Supply and Maintenance of the Lightning Alert System, during the financial year 2026. You are requested to submit your bid electronically to the email: info@kigaligolf.rw/ procurement@kigaligolf.rw and hard copy to Kigali Golf Course Board room; KG 548 Street & KG 13 Avenue| P.O Box 1919 Kigali-Rwanda the no later than 28th October 2026 at 10:00 Your bid should be compiled by the following documents: Photocopy of trading license having the activity bided for as its main activity Testimonial of tax clearance from RRA. Testimonial of debt clearance from Rwanda social security board Proof of purchase of the tender document (10,000 RWF), to be paid to account number 00040-06992621-27 (Bank of Kigali), in the name of RUGC. Declaration of Commitment letter. Detailed description of the essential technical characteristics of the goods to be provided establishing conformity to technical specifications. It is in this regard that we invite you to submit your quotations, and all bids will be sent to RUGC Email: info@kigaligolf.rw and Procurement@kigaligolf.rw procurement not later than 28th October 2026 at 10:00 AM. Enquiries regarding this tender may be addressed to Email: info@kigaligolf.rw/ Procurement@kigaligolf.rw. or Tel: 252 500 000. 1. Introduction Bidders are invited to submit a Technical Proposal and a Financial Proposal, as specified in these Instructions to the Bidders. The Proposal will be the basis for contract negotiations and ultimately for a signed contract/ Purchase order with the selected Bidder. The Bidder shall bear all costs associated with the preparation and submission of their proposal and contract negotiation. Eligibility Criteria Administrative The Bidder shall submit the following documents: Photocopy of trading license having the activity bided for as its main activity Testimonial of tax clearance from RRA. Testimonial of debt clearance from Rwanda social security board Proof of purchase of the tender document (10,000 RWF), to be paid to account number 00040-06992621-27 (Bank of Kigali), in the name of RUGC Declaration of Commitment letter. Criteria of technical and financial conformity. Detailed description of the essential technical characteristics of the goods to be provided establishing conformity to technical specifications. Evaluation of Proposals The evaluation of Proposals will be done as detailed below: Preliminary examination to determine eligibility (as defined below) and administrative compliance to this tender on a pass/fail Proposals failing at any stage will be eliminated and not considered in subsequent stages. Detailed Technical Proposals failing at any stage will be eliminated and not considered in subsequent Financial Proposal evaluation An accurate and clear detailed summary of the cost of the financial proposal 4. Best Evaluated Bid The best evaluated bid shall be the lowest priced quotation, which is eligible and technically compliant. 5. Terms of Payment Payment shall be made against the invoice after delivery of the product through bank transfer in favor of the Bidder ’s Bank. Payment shall be made within 30 days against submission of your Invoice and supporting documents following delivery of the goods. The Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course Ltd will pay correctly addressed and undisputed invoices within 30 days. The essential information on the invoice for the RUGC is: A description of the product The invoice should be attached to the contract/Purchase Addressed to the finance department for The costs include VAT (if applicable). Bank details should be accurate and conform to the 6. Award of Contract The contract will be awarded after the evaluation of the Administration, Technical and Financial Proposal. 7. Taxes The Bidder may be subject to local taxes on amounts payable by the Client under the Contract. 8. Delivery period The goods shall be delivered to RUGC within fifteen (15) days from the date of issuance of the Purchase Order, in accordance with the terms and conditions of the contract. The Bidder may request a clarification of any of the RFP documents up to two (2) days before the proposal submission date. Any request for clarification must be sent in writing, or by standard electronic means to the Client’s address indicated in the instructions to Bidder. 10. Preparation of Proposals In preparing their Proposal, the Bidder is expected to examine in detail the documents comprising the RFP. 11. Language Documents to be issued by the Bidder as part of this assignment must be in English. 12. Technical Proposal A Bidder is required to submit a Full Technical Proposal (FTP) that reflects and matches the specifications outlined in the RFP. 13. Financial Proposals A Bidder is required to submit a Financial Proposal (FP). It shall list all costs associated with this assignment, including all costs as below. SECTION 4: TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS OF LIGHTNING ALERT SYSTEM Supply, Delivery and Installation of Replacement Spare Parts for PREVISTORM® Electric Field Sensor/Lightening Alert System Installed at RUGC 1. Scope of work The Supplier shall supply, deliver, and install the following, and provide commissioning support to restore full sensor functionality: Conduct a deep a detailed system inspection to diagnose the root cause of the failure and propose the most adequate solution PREVISTORM® Electric Field Sensor Motherboard, 24V , replacing the damaged unit identified in the site inspection. Associated connection cables, adapters, and consumables required for a complete, functional installation (e.g., RS232 to USB adapter cable, sensor connection cabling). On-site installation of the replacement part into the existing enclosure/mounting, reconnection to the system console, and verification of communication and readings. Basic operational training for the Organization's designated personnel on monitoring the console output and recognizing fault conditions. 2 Spare Part Specification (for Reference) The Supplier shall confirm exact part numbers and compatibility with the existing PREVISTORM® installation prior to order confirmation. Item Reference Qty Notes PREVISTORM® Electric Field Sensor Motherboard, 24V 700023 1 Primary replacement part RS232 (D-Sub 9) to USB Adapter Cable 700053 1 Console communication interface Connection cabling / accessories [Confirm with supplier] As required To match existing installation Detailed technical specifications of PREVISTORM® Electric Field Sensor Motherboard, 24V. Normative: IEC 62793:2016. CLASS A. EN 55011/22 (Radiated and Conducted) EN 61000-3-2, EN 61000-3-3 EN 61000-4-3, EN 61000-4-4, EN 61000-4-5, EN 61000-4-6, EN 61000-4-8, EN 61000-4-11 Environmental: Operating temperature: -23ºC a +50ºC. Humidity: 0% a 100%. IP Level: IP65. Construction: Operating principle: Electric Field Mill. Motor type: brushless. Material: Stainless steel and aluminium. Fixation: Direct insertion into the mast top. Weight: 1,85kg. Electric: Cabling: 20 meters multi-via cable. Contact INGESCO for other lengths and customizations. Power: Standard model: 24V±10%@500mA(max). Extended model with de-icing: 48V±10%@2.0A(max). Communications interface: Isolated RS232, 57600, 8n1, Full-duplex. Signalling outputs: 2 isolated relay outputs. Operation: Measurement range: ±100kVm-1. Resolution: 1Vm-1 (when operating at highest sensitivity). Precision: ±10Vm-1 (when operating at highest sensitivity). Data rate: 4 samples per second. Lightning detection range: up to 20km. Response time: 150ms (with data filtering disabled). Alarm levels: 4 (No alarm, Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3). Options and extras: Power supply: Consult INGESCO. Customized cable: Contact INGESCO. De-icing and heaters: Available only for the 48V model. Recommended for installation in sites where snow and frost occur. Remote console: Console with LCD display, integrated power supply, and four (4) dry relay outputs. Contact INGESCO specifying the product code “PREVISTORM® Thunderstorm Warning System MAD” Jacobus Johannes Visagie, General Manager Attachment attachment_file_8420f849942e787c6ff3

title: Public Notice – Invitation to Submit Fleet Offers (VW Fleet Deals)
raw_text: PUBLIC NOTICE INVITATION TO SUBMIT FLEET OFFERS VW Fleet Deals: sale of pre-owned Volkswagen vehicles in fleet quantities Volkswagen Mobility Solutions Rwanda Ltd invites companies, public institutions, NGOs and individuals to submit offers to purchase pre-owned Volkswagen vehicles in fleet quantities. Bidders name the models, the number of units and the price they propose per vehicle. Offers close on 30th October 2026. 1. Vehicles available Model Year Units Seats / fuel Mileage Indicative price (RWF) T6 Caravelle 2025 4 7 · Diesel 30–50,000 km 52,000,000 Teramont 2023 17 7 · Petrol 30–55,000 km 55,000,000 Tiguan Allspace 2023 11 7 · Petrol 30–50,000 km 37,000,000 T-Cross 2024 30 5 · Petrol 40–60,000 km 35,000,000 Virtus 2024 40 5 · Petrol 40–60,000 km 30,000,000 Total 102 All vehicles are automatic. Indicative prices are per vehicle; mileage varies by vehicle and warranty cover varies by registration year. 2. Who may submit an offer Registered companies, public institutions, NGOs, embassies and international organisations Individuals Offers may be for one vehicle or several, in any combination of models 3. Viewing and inspection Bidders are encouraged to inspect the vehicles before submitting an offer. Location: Amahoro Stadium parking (Kwa Rwahama), Kigali Hours: Monday to Sunday, 8:00 am – 6:00 pm 4. How to submit an offer Scan the QR code or click here to submit your Fleet Offer. State your company or name, contact details, the models and number of units you want, and your proposed price per vehicle. Offers may also be sent by email to sales.rw@vw.rw . Deadline: 30th October 2026. Late offers will not be considered. 5. Evaluation and selection Volkswagen Mobility Solutions Rwanda will review all offers after the deadline, taking into account the price offered, the number of units and the payment terms. Selected bidders will be contacted directly. Offers are treated as confidential. Volkswagen Mobility Solutions Rwanda reserves the right to accept or reject any offer, in whole or in part, without giving reasons. The highest offer will not necessarily be accepted. Enquiries: 0781 924 627 | 0788 368 527 · sales.rw@vw.rw Management, Volkswagen Mobility Solutions Rwanda Ltd

title: Tender Notice for Construction of Poser Houses for Poser and Mental Health Beneficiaries at Burera, Kirehe and Kayonza Districts
raw_text: PUBLIC TENDER NOTICE # PIH/IMB/10819/M09/FY27 TENDER TITTLE: CONSTRUCTION OF POSER HOUSES FOR POSER AND MENTAL HEALTH BENEFICIARIES AT BURERA, KIREHE AND KAYONZA DISTRICTS. SOURCING METHOD: OPEN COMPETITION FOR DOMESTIC COMPANIES. Partners In Health (PIH) is a nonprofit organization with its headquarters in Boston, Massachusetts, whose mission is to provide quality health care for poor and most in need populations around the world. Since 2005, the Ministry of Health in Rwanda has worked with PIH Rwanda, also known as Inshuti Mu Buzima, to improve the quality of care in the country and increase health care access for Rwanda most in need populations. PIH/IMB have since helped to bring high-quality health care to three Districts namely: Kayonza, Burera and Kirehe. Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima is seeking proposals from qualified and authorized Construction companies for Construction of POSER Houses for POSER and Mental Health beneficiaries at Burera, Kirehe and Kayonza Districts as per term of reference (ToRs) and BoQ found in annex. Interested and qualified bidders should provide their proposals bearing the following requirements: I. BIDDERS/ VENDORS ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA The bidders falling in any of the following categories will be ineligible to participate in this tender and / or its award: The Bidder should not be suspended or blacklisted by PIH-IMB or OnePIH nor blacklisted or revoked licenses by the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority or other relevant regulatory bodies. The Bidder should not have any ongoing contracts with PIH-IMB that demonstrates poor performance. Vendors or Companies owner must not be employed by PIH or One PIH within five past years, unless PIH seeks their expertise for consultancy services based on proven specialized knowledge. Any bidder that owns operates, or exercises controlling shareholding in more than one company is strictly prohibited from submitting more than one bid under this tender. Submission of multiple bids by related or affiliated entities under the same beneficial ownership shall constitute a breach of tender participation rules. NB: Non-compliance with any of above provision shall result in the annulment of bid examination process/ tender competition. II. COMPULSORY REQUIREMENTS: a. Site visit certificate is obligatory required. The site visits for the referenced project are scheduled as follows: Kirehe District: the site visit is scheduled to take place on Tuesday, September 29, 2026. All bidders will be required to assemble at the Kirehe Partners in Health/IMB Office at 10:00 AM for departure to the project site. Kayonza District: the site visit is scheduled to take place on Wednesday, September 30, 2026. All bidders will be required to assemble at the KayonzaPartners in Health/IMB Office (Rwinkwavu) at 10:00 AM for departure to the project site. Burera District: the site visit is scheduled to take place on Thursday, October 01, 2026. All bidders will be required to assemble at the Burera Partners in Health/IMB Office (Butaro) at 10:00 AM for departure to the project site. Attendance at the respective site visits will be mandatory for all bidders. A Certificate of Site Visit Attendance will be issued by the Partners In Health representative to the participated companies. b. Bid Security Requirements: The Bidders must submit a bid security based on the value of their financial proposal, as follows: For financial proposals ≥ RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.1%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 950,000,001 to RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.5%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 500,000,001 to RWF 950,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.0%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 100,000,001 to RWF 500,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.5%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 20,000,001 to RWF 100,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 2.0%. No bid security is required for financial proposals with a value of ≤ RWF 20,000,000. III. ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENT: The Bidder shall submit Company profile include: company name; location details, showing a well-known physical address building; Street number Emails, contacts. The Bidder shall submit registration of domestic company issued by RDB in the same domain required. The Bidder shall submit valid RRA tax clearance. The Bidder shall submit VAT registration certificate. IV. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Interested construction companies should consider ToRs (Terms of references) and BoQ available in Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System following this link: (https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/index.php) V. FINANCIALLY, THE BID SHALL INDICATE: A. A commitment letter for the submission of the Performance Security (Bank Guarantee). The letter shall state that, if awarded, the bidder will provide a Performance Security (Bank Guarantee) prior to signing the contract. The Performance Security shall depend on the contract value, as follows: 5% of the contract whose value exceeds FRW 500,000,000; 6% of the contract value between FRW 100,000,000 FRW to FRW 500,000,000; 7% of the contract value between FRW 50,000,000 to FRW 100,000,000; 10% of the contract price whose value is between FRW 20,000,001 to FRW 50,000,000. The performance security is not required for contracts valued at or below FRW 20,000,000. B. The financial proposal shall be submitted in Rwandan Francs currency. C. The financial proposal shall include all applicable taxes and charges. D. The financial proposal shall include terms and conditions of payment (preferably after execution of project). E. The proposal should indicate the shortest execution period. F. The financial proposal validity shall not be lower than 120 calendar days from the day of its submission to PIH. VI. SUBMISSION OF BIDS TO PIH: All proposals from interested bidders must be electronically submitted to Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System ( https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/suppliersubmission.php ) before October 19, 2026 to 11: 59 pm (closing time) Kigali time prompt – Failing to follow this instruction proposals will not be considered. The results of public opening will be available in the system starting from October 20, 2026 00: 00 am. Special Notes: (1) There is no fee paid to obtain the Tender document. (2) Partners In Health is not obliged to purchase or to pay for any costs incurred by the bidder in preparation of his/her proposal in response to this tender notice. (3) PIH/IMB employees are restricted from participating in any PIH tender. (4) For more information about this tender interested bidders shall contact Partners In Health team using following email address:imbprocurement@pih.org/procurement.pih@gmail.com (5)PIH e-procurement bidding processes tutorial is available on: https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/biddingvideo.html Done at Kigali on September 15, 2026 Senior Director of Procurement & Logistics Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima Attachment attachment_file_0f01042cdc6fad1d2af4

title: Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Supply of Cows for the Rwanda Dairy Development Project (RDDP II)
raw_text: Project/Activity Name Heifer International Rwanda Agresso Work order: RW1350 Country: Rwanda Advertisement for Procurement Request for Quotation (RFQ) Supply of Cows for the Rwanda Dairy Development Project (RDDP II) Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a nonprofit International non-governmental organization whose mission to end hunger and poverty, while caring for the earth through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become the flagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. Heifer International Rwanda is in partnering with the Government of Rwanda through the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources for the implementation of the Rwanda Dairy Development Project (RDDP II). Under this partnership, Heifer International Rwanda invites qualified and eligible suppliers to submit quotations for the supply and delivery of cowsheds construction materials to the project locations as listed in the RFQ. Purpose and Objective The main objective is to invite qualified bidders to submit quotations for the supply and delivery of pregnant dairy heifers to beneficiaries in fifteen (15) districts. The procurement is divided into four (4) lots corresponding to Rwanda's four provinces. A bidder may submit a quotation for one or more lots but may be awarded a maximum of one (1) lot. Each lot will be evaluated independently. How to Apply Detailed request for Quotation (RFQ) is attached below. All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their proposals, marked with clear subject line: “Supply and Delivery of Cows for RDDP II” to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 22nd October2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time. Done on September 24th, 2026. Heifer International Rwanda Management Attachment attachment_file_d3744bb108c3d9092cc1

Under this partnership, Heifer International Rwanda invites qualified and eligible suppliers to submit quotations for the supply and delivery of cowsheds construction materials to the project locations as listed in the RFQ. Purpose and Objective The main objective is to invite qualified bidders to submit quotations for the supply and delivery of pregnant dairy heifers to beneficiaries in fifteen (15) districts. The procurement is divided into four (4) lots corresponding to Rwanda's four provinces. A bidder may submit a quotation for one or more lots but may be awarded a maximum of one (1) lot. Each lot will be evaluated independently. How to Apply Detailed request for Quotation (RFQ) is attached below. All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their proposals, marked with clear subject line: “Supply and Delivery of Cows for RDDP II” to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 22nd October2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time. Done on September 24th, 2026. Heifer International Rwanda Management Attachment attachment_file_d3744bb108c3d9092cc1

title: Expressions of Interest Requested for Nyakabingo Project – Construction of the Plant
raw_text: EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST REQUESTED Nyakabingo Project – Construction of the Plant Trinity Nyakabingo Mine Limited is expanding the Nyakabingo Mine. With construction scheduled to commence in 2027, the Nyakabingo Project will significantly grow mine output by opening new reserves and introducing bulk mining, the use of larger mining equipment and the construction of mineral processing facilities to process run-of-mine material and legacy stockpiled material. These plans give the mine the opportunity to double current production levels. Trinity Metals Limited is seeking expressions of interest (EOI) from potential business partners to assist in executing the Nyakabingo Project. The following packages are included in this call for EOI: Package No. Package Name CC-001 Earthworks and Civils Construction CM-001 Structural, Mechanical, Piping and Platework Supply and Erection CM-002 Infrastructural Buildings (offices, stores, etc.) CL-001 Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Installation Package titles are indicative only; detailed scopes of work will be issued with the technical and commercial requirements. Respondents may express interest in one or more packages, either individually or as part of a consortium. Information Required for Evaluation Certified company financial statements for the past three (3) years; Company ownership structure (preference will be given to companies owned by Rwandan citizens); Company organogram and résumés of key personnel; Description of company assets, equipment and facilities; Company health and safety record; Quality assurance systems; A reference list of three (3) similar services delivered, including the scope of work, date, order value (stating currency) and client identification; Certificate of incorporation or business registration, and any relevant contractor licences; and RRA Tax Clearance Certificate. Submission All submissions must be in English and provided as a single PDF file not exceeding 20 MB. Submissions that omit the information listed above may not be evaluated. Businesses are invited to express their interest by emailing tender@trinity-metals.com no later than 12:00 CAT on 2 November 2026, clearly stating which package(s) they are responding to. Disclaimer This call for expressions of interest is not an invitation to tender and does not constitute an offer or a commitment of any kind. Trinity Metals Limited reserves the right to amend the packages, to shortlist or decline any respondent, and to discontinue this process at any time without liability. Respondents bear their own costs of participation, and no fee is payable to Trinity Nyakabingo Mine Limited or any third party to participate.

title: Tender Notice for Furnishing of the DUHAMIC-ADRI Apartment Building (Serenity Residence), Kicukiro District, Niboye Sector
raw_text: TENDER NOTICE TENDER TITLE: FURNISHING OF THE DUHAMIC-ADRI APARTMENT BUILDING (SERENITY RESIDENCE), KICUKIRO DISTRICT, NIBOYE SECTOR. TENDER PUBLICATION DATE October 16,2026 SUBMISSION DEADLINE October 26,2026, at 11:00AM SITE VISIT DATE &TIME Wednesday, October 21,2026 At Kicukiro Niboye Near DUHAMI-ADRI Headquarters VISIT CONTACT 0788305329 SUBMISSION LOCATION DUHAMIC-ADRI Head Office, Kicukiro-Niboye (Only hard copy submissions are accepted) INQUIRY CONTACT EMAIL procurement@duhamic.org.rw Brief description of DUHAMIC-ADRI DUHAMIC -ADRI is an on-profit organization located in Kigali, the capital city of Rwanda, in Kicukiro District, Niboye Sector. Officially operating in Rwanda since 12th July 1985 Mission: Supporting integrated initiatives for Holistic Development of Rural Population in their struggle for self-reliance’ Vision: A rural world responsible for its self-socio-economic development Core Values: Integrity, Professionalism, Transparency Objectives Fighting against the marginalization of rural areas. Stimulating the creation and consolidation of associations, cooperatives and farmers' groups. Enhancing the work of farmers' associations by initiating and encouraging the development of organizational structures such as autonomous groups, cooperatives and unions. Supporting rural development initiatives in various areas of socio-economic development. Tender background In pursuit of institutional sustainability, DUHAMIC-ADRI has invested in the construction of a multi-storey apartment building (Basement + Ground Floor + 2 Upper Floors + Penthouse) located in Kicukiro District, Niboye Sector, on parcels identified under UPIs 1/03/09/02/467, 1/03/09/02/466 and 1/03/09/02/1684. The building is about to be completed and will soon be opened for use. Once completed, it will comprise 14 residential units: 7 one-bedroom apartments with a living room, 3 two-bedroom apartments with a living room and 4 studio apartments, each equipped with a kitchen. To make them ready for use as furnished, mid-range rental apartments, DUHAMIC-ADRI is hiring three (3) qualified, experienced and reputable service providers to carry out the furnishing works, divided into the following three lots: Lot 1: Construction works & construction-related items Lot 2: Supply of furniture, furnishings & non-electrical equipment; Lot 3: Supply of electronics, electrical appliances & equipment The items to be supplied and installed will be in line with the furniture and interior design proposal selected by DUHAMIC-ADRI for the building. The detailed list of items per lot, with quantities and specifications, is provided in the attached Terms of Reference. title: Tender Notice for Provision of Hotel Services
raw_text: TENDER NOTICE PROVISION OF HOTEL SERVICES Pro-Femmes Twese Hamwe (PFTH) is an Umbrella of Rwandan Civil Society Organizations aiming at advancement of women status, peace and development. It was established in October 1992 and currently represents 52 member organizations within the country. The mission of Pro-Femmes/ Twese Hamwe is to eradicate all forms of discrimination against women, to promote their socio-economic political and legal status, and to enhance the institutional and organizational capacities of its member organizations through the promotion of sustainable human development approach based on gender equality and a culture of peace, justice and human rights. PFTH is thus looking for competent service providers to provide hotel services in the following locations: Lot 1: City of Kigali (Centre d’acceuils) ONLY; Lot 2: Southern Province (Nyamagabe, Nyaruguru, Kamonyi, Ruhango and Gisagara Districts); Lot 3: Western Province (Rusizi, Karongi, Rutsiro, Nyabihu and Nyamasheke districts); Lot 4: Eastern Province (Rwamagana, Kayonza, Nyagatare, Gatsibo, Ngoma, Kirehe and Bugesera districts); Lot 5: Northern Province (Rulindo, Burera, Gakenke, Musanze and Gicumbi districts). Tender Documents are obtained on any working day from 8:30 am to 5:00pm local time at PRO-FEMMES TWESE HAMWE Central Secretariat Office, upon presentation of proof payment of a non-refundable fee of ten thousand Rwandan francs(10,000Frw) to the account No: 1002190104949201 of PRO-FEMMES TWESE HAMWE opened in ACCESS Bank. Well-printed and properly bound proposals should be submitted (The technical proposal and financial proposal) in one Big envelope (outer envelope). The application shall be addressed to the Executive Director of Pro-Femmes Twese Hamwe and shall be submitted at PFTH central secertatiat, Head Office in Gahanga sector, Kicukiro district –Kigali City, not later than Monday 26th October 2026at 10:00 AM (Local time). Done at Kigali on 14th October 2026 Annet KAKIBIBI Executive Director

title: Expression of Interest (EoI) for Supply Reusable Sanitary Pads
raw_text: Expression of Interest (EOI): Supply reusable Sanitary Pads Reference Number: 7000025524 Publication date: 15.10.2026 Introduction The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH is a federally owned international cooperation enterprise for sustainable development with worldwide operations. The GIZ Office in Kigali covers GIZ’s portfolio in Rwanda and Burundi. GIZ Rwanda/Burundi implements projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Union and other commissioning authorities in the following priority areas: Sustainable Economic Development; Good Governance; Climate, Energy and Sustainable Urban Development; Digitalization and Digital Economy; and regional projects in the Great Lakes Region. Context GIZ Rwanda’s projects “Prevention of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence” and “ZFD – Supporting Peaceful Coexistence between Host Communities and Refugees” are part of the Rwandan - German development cooperation implemented by GIZ. Both work closely with civil society organizations. Their shared objectives are to strengthen and expand sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) prevention services and services around Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) provided by non-governmental actors and improving support for people affected by SGBV - both within and outside refugee camps. The projects intend to further strengthen the integrated approach on GBV prevention, SRHR and Menstrual Health and Hygiene and Period Poverty alongside peace peacebuilding and gender-based violence prevention It is in that context that GIZ is looking for a reputed and experienced company to supply the following reusable sanitary pads/items: The specifications and quantities are in the table below: Specification of items NO ITEM ITEM SPECIFICATIOM QUANTITY 1 REUSABLE SANITARY PADS Each pack should contain: 5 reusable sanitary pads. Reusable cloth pads with wings Medium size: 30cm length and 18cm width with wings Shall be able to handle normal and more heavily flow. A hanger for drying. Each pack should have one leak proof travel pouch to store a minimum of two soiled pads and shall be reusable. An info sheet;( must be multilingual English, French and Kinyarwanda) Instructions for use and shall include use, wash, and care instructions, preferably with illustrations or pictograms. Top sheet is made of fleece. The absorbent core is made of Microfiber. The reusable sanitary pads shall have securement mechanisms such as plastic snaps for the wings to firmly attach the product to underwear to prevent dislocation while use. Product shall be unscented only. The reusable sanitary pads are packed in an appealing, durable bag that can be closed with a zipper (it is not visible what is inside)" The pads shall be free from: acids and alkali, dust and particulate matter, bad odour bleeding of colour, shedding fibres chemical residues like chlorine, herbicides, pesticides, heavy metals. Products shall be capable of being soaked and washed thoroughly in water up to 60℃ using soap or laundry detergent. Wear Time: Shall be able to wear for 6 to 8 hours. Durability: the product shall be able to withstand a minimum of 120 washes during hand wash The seam line shall be free of loose threads and neat. It shall have dimensional stability with good tensile strength and seam strength. 2500 packs of 5 reusable sanitary pads each(therefore, a total of 12.500 reusable sanitary pads) Procedure The assessment is divided into three stages: Eligibility check, technical and financial evaluation: Eligibility criteria Participating companies must meet the following eligibility criteria: The company must have a minimum experience of 3 years in Rwanda supplying similar items to different institutions. three Letters of Reference from the past three years from such institutions must be provided. The company must possess a valid registration certificate (issued by RDB), VAT certificate (issued by RRA) and latest Tax clearance certificate (issued by RRA). The company must confirm in writing that the offer is valid until at least 4 weeks after the submission period has ended. Please submit the documentary evidence for the above criteria. Non-submission/Partial submission of commercial/technical documents mentioned above by any supplier will lead to a rejection of the entire bid. Technical Assessment The bidders are encouraged to include a company profile that displays they fulfil the eligibility requirements. The technical specification of each item proposed must meet the technical requirements as described above. The offer must provide clear and complete specifications of items proposed. As part of the technical evaluation process, GIZ will request eligible bidders to provide a sample of products based on the technical specification. This sample must be delivered to GIZ Rwanda’s Country Office in Kiyovu, 17 KN 41 St, Kigali within 5 working days upon instructions by GIZ’s Procurement Department. The cost of the sample is borne by the bidder. By submitting an offer, the supplier agrees that there is no additional charge for a sample of product to GIZ as a buyer. Upon completion of the technical evaluation, GIZ will inform suppliers when and where to pick up the samples. The samples must be in good condition and will be returned similarly after finalization of the evaluation. Financial Evaluation The financial evaluation will be done only in respect of those firms, which meet the eligibility criteria and the technical requirements. Offer must indicate the unit price of item and total price as per quantities given. Total amount of the price must be VAT exclusive, if applicable. Other conditions: Delivery place: The items will be delivered at Golf View Rise Building at Kacyiru-Gasabo, KG 563 St. Delivery period: the items must be delivered to GIZ within 14 days after signing confirmation of the order. Submission of the offer Please submit electronically your offer in PDF file to this email only: RW_Quotation@giz.deuntil latest 28.10.2026 You must write in your email subject this sentence: 7000025524 - Supply of Reusable Sanitary Pads without this sentence, your offer may not be considered. If the emails exceed the default email size of 30MB, offers can be exceptionally submitted through https://filetransfer.giz.de/ Offers submitted through any other sharing platform, as google documents or similar will not be considered. Hard copies are not allowed this time. GIZ Rwanda reserves all rights

title: Tender Notice For supply and Delivery of Infant Formula at Rwinkwavu IMB Pharmacy Warehouse Under a Framework Agreement
raw_text: PUBLIC TENDER NOTICE # PIH/IMB/10941 /M10/FY27 TENDER TITTLE: SUPPLY AND DELIVERY OF INFANT FORMULA AT RWINKWAVU IMB PHARMACY WAREHOUSE UNDER A FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT. SOURCING METHOD: OPEN COMPETITION FOR DOMESTIC COMPANIES. Partners In Health (PIH) is a nonprofit organization with its headquarters in Boston, Massachusetts, whose mission is to provide quality health care for poor and most in need populations around the world. Since 2005, the Ministry of Health in Rwanda has worked with PIH Rwanda, also known as Inshuti Mu Buzima, to improve the quality of care in the country and increase health care access for Rwanda most in need populations. PIH/IMB have since helped to bring high-quality health care to three Districts namely: Kayonza, Burera and Kirehe. Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima is seeking proposals from qualified and authorized medical companies to supply infant formula at Rwinkwavu IMB Pharmacy warehouse under a framework agreement as per term of reference (ToRs) found in annex. Interested and qualified bidders should provide their proposals bearing the following requirements: BIDDERS/ VENDORS ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA The bidders falling in any of the following categories will be ineligible to participate in this tender and / or its award: The Bidder should not be suspended or blacklisted by PIH-IMB or OnePIH nor blacklisted or revoked licenses by the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority or other relevant regulatory bodies. The Bidder should not have any ongoing contracts with PIH-IMB that demonstrates poor performance. Vendors or Companies owner must not be employed by PIH or One PIH within five past years, unless PIH seeks their expertise for consultancy services based on proven specialized knowledge. Any bidder that owns operates, or exercises controlling shareholding in more than one company is strictly prohibited from submitting more than one bid under this tender. Submission of multiple bids by related or affiliated entities under the same beneficial ownership shall constitute a breach of tender participation rules. NB: Non-compliance with any of above provision shall result in the annulment of bid examination process/ tender competition. COMPULSORY REQUIREMENTS: The Bidder shall submit a comprehensive Company Profile, including, but not limited to, the following: Company Identification; Physical Address and Contact Details; Legal and Registration Information; Nature of Business; Ownership and Management Structure; Relevant Experience and Capacity; Business Facilities including warehouse(s) and/or store(s); and Business Partners. III. ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENT: The Bidder shall submit registration of domestic company issued by RDB in the same domain required. The Bidder shall submit valid RRA tax clearance. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Bidders should consider ToRs available in Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System following this link: (https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/index.php) FINANCIALLY, THE BID SHALL INDICATE: A commitment letter for the submission of the Performance Security (Bank Guarantee). The letter shall state that, if awarded, the bidder will provide a Performance Security (Bank Guarantee per each purchase order exceeding FRW 20,000,000. The financial proposal shall be submitted in Rwandan Francs currency. The financial proposal shall include all applicable taxes and charges. The bidder shall specify the brand and country of origin of each proposed product. The financial proposal shall include terms and conditions of payment (preferably after delivery). The proposal should indicate the shortest delivery period after reception of purchase order The financial proposal validity shall not be lower than 120 calendar days from the day of its submission to PIH. INCOTERMS:DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) at Kayonza IMB office (Rwinkwavu warehouse) BID EVALUATION AND TENDER AWARD The bids will be evaluated as one lot, and the tender will be awarded to one successful bidder for the entire lot. Bidders are therefore encouraged to submit quotations for all items included in the tender. VIII. SUBMISSION OF BIDS TO PIH: All proposals from interested bidders must be electronically submitted to Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System ( https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/suppliersubmission.php ) before November 09, 2026 to 11: 59 pm (closing time) Kigali time prompt – Failing to follow this instruction proposals will not be considered. The results of public opening will be available in the system starting from November 10, 2026, 00: 00 am. SPECIAL NOTES: There is no fee paid to obtain the Tender document. Partners In Health is not obliged to purchase or to pay for any costs incurred by the bidder in preparation of his/her proposal in response to this tender notice. PIH/IMB employees are restricted from participating in any PIH tender. For more information about this tender interested bidders shall contact Partners In Health team using following email address:imbprocurement@pih.org/procurement.pih@gmail.com. The PIH Team will provide to invited suppliers any technical support in regard with this Tender during working hours from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm using e-mail addresses above mentioned PIH e-procurement bidding processes tutorial is available on: https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/biddingvideo.html Done at Kigali on October 9, 2026 Senior Director of Procurement & Logistics Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima Attachment attachment_file_a9674ac2eda1eb72e9db

title: Request for Quotation (RFQ)_Supply and Delivery of Goats and Sheep for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project
raw_text: Project/Activity Name Heifer International Rwanda Agresso Work order: RW1338 Country: Rwanda Advertisement for Procurement Request for Quotation (RFQ) Supply and Delivery of Goats and Sheep for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project. Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a Nonprofit and International Non-governmental Organization with the mission to alleviate hunger and poverty, while caring for the environment through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become theflagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. Heifer International Rwanda partners with smallholder farmers to build sustainable livelihoods by empowering them to use their own energy, ingenuity, and dreams to fuel their success out of hunger and poverty. Heifer programs mobilize communities and foster the organization of associations, cooperatives and social networks while strengthening their capacity to address development challenges. Purpose and Objective The objective of this procurement is to obtain the required quantities of livestock, meeting the prescribed technical and quality standards, and to deliver them to the designated locations in Rwanda’s Northern, Southern, and Western Provinces. How to Apply Detailed request for Quotation (RFQ) is attached below. All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their proposals, marked with clear subject line: “Supply and Delivery of Goats and Sheep for PRISM Project” to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 29th October2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time. Done on October 5th, 2026. Heifer International Rwanda Management Attachment attachment_file_b2ce3b2c8d99c849dde7

raw_text: A call for expressions of interest for the supply and service provision by pre-qualified service providers for the year 2026 The African Evangelistic Enterprise (AEE-Rwanda) is a Christian, local, non-Governmental organization dedicated to working with children, youths, families and their communities to address the root causes of poverty. title: Tender Notice for Provision of Migration Services for Google Workspace to Microsoft 365 and Mac Device Management
raw_text: SUSTAINABLE GROWERS RWANDA P.O BOX 864 Kigali, Rwanda INVITATION TO BID Title of Tender: Provision of Migration Services for Google Workspace to Microsoft 365 and Mac Device ManagementTender Reference Number: MSGWS/10/2026 Procurement Method: Open Tender Date of Issue: 13 October 2026 Submission Deadline: 23 October 2026 at 5:00 PM (17h00) Kigali time I. Introduction Sustainable Growers Rwanda (SGR) is a non-governmental organization that specializes in innovative coffee cultivation training for smallholder women coffee farmers, with the goal of increasing their visibility in the coffee supply chain. Supported by Bloomberg Philanthropies and the governments of Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania, SGR has reached over 77,000 women farmers and over 341,000 family members. SGR currently runs on Google Workspace and uses Apple MacBooks exclusively. It intends to move to Microsoft 365 Business Premium and adopt cloud-native identity and device management through Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Intune. SGR has approximately 19 users and will not deploy or maintain any on-premises infrastructure. SGR is therefore seeking a qualified Microsoft partner to plan and deliver the migration, configure the tenant and its security baseline, bring the MacBook estate under management, and hand over a documented environment that the SGR IT Manager can operate independently. II. General Qualifications and Required Documents The objective of this tender is to identify a professional, experienced firm to deliver a complete Google Workspace to Microsoft 365 migration and Mac device management implementation for SGR. 1. Administrative documents (mandatory, pass/fail) Registration certificate from RDB Valid tax clearance certificate from Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) Valid social security clearance certificate from RSSB, if applicable Confirmation that the bidder has an Electronic Billing Machine (EBM) Evidence of current Microsoft Partner status (e.g. Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program listing or partner ID) At least three (3) completed Microsoft 365 migration or configuration projects; at least one should include migration from Google Workspace or another non-Microsoft platform Demonstrated experience managing Apple macOS devices through Microsoft Intune, with at least one reference. Administrative requirements for international bidders. This tender is open to qualified national and international firms. In place of items 1 to 4 above, international bidders must submit valid company registration documents and equivalent tax compliance certificates or other applicable statutory documents issued by the competent authorities in their country of establishment, subject to SGR’s verification and acceptance. 2. Pricing instructions All prices must be quoted in Rwandan Francs (RWF), with VAT shown separately and included in the total. International bidders must convert their prices into RWF and state the exchange rate and date used. Migration and implementation services must be quoted at standard commercial rates and itemized separately from any Microsoft licensing costs. Any optional item, assumption or exclusion must be stated separately. SGR will not accept unapproved hidden or post-award charges. Prices shall not change for the duration of the contract. Pricing and withholding taxes. International bidders shall ensure that their financial quotations take into account all applicable taxes and statutory deductions under Rwandan law, including withholding taxes (WHT). Where applicable, withholding tax shall be deducted and remitted to the Rwanda Revenue Authority in accordance with the law. Bidders should factor this tax treatment into their quoted prices, as withholding tax shall not constitute an additional payment over and above the accepted contract price. III. Terms of Reference 1. Objectives The objective of this assignment is to contract a qualified service provider to: Migrate SGR from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365 Business Premium without permanent loss of mail, calendar or file data. Establish Microsoft Entra ID as the primary identity platform for all users and connected applications. Implement Microsoft Intune for management of all SGR macOS devices. Configure Microsoft security and compliance baseline controls, including MFA, Conditional Access, self-service password reset and Microsoft Defender for Business. Migrate Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive content to Exchange Online, OneDrive and SharePoint Online, validated against an agreed test plan. Create Apple Business Manager (ABM), integrate it with Entra ID and Intune, and recommend a future device procurement and enrolment path. Provide knowledge transfer, administrator training and documentation so the SGR IT Manager can run the environment after handover. 2. Current Environment and Target State Figures below are estimates. The selected provider must measure and confirm them during discovery. Area Current Target Users Approximately 19 Approximately 19 on Microsoft 365 Business Premium (nonprofit) Identity Google Workspace accounts Microsoft Entra ID Mail and calendar Gmail, Google Calendar Exchange Online with Outlook Files Google Drive OneDrive and SharePoint Online Meetings and chat Google Meet Microsoft Teams Devices Approximately 20 Apple MacBooks from multiple vendors, not centrally managed Same devices enrolled and managed in Intune Endpoint protection Not centrally managed Microsoft Defender for Business Device procurement Mixed vendors, no central enrolment Apple Business Manager linked to Intune On-premises infrastructure None None, and none planned Data to migrate Approximately 1.2 TB (Gmail and Google Drive combined) Migrated and validated in Microsoft 365 3. Scope of Work The selected provider shall deliver the following services. Bidders may propose their own phasing, but every item below must be covered. 3.1 Assessment and discovery Audit the Google Workspace tenant: users, groups, aliases, delegated access, service accounts, shared drives, sharing permissions and external links, calendar resources and shared calendars. Measure actual mail and Drive volumes per user and per shared drive, rather than relying on the 1.2 TB estimate. Identify all third-party services that use "Sign in with Google" or integrate with Google Workspace, and propose how each will authenticate after migration. Inventory every MacBook: model, chipset, macOS version, purchase source, serial number and Apple Business Manager eligibility. Review domains, DNS hosting and current MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records. Produce a migration plan and risk assessment, including migration tooling, data mapping, pre-stage and delta sync approach, cutover runbook, rollback plan with go/no-go criteria, and an end-user communication plan. 3.2 Microsoft 365 tenant configuration Configure Entra ID: domains, users, groups, roles and group-based licensing. Enforce multi-factor authentication (Microsoft Authenticator) for all users and configure self-service password reset. Create and document break-glass emergency access accounts and apply a least-privilege administrator model. Build Conditional Access policies (MFA, block legacy authentication, compliant-device requirement), tested in report-only mode before enforcement. Apply Microsoft-recommended security baselines and Exchange Online protection (anti-spam, anti-phishing, Safe Links, malware). Configure baseline Microsoft Purview controls: starting sensitivity labels, data loss prevention rules and retention policies. 3.3 Google Workspace migration Migrate Gmail to Exchange Online, Google Calendar to Outlook, and Google Drive and shared drives to OneDrive and SharePoint Online. Agree how Google-native files (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Sites, Apps Script) will be converted or handled as exceptions. Run a pilot with the IT Manager and a small user group before production migration. Pre-stage bulk data ahead of cutover so the go-live weekend carries only the final delta sync, DNS change and validation. Execute the cutover over a single weekend and validate mail flow, calendar integrity, file access, permissions and sign-in against the agreed test plan. Provide on-site support on the first business day after cutover. 3.4 Microsoft Teams deployment Configure team and channel structure, meeting, messaging and calling policies, external and guest access, and collaboration settings. 3.5 Microsoft Intune implementation Configure macOS enrolment (Company Portal and Automated Device Enrolment where eligible). Deploy compliance policies (OS version, FileVault, firewall, password) and configuration profiles. Enable FileVault encryption with recovery key escrow and a software update policy. Deploy Microsoft 365 apps and agreed business applications. Enrol and validate all approximately 20 MacBooks, securing business data before any device reset. 3.6 Microsoft Defender for Business Onboard all enrolled devices through Intune and configure next-generation protection, attack surface reduction, alerting and reporting. Connect device risk signals to Conditional Access. 3.7 Apple Business Manager assessment and setup Create or verify the ABM account, complete Apple organization verification, and link ABM to Intune and Entra ID. Configure Automated Device Enrolment profiles and the Apps and Books token. Document per-device eligibility and recommend a future procurement path so new MacBooks enrol automatically. 3.8 Knowledge transfer and documentation Involve the SGR IT Manager throughout configuration. Deliver hands-on administrator training covering the admin center, Entra ID, Exchange Online, Intune, ABM and Defender. Deliver a short end-user readiness session with a written guide before cutover. Produce as-built documentation, an administrator runbook (including joiner and leaver procedures), support procedures and a handover report. 3.9 Post-go-live support Provide 30 days of included support from handover, covering defects, migration follow-up, enrolment issues and IT Manager assistance. Propose optional support arrangements beyond the 30 days, priced separately. 4. Deliverables Each deliverable will be accepted by SGR against the criteria below. Migration acceptance is a separate, explicit sign-off after post-cutover validation. # Deliverable Acceptance criteria D1 Discovery and assessment report Complete inventory of users, groups, shared drives, third-party integrations and devices, with measured data volumes and rated risks D2 Migration plan and implementation schedule Approved by SGR; includes data mapping, cutover runbook, test plan, rollback triggers and communication plan D3 Configured Microsoft 365 tenant Entra ID licensed; all users registered for MFA; SSPR live; break-glass accounts documented; Conditional Access enforced with no unintended lockouts D4 Exchange Online implementation Mail flow tested inbound and outbound; SPF, DKIM and DMARC configured; protection policies applied D5 Teams implementation Teams, channels and policies deployed; meetings, chat and external access tested D6 Intune implementation Enrolment, compliance and configuration profiles deployed and validated on pilot devices D7 macOS device enrolment and management All in-scope MacBooks enrolled, FileVault enabled with keys escrowed, every device compliant D8 Microsoft Defender for Business implementation All enrolled devices onboarded and reporting; alerting configured; no unresolved high-severity alerts at handover D9 Apple Business Manager setup and recommendations ABM created and linked to Intune; enrolment profile configured; per-device eligibility and procurement recommendations documented D10 Google Workspace data migration Mail, calendar and Drive content migrated and validated; exceptions logged and accepted by SGR D11 IT Manager training Training delivered and signed off by the SGR IT Manager; sessions recorded on request D12 As-built documentation and support procedures Configuration documents, administrator runbook and end-user guide reviewed and accepted by SGR D13 Project handover report Handover session completed; open items listed with owners and dates D14 30 days post-go-live support Support delivered from handover date, closed with a review of Secure Score, device compliance and open items 5. Timeline and Migration Approach The assignment should be completed within a maximum of six (6) weeks from contract signing, followed by 30 days of post-go-live support. Bidders must submit a detailed work plan; the phasing below is indicative. Phase Key activities Indicative duration 1. Discovery and migration design Google Workspace audit, device inventory, migration and rollback plan, SGR sign-off Week 1 2. Tenant build and security baseline Entra ID, MFA, Conditional Access (report-only), Exchange, Teams, SharePoint, Intune, Defender, ABM, Purview Weeks 2 to 3 3. Pilot, data migration and cutover Pilot group, bulk data pre-stage, device enrolment, cutover weekend, day-one support Weeks 4 4. Stabilization and handover Monitoring and tuning, residual items, training, documentation, handover Weeks 5 to 6 The approach must respect these principles: Build alongside, then switch. The Microsoft 365 tenant is configured and tested while staff keep working in Google Workspace. Single-weekend cutover. The production cutover happens over one weekend, on a date approved by SGR that avoids month-end, audits and major events. Phase gates. No phase starts until SGR signs off the previous one; no user data moves before the tenant is accepted. Defined rollback. A written rollback plan with go/no-go criteria is agreed and tested before go-live. Google Workspace retained. Google Workspace stays licensed and available until SGR formally accepts the migration. 6. SGR Responsibilities SGR will provide: Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 administrator access for the duration of the project. Access to DNS hosting, or a person able to make DNS changes during the cutover window. Confirmation that Microsoft 365 Business Premium nonprofit licences are active and sufficient. SGR's D-U-N-S number and an authorized contact for Apple Business Manager verification. Two to three pilot users, and access to all MacBooks for scheduled enrolment. Timely decisions and sign-offs within the turnaround agreed at kick-off. 7. Out of Scope On-premises infrastructure deployment, configuration or management. Windows device management (the estate is macOS only). Custom application development, including rebuilding Google Apps Script automations. 8. Key Personnel The bidder must propose a team with, at minimum: Role Minimum qualification Minimum experience Lead consultant / project lead Degree in IT, computer science or related field; Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert or equivalent 7 years, including at least 2 Microsoft 365 migrations as lead Endpoint engineer Microsoft Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate or equivalent; Apple/macOS management experience 3 years in system administration and device management Security engineer Relevant Microsoft security or identity certification (e.g. SC-300, SC-200) 3 years in system administration or security operations 9. Technical Proposal Requirements Company profile, registration documents and Microsoft Partner evidence Understanding of the assignment and proposed methodology Detailed work plan and timeline, including the proposed cutover weekend approach Proposed migration tooling and how it handles the 1.2 TB volume, Google API throttling and Google-native file conversion Rollback plan with go/no-go criteria Proposed security baseline, mapped to Microsoft recommendations or the CIS Critical Security Controls, stating any controls not covered Approach to enrolling existing MacBooks not eligible for Automated Device Enrolment Training and knowledge transfer plan Risk register with mitigations Assumptions and SGR responsibilities Post-implementation support options beyond the included 30 days Team composition, CVs and certifications 10. Financial Proposal Requirements The financial proposal must be submitted in RWF and must show: Section Content required A. Migration and implementation services Itemized by phase or service area, at standard commercial rates B. 30-day post-go-live support Confirmed as included, or priced if not C. Optional items Each optional item (Section 7) priced separately The bidder must also state the quotation validity period and proposed payment terms. 11. Evaluation Criteria Criterion Weight Methodology, work plan, cutover and rollback approach 25% Experience with similar Microsoft 365 migrations and macOS management (references) 20% Qualifications and certifications of key personnel 15% Security baseline, training and knowledge transfer plan 10% Pricing competitiveness and transparency 25% Experience with NGOs or the development sector 5% IV. Standard Provisions Guidelines, policies and ethics. All bidders must commit to the SGR Procurement Procedures Manual, the SGR Anti-terrorism and Anti-money Laundering Policy, and the SGR Anti-fraud, Bribery and Corruption Policy. Conflict of interest and disqualification. Bidders shall disclose any relationship with SGR staff and shall not submit more than one bid. SGR will disqualify any bidder that attempts to influence the process improperly, colludes with other bidders, engages in bribery, is blacklisted by the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority or SGR, has corruption-related convictions, unresolved contract disputes or is in bankruptcy proceedings. Bids received late, incomplete, with unsigned handwritten amendments, or with misleading information will also be disqualified. Data protection and confidentiality. The selected provider will have administrative access to SGR systems and data. It must sign a confidentiality and data processing agreement, comply with Rwanda's Law No. 058/2021 on the protection of personal data and privacy, use access only for this assignment, and return or remove all credentials and data at handover. Evaluation and award. The contract will be awarded through quality and cost-based selection to the responsive bidder with the highest combined score. SGR may request clarifications, a presentation of the proposed approach, or negotiate with any bidder before award. Withdrawal. SGR reserves the right to withdraw this tender at any time without notice or liability, and to accept or reject any bid without giving reasons. Tender costs. Bidders bear all costs of preparing their bid, whether or not successful. Notification of award. All bidders will receive formal notification of the outcome. Bid validity. Bids shall remain valid for 60 days from the submission deadline. V. Guideline for Bid Submission Interested and qualified firms must submit separate technical and financial proposals electronically to recruitment@sustainablegrowers.org not later than 23 October 2026 at 5:00 PM (17h00) local time. Late bids will be automatically rejected. Questions may be sent to the same address no later than 21 October 2026 at 5:00 PM (17h00) local time. Only written answers issued by SGR are official; verbal information from SGR staff is not binding. SGR may request further information from any bidder, and failure to respond by the stated deadline may lead to disqualification. Done at Kigali, on 13 October 2026 Christine Condo Chief Executive Officer, Sustainable Growers

title: Expression of Interest (EoI) for Supply of Office Cleaning Materials
raw_text: Expression of Interest (EOI) SUPPLY OF OFFICE CLEANING MATERIALS. Reference Number: 7000025573 Publication date: 15.10.2026 Introduction The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH is a federally owned international cooperation enterprise for sustainable development with worldwide operations. The GIZ Office in Kigali covers GIZ’s portfolio in Rwanda and Burundi. GIZ Rwanda/Burundi implements projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Union and other commissioning authorities in the following priority areas: Sustainable Economic Development; Good Governance; Climate, Energy and Sustainable Urban Development; Digitalization and Digital Economy; and regional projects in the Great Lakes Region. The GIZ Office in Kigali is responsible for financial, administrative, and human resource management functions covering the GIZ activities in Rwanda and Burundi. GIZ intends to engage a reliable supplier to supply cleaning materials regularly, as and when the need arises. Scope of services The selected supplier is expected to perform the following scope of work. Supply of cleaning materials and supply procedure The supplier is responsible for the supply of cleaning materials (such as toilet paper, paper towels, detergents and soaps, disinfectants, glass cleaners, air fresheners, mops and mopping cloths, brooms, dustbins and other cleaning consumables and equipment) as per the demand received from GIZ project offices in Rwanda. Purchase orders may be combined or may be for even a single unit, as and when the requirement arises for any category of items, under our framework agreement. GIZ will issue a purchase order indicating the needed items and the respective quantities. The format of the purchase order will be agreed upon after the EoI procedure has been finalized. Once a purchase order is issued, the supplier is responsible for delivering the respective items within up to 5 working days after accepting the confirmed purchase order. The successful supplier shall deliver the items to any GIZ office location throughout Rwanda. However, GIZ's offices in Kigali will remain the major delivery points, as indicated in each order. Quantitative requirements The quantities of cleaning materials to be ordered under this framework agreement are indicative and non-binding. They have been estimated based on the average monthly consumption of cleaning materials by the GIZ Office in Kigali over the previous two (2) years (2024 and 2025), as summarized in the table below. These figures are provided for the supplier’s planning purposes only and do not constitute a guaranteed order volume. Actual quantities ordered during the agreement period will depend on GIZ’s actual needs and may be higher or lower than the estimates below. title: Request for Proposals for Recruiting a Consulting Firm to Undertake an Assessment and Develop Actionable Recommendations for Strengthening and Scaling Up the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS) in Rwanda
raw_text: ACCESS TO FINANCE RWANDA Request for Proposals For RECRUITING A CONSULTING FIRM TO UNDERTAKE AN ASSESSMENT AND DEVELOP ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR STRENGTHENING AND SCALING UP THE NATIONAL AGRICULTURE INSURANCE SCHEME (NAIS) IN RWANDA. Subject of Procurement: RECRUITING A CONSULTING FIRM TO UNDERTAKE AN ASSESSMENT AND DEVELOP ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR STRENGTHENING AND SCALING UP THE NATIONAL AGRICULTURE INSURANCE SCHEME (NAIS) IN RWANDA. Procurement Reference Number: AFR/RFP-STRENGTHENING NAIS/OCT/2026. Date of Issue: OCTOBER 16, 2026 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS PROCUREMENT REFERENCE NUMBER: AFR/RFP-STRENGTHENING NAIS/OCT/2026. 1. Background and Rationale The Government of Rwanda launched the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS) in 2019 as a flagship agricultural risk-financing instrument to protect farmers against insured crop and livestock losses, strengthen resilience, and facilitate access to agricultural finance. The Scheme is implemented through a public-private partnership bringing together Government institutions, insurers, reinsurers, financial institutions, farmer organizations, veterinarians, loss assessors, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders. NAIS has now transitioned from its establishment phase into a consolidation and scale-up phase, marked by expanded coverage across crop and livestock value chains, growing awareness and uptake of agricultural insurance, increased claims support to affected farmers, and strengthened collaboration among sector stakeholders. However, important challenges remain around insurance literacy and uptake, product relevance and affordability, claims experience, data quality and availability, digitalization, integration with agricultural finance, actuarial and reinsurance arrangements, subsidy sustainability, and effective monitoring and evaluation. Against this backdrop, MINECOFIN, MINAGRI, and AFR intend to undertake an independent assessment to evaluate progress made to date, identify key achievements, lessons learned, and persistent gaps, and generate practical, evidence-based recommendations to inform the strengthening and revamping of the next phase of the NAIS. The assessment will be aligned with NST2, PSTA5, Vision 2050, the Financial Sector Development Programme, the National Insurance Strategy, Rwanda’s Disaster Risk Financing priorities, and relevant international good practices, ensuring that the future design and implementation of NAIS is responsive to Rwanda’s evolving agricultural risk landscape and broader financial resilience objectives. 2. Objective of the assessment The overall objective of the assessment is to generate a robust evidence base and practical, prioritized, and actionable recommendations to guide Rwanda in strengthening and transitioning the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS) into a modern, sustainable, inclusive, market-oriented, and climate-smart agricultural risk-financing instrument. The assessment will evaluate the Scheme’s performance, achievements, and contribution during the InsuResilience Solutions Fund (ISF) and Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation (CDAT) implementation period; assess its value for money, financial and fiscal sustainability, market-development effects, and broader economic additionality; and identify the operational, financial, institutional, regulatory, and policy reforms required for the next phase. It will inform measures to improve farmers’ protection against agricultural risks; crowd in private capital and capabilities; deepen the agricultural insurance market and generate positive spillovers for the wider insurance sector; expand access to credit and other financial services; stimulate productive investment, enterprise growth, and commercialization; strengthen climate resilience and inclusion; and contribute to food security, improved rural livelihoods, and sustainable agricultural transformation. 2.1 Specific Objectives The assessment will pursue the following specific objectives: Assess NAIS performance, resilience, and development outcomes: Evaluate progress against the Scheme’s strategic objectives; assess its contribution to farmers’ risk resilience, recovery, livelihoods, and broader agricultural development outcomes; identify achievements, lessons, implementation challenges, and persistent gaps; and assess the effectiveness of operational, institutional, policy and governance arrangements. Assess the relevance, effectiveness, quality and inclusiveness of products and delivery: Evaluate product suitability, affordability, coverage, basis risk and performance in addressing farmers’ evolving risks; assess awareness, uptake, renewal, retention and satisfaction; and review the efficiency, timeliness, transparency and accessibility of enrolment, underwriting, loss assessment, claims settlement and digital delivery, with results disaggregated where feasible by sex, age, farm size, geography, value chain and vulnerability. Assess value for money, financial sustainability, and fiscal affordability: Evaluate public expenditure on premium subsidies and scheme administration against economy, efficiency, effectiveness, equity, additionality, and sustainability; analyse subsidy incidence, leverage of farmer premiums and private capital, unit costs and benefits, fiscal risks, and alternative scale-up scenarios; and assess pricing, claims, reinsurance, and risk-sharing arrangements. Where monetization is feasible, estimate indicative benefit-cost or social-return measures; otherwise, apply a transparent value-for-money scorecard. Assess agricultural insurance and wider insurance-market development: Determine NAIS’s contribution to market depth, competition, product and distribution innovation, insurer and reinsurer participation, professional and data capabilities, geographic and value-chain reach, farmer retention, and unsubsidized uptake. Examine whether public support crowds in or crowds out commercial products and investment, the potential pathway toward reduced dependence on subsidies, and evidenced spillovers to the broader insurance market, including rural distribution, digital infrastructure, insurance awareness, consumer trust, and uptake of other suitable insurance products. Assess private-sector growth, access to finance and economic additionality: Examine whether NAIS facilitates entry, investment and continued participation by insurers, reinsurers, financial institutions, intermediaries, aggregators and technology providers; assess its contribution to farmers’ and agribusinesses’ access to credit and other financial services, productive investment, adoption of improved and climate-smart technologies, enterprise growth and value-chain development; and clearly distinguish observed associations and plausible contribution pathways from causal attribution. Benchmark NAIS and identify strategic reform and innovation opportunities: Benchmark NAIS against relevant regional and international good practices; identify transferable lessons and practical opportunities for institutional, regulatory, product, delivery, digital, financial, and climate-risk-management reform; and define priority actions aligned with NST2, PSTA5, Vision 2050, the Financial Sector Development Programme, the National Insurance Strategy and Rwanda’s disaster risk-financing priorities. Develop a practical reform and implementation framework for the next phase of NAIS: Translate findings into a prioritized and sequenced implementation roadmap with clear responsibilities, indicative timelines, resource requirements where feasible, implementation risks, and a results-based Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning framework covering operational, financial, market-development, economic, inclusion, resilience, and broader development outcomes. Interested bidders must confirm their intention to submit a bid by Wednesday October 21, 2026, at 17h00 HRS CAT Any requests for clarifications to the RFP may be submitted by Monday, October 26, 2026, 17h00 HRS CAT. Bidders should submit their proposals no later than Thursday November 5, 2026, 17:00 HRS CAT Responding bidders are advised that this solicitation does not in any way obligate AFR to make a contract award or compensate the responding firms for any costs associated with the preparation and submission of their proposals. Additionally, AFR may award a contract without conducting negotiations; all proposals should be submitted initially using your most favorable terms. AFR reserves the right to award any resultant contract to other than the offeror submitting the lowest price proposal based on technical excellence, schedule superiority or client request. title: Request for Proposal for Supply, Installation, Testing and Commissioning of 30 kV / 0.4 kV Power Supply Infrastructure and a 315 kVA Distribution Transformer
raw_text: easyHATCH Ltd ("the Company" or "the Client") operates a poultry farm in Cyuve Sector, Musanze District, Rwanda. The farm's continued development requires a dedicated medium-voltage (MV) grid connection and an on-site distribution transformer. Following the Energy Utility Corporation Limited (EUCL)’s issued Supervision Quotation for the Power Supply to easyHATCH Ltd, setting out the technical design for the connection and a Bill of Quantities (BoQ) for the materials required. EUCL's quotation is for design supervision and final testing/commissioning oversight only. ! Purpose of this RFP easyHATCH Ltd is seeking competitive proposals from qualified, RURA-approved electrical contractors to supply all materials, and to install, test and commission the complete MV/LV power supply infrastructure described in Section 2 below — including the supply, installation and commissioning of the 315 kVA transformer — in accordance with EUCL's approved technical design and Rwanda's electricity-sector technical standards, and to EUCL's satisfaction at final witness testing. Kindly download the attached document for full details. Attachment attachment_file_5b0780f65112b34d7e83
