title: Tender Notice for Supply, Delivery, Testing and Commissioning of Six (6) 500 Kva Generator Sets (Goods)
raw_text: NOTICE OF INVITATION TO TENDER N° A-RWA030-2026-8534 Title: Supply,Delivery,Testing and Commissioning of Six (6) 500 kVA Generator Sets (Goods) In the framework of project RWA/030 receiving financial support from the governments of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and Rwanda This notice of invitation is launched by and according to the procedures of LuxDev, the Luxembourg Development Cooperation Agency, on behalf of project RWA/030 receiving financial support from the governments of Rwanda and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. 1. Identification and financing of the Project/Programme Title: Project RWA/030 - Improving skills for holistic employment in modern agriculture (ISHEMA) Source of financing: The government of Rwanda and the government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg as set out in the project’s/programme’s bilateral agreement n° dated 18/10/2024. Status of financing: Approved 2. Identification of the Contract Type of contract: Goods Object: Supply, Delivery, Testing and Commissioning of Six (6) 500 kVA Generator Sets Number: A-RWA030-2026-8534 Number of lots: 2 Lot 1: Generator Sets, Synchronizing/Transfer Equipment and Associated Services Lot 2: Civil Works, External Electrical Works and Fuel Infrastructure Grouping of lots: possible, a tenderer may be awarded more than a single lot if he satisfies, cumulatively, the administrative and technical requirements of the lots to which he is tendering. 3. Eligibility and evaluation criteria Origin: No restriction Eligibility: Economic operators satisfying the criteria included in the statement of good standing and in the ethics clauses of the general regulations. Evaluation: The most economically advantageous tender on the basis of price, administrative and technical criteria for both options diesel and gas and incoterm DAP will be granted the contract. Variants: variants will be considered 4. Location and timeframe Location of the project: Rwanda Terms and place of delivery: as per the technical specifications, Incoterm will DAP (Kinazi TSS, Gitwe TSS and Mutobo TSS in Rwanda). The final destination and installation of the equipment will be to 3 (three) sites in Rwanda: Mutobo Technical Secondary School (Mutobo TSS) in Musanze District, Kinazi Technical Secondary School (Kinazi TSS) in Ruhango District and Gitwe Technical Secondary School (Gitwe TSS) in Ngoma District. Performance period of the contract (per lot and not cumulative in case of award of several lots to the same tenderer) is 6 (six) months. commencing from the date indicated in the administrative order to commence services and ending with provisional acceptance. Final acceptance and warranty obligations shall be governed by Articles 40 and 42 and shall survive the performance period. Validity period of tenders: 120 days from the time limit for receipt of tenders 5. Vendors or Companies owner must not be employed by PIH or One PIH within five past years, unless PIH seeks their expertise for consultancy services based on proven specialized knowledge. Submission of multiple bids by related or affiliated entities under the same beneficial ownership shall constitute a breach of tender participation rules. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 950,000,001 to RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.5%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 500,000,001 to RWF 950,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.0%. title: Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Supply of Office Consummables
raw_text: Project/Activity Name Heifer International Rwanda Agresso Work order: RW0000 Country: Rwanda Advertisement for Procurement Request for Quotation (RFQ) Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a Nonprofit and International Non-governmental Organization with the mission to alleviate hunger and poverty, while caring for the environment through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become the flagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. Heifer International Rwanda partners with smallholder farmers to build sustainable livelihoods by empowering them to use their own energy, ingenuity, and dreams to fuel their success out of hunger and poverty. Heifer programs mobilize communities and foster the organization of associations, cooperatives and social networks while strengthening their capacity to address development challenges. Purpose and Objective The main objective of this tender is to ensure the timely, reliable, and consistent supply of office consumables. The selected supplier(s) will support Heifer’s daily office operations by providing quality products that meet the organization’s requirements, ensuring availability, convenience, and a conducive working environment for staff and visitors. All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their Bids, marked with clear subject line: “SUPPLY OF OFFICE CONSUMMABLES”to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 26th October 2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time. title: Prequalification of Suppliers and Update of the Food, Goods & Services Vendor Roster
raw_text: 29 September 2026 PREQUALIFICATION OF SUPPLIERS AND UPDATE OF THE FOOD, GOODS & SERVICES VENDOR ROSTER EOI number: RWA26NF005 A. Background 1. The United Nations World Food Programme hereinafter referred to as the “WFP”, with its Headquarters located in Via C.G. Viola, 68/70, 00148 Rome, Italy is the leading humanitarian organization saving lives and changing lives, delivering food assistance in emergencies and working with communities to improve nutrition and build resilience by assisting almost 100 million people in around 83 countries each year. 2. The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), Rwanda Country Office, invites qualified and experienced companies to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for prequalification and possible inclusion in its Food, Goods and Services Vendor Roster. This exercise is intended to broaden WFP Rwanda’s supplier base, attract new and capable market participants, align the roster with the current WFP procurement taxonomy, and update the information and continued interest of suppliers already included in the roster. 3. IMPORTANT FOR CURRENT ROSTER SUPPLIERS Existing suppliers that have not responded to WFP Rwanda solicitation invitations during the period from 1 January 2026 to the date of this EOI are required to re-apply if they wish to remain under consideration for future procurement opportunities. Existing suppliers whose company information, ownership, contacts, legal documents, banking details, capacity, or service offering has changed are also required to respond and submit updated information. A current roster entry does not constitute automatic confirmation or renewal. B. Categories Covered by the EOI Suppliers may apply under the WFP procurement taxonomy shown in Annex 1. Applicants must select the category or categories that accurately reflect their demonstrated legal mandate, technical capacity, experience, staffing, equipment, and financial capability. A supplier may apply for a maximum of TWO (2) Level 3 categories across the entire EOI C. Mandatory Cover Letter Instructions The signed cover letter must clearly state: the applicant’s full legal name and registration number; whether the applicant is a new supplier or is already included in the WFP Rwanda vendor roster; the exact taxonomy selection for each application: Level 1 category, Level 2 category, and Level 3 category; a maximum of two Level 3 categories for which the supplier seeks prequalification; a brief explanation of the supplier’s relevant capability and experience for each selected category; and the name, title, telephone number, and email address of the authorized focal point. Applications that do not clearly identify the selected category or that apply for more than two categories may be considered non-compliant. D. Eligibility and Minimum Qualification Criteria Legally registered and authorized to operate in the relevant field. Valid tax registration and tax compliance status. Demonstrated relevant experience in each category applied for. Adequate technical capacity, qualified personnel, equipment, systems, and operational capability. Adequate financial capacity to perform potential contracts. Ability to comply with applicable WFP contractual, ethical, safeguarding, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, sanctions, health, safety, environmental, and quality requirements. No conflict of interest that would compromise participation in a WFP procurement process. E. Submission Requirements Signed cover letter meeting Section 3 requirements. Completed supplier information form, including legal name, physical address, contacts, ownership, and authorized representative. Valid certificate of registration/incorporation and relevant operating licences. Valid tax registration and tax clearance/compliance certificate. Company profile describing core business, years of operation, staffing, facilities, equipment, geographic coverage, and organizational structure. Evidence of relevant experience for each category applied for, such as contracts, purchase orders, completion certificates, or client reference letters. Audited financial statements for the most recent three financial years, or acceptable alternative evidence where audited statements are not legally required, subject to WFP review. Current bank details and bank reference letter, where requested during due diligence. UNGM registration number, if available. Suppliers not yet registered may be requested to register at a later stage. For existing roster suppliers, a declaration confirming whether company information remains unchanged or identifying all updates since the last submission. All supporting documentation listed above shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions provided in the EOI and submitted via email to rwa.procurement@wfp.org referencing the subject ‘’Response to EOI ref. No RWA26NF005’’. The deadline for response to this request for EOI: (Friday, 31st October 2026, 1700hrs, Kigali Time) WFP will not consider incomplete or unsigned submissions. All responses and supporting documentation received will be treated as strictly confidential and will not be made available to the public. This request for EOI does not constitute a solicitation. WFP reserves the right to change or cancel this procurement process or any of its requirements at any time during the process; any such action will be communicated to all participants. Should you have any questions please do not hesitate to contact us at rwa.procurement@wfp.org. Evaluation Process: After the deadline for submission of responses has passed, WFP will evaluate responses received and will notify eligible participants of the outcome of the evaluation. Eligible suppliers will be invited to participate in the bidding process for the proposed tender. Sincerely, _________________________________ Hien ADJEMIAN Head of Supply Chain World Food Programme, Rwanda Attachment attachment_file_fc8effb2172e2e62a77f attachment_file_adc538086e91ba10ab5e

title: Invitation for Expressions of Interest (EoI) for Provision of Project Management Consultancy Services for Electronic Security Systems Projects
raw_text: ISCO SECURITY LTD INVITATION FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (EOI) PROVISION OF PROJECT MANAGEMENT CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR ELECTRONIC SECURITY SYSTEMS PROJECTS 1. Background ISCO Security Ltd is a leading private security company and systems integrator engaged in the design, supply, installation, configuration, integration, testing, commissioning and maintenance of security technologies, including CCTV surveillance systems, access control systems, intrusion alarm systems, fire detection and fire alarm systems, X-ray baggage scanners, walk-through and hand-held metal detectors, electric fencing, public address systems, perimeter security systems, integrated security management systems and video management systems, together with related electronic and low-voltage solutions. ISCO Security delivers projects of varying size and complexity for government institutions, financial institutions, private companies, NGOs, industrial facilities, hospitality establishments, educational institutions, healthcare facilities and other organisations. In line with its commitment to excellence, sound project governance and professional project delivery, ISCO Security intends to establish a pool of highly qualified Project Management Consultants to be engaged on a project-by-project basis. 2. Objective of the Consultancy The objective is to engage Project Management Consultants who will provide professional project management and technical oversight services across the full project lifecycle, from initiation and planning through execution, testing, commissioning, handover and close-out, ensuring that assignments are delivered to the agreed scope, schedule, budget, quality standards and technical specifications, with effective stakeholder coordination and client satisfaction. 3. Eligibility Expressions of Interest are invited from: Individual Consultants Consulting Firms Applicants must be legally constituted or registered to provide consultancy services and must be in good standing with all applicable statutory and regulatory authorities. 4. Technical Expertise Required Demonstrated working knowledge of the design, installation, integration, testing and commissioning of CCTV and video management systems, access control, intrusion detection, fire detection and alarm systems, screening and detection equipment, perimeter protection, public address systems and integrated security management platforms; together with applicable international standards, structured cabling, network infrastructure, power and earthing requirements, and factory and site acceptance testing regimes. 5. Brief Description of the Assignments Selected consultants will be engaged on a project-by-project basis. The duration of each assignment will correspond to the duration of the assigned project and will therefore vary according to project scope, complexity and contractual timelines. Assignments will typically comprise project planning and scheduling, cost control, procurement and resource coordination, technical oversight, site supervision, quality assurance, technical compliance verification, scope, risk, issue and change management, stakeholder coordination, chairing and recording of project meetings, monitoring of installation, testing and commissioning, and structured project reporting. Consultants will report to the ISCO Security Project Steering Committee. 6. Submission Deadline Expressions of Interest must be received no later than 23rd October 2026 at 17:00 Hrs via email: recruitment@isco.co.rw Done at Kigali, on 08 October 2026. _____________________________ Nepo. title: Terms of Reference for Partners’ M&E Systems Assessment and Analysis
raw_text: Terms of Reference for Partners’ M&E Systems Assessment and Analysis I. Background Information Trócaire Rwanda has received funding from Irish Aid under the five-year Ireland’s Civil Society Partnership (ICSP) 2023–2027 funding scheme. The grant runs from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2027 and contributes to the vision of A Better World, while supporting transformation at community level across Trócaire’s country programme. Through this funding, and in collaboration with its partners, Trócaire Rwanda works to advance climate and environmental justice and women’s empowerment through local action and global advocacy. The programme supports rural communities to build sustainable and resilient livelihoods and strengthen their capacity to withstand disasters. It also promotes the protection, voice, and influence of women and girls, including prevention of and response to gender-based violence, while supporting women’s leadership and participation in decision-making at all levels. In addition, Trócaire Rwanda is committed to strengthening partnerships with local organizations by advancing meaningful localization, where power and responsibility are increasingly shifted to local and national actors to deliver effective, relevant, timely, and appropriate support to communities. As part of its partner capacity-strengthening agenda, and in response to identified gaps and partner needs, Trócaire Rwanda seeks to support partners to strengthen project and programme delivery by improving their M&E systems. This support aims to ensure that partners have practical, context-responsive systems that generate reliable evidence for programme management, learning, accountability, and decision-making. Trócaire Rwanda will engage a professional consultant with expertise in monitoring and evaluation systems to assess and analyse partners’ existing M&E systems. The assessment will determine system availability, functionality, strengths, gaps, and improvement needs, and provide practical, partner-specific recommendations on whether to strengthen existing systems, adapt available digital solutions, or adopt new systems where appropriate. The assessment will focus on 5 of the 12 ICSP partners, including Caritas Gikongoro, ARCT-Ruhuka, BIOCOOR, The Green Protector, CEJP. The findings will inform partner-specific recommendations and guide future decisions on M&E system strengthening and digitalization support. II. Overall Objective To assess each selected partner’s M&E system, identify key strengths and gaps, and recommend the most suitable system-strengthening options to improve monitoring, reporting, data management, learning, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making. III. Specific Objectives Assess the current availability, structure, functionality, and use of M&E systems within each selected partner organization. Identify key strengths, gaps, risks, and improvement needs related to data collection, storage, analysis, reporting, documentation, data quality, and evidence use. Analyse each partner’s operational context, programme requirements, staff capacity, reporting obligations, data volume, and readiness for system strengthening or digitalization. Recommend the most appropriate M&E system option for each partner, including whether to strengthen an existing system, adapt an available solution, or introduce a new system. Provide a clear roadmap for partner-specific M&E system strengthening, including priority actions, required resources, estimated costs, and implementation considerations. IV. Scope of work The consultant will assess and analyse the M&E systems of selected Trócaire Rwanda ICSP partners. The assignment will identify each partner’s current system status, gaps, improvement opportunities, and the most suitable system option based on needs, capacity, context, and affordability. a) Assessment of existing M&E systems and partner needs The consultant will review each partner’s M&E tools, processes, databases, reporting templates, data flows, documentation practices, and data use mechanisms. The assessment will identify what is available, functional, missing, or requiring improvement to support effective monitoring, reporting, learning, accountability, and decision-making. b) Analysis of suitable M&E system options and cost considerations The consultant will compare available system options against agreed criteria, including relevance, affordability, ease of use, adaptability, data security, interoperability, reporting functionality, scalability, maintenance requirements, sustainability, and staff capacity. The analysis should guide Trócaire Rwanda’s decisions on partner-specific M&E system strengthening and investment priorities. The assignment will include the following key tasks: 1. Partner M&E system assessment Assess each partner’s existing M&E system, including data collection, storage, analysis, reporting, documentation, data quality assurance, feedback mechanisms, and evidence use. Consult partner organizations to understand business processes, user needs, reporting requirements, capacity gaps, and system expectations. Map each partner’s current data flows, tools, data volume, reporting processes, and system-related risks. 2. Gap analysis and system requirements Analyse strengths, weaknesses, gaps, duplication, risks, and opportunities for improving each partner’s M&E system. Define partner-specific functional, technical, data management, reporting, dashboard, data protection, and user access requirements. 3. System option analysis and recommendations Review and compare suitable M&E system options for each partner, including existing systems, adaptable digital solutions, open-source tools, subscription-based platforms, and new system development where necessary. Assess each option against relevance, affordability, usability, adaptability, data security, sustainability, scalability, interoperability, maintenance requirements, and partner readiness. Recommend the most suitable M&E system option for each partner, with clear justification and practical implementation recommendations. 4. Roadmap and reporting Prepare partner-specific assessment profiles summarising current system availability, gaps, priorities, and recommended solutions. Develop a consolidated assessment and analysis report outlining M&E system availability, key gaps, practical solutions, and partner-specific recommendations. Present findings and recommendations to Trócaire for validation and management decision-making. V. Methodology The consultant will use a participatory, analytical, and user-centred approach that reflects partners’ operational realities, M&E practices, reporting requirements, user capacities, and system-strengthening priorities. The assignment will include document review, M&E system mapping, tool review, gap analysis, option appraisal, validation, and reporting. The methodology should explain how the consultant will engage partner staff, assess existing M&E systems, document current practices, identify gaps, compare system options, and validate findings. It should also outline the assessment roadmap and show how recommendations will be tailored to each partner. Recommendations should be practical, affordable, sustainable, and aligned with each partner’s staffing capacity, data volume, programme complexity, system infrastructure, and long-term M&E needs. Applicants must submit a detailed technical methodology and work plan outlining the proposed assessment approach, stakeholder engagement process, analysis framework, system option appraisal criteria, quality assurance measures, risk mitigation strategies, deliverables, and timeline. VI. Expected outputs and results An approved inception report setting out the assessment methodology, work plan, system assessment criteria, and stakeholder engagement approach. Partner-specific M&E system assessment profiles showing current system availability, functionality, strengths, gaps, risks, and improvement priorities. A consolidated gap analysis report covering key M&E system gaps, practical solutions, and sustainability considerations. A comparative analysis of suitable M&E system options for each partner, covering availability, gaps, improvement needs, adaptability, usability, security, scalability, maintenance, and sustainability. A final assessment and analysis report with clear recommendations on the most appropriate M&E system solution for each partner, including justification and practical implementation considerations. VII. Duration of the assignment The assignment is expected to be completed within three weeks (21 days). This period will cover partner system review, assessment, analysis, validation, and reporting of findings. VIII. Reporting and Supervision Arrangements The consultant will report to and receive regular support from Trócaire’s Monitoring, Inclusion, and Learning Advisor (MILA), in close consultation with relevant Trócaire staff and partner organizations. Regular progress check-ins will be held to review assessment progress, address risks, validate emerging findings, and confirm next steps. The consultant will be expected to maintain close coordination with selected partner organizations throughout the assessment, analysis, validation, and reporting process. IX. Safeguarding All consultants working with Trócaire are required to sign and comply with Trócaire’s safeguarding and data protection principles. Any breach of these principles by the consultant or team members may result in immediate contract cancellation. X. Consultant Qualifications and Experience Advanced degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Information Systems, Data Management, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Statistics, Project Management, or a related field. Proven experience in assessing, analysing, designing, or strengthening M&E, MIS, PMIS, or digital data management systems for development or humanitarian programmes. Strong understanding of monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning systems, including indicator tracking, reporting workflows, data quality assurance, dashboards, and evidence use. Demonstrated experience in systems assessment, gap analysis, business process mapping, requirements analysis, option appraisal, and preparation of practical recommendations. Experience facilitating consultations with NGOs, local partners, programme teams, and system users. Knowledge of data protection, information security, confidentiality, and responsible data management practices. Excellent analytical, facilitation, report-writing, and communication skills; knowledge of Kinyarwanda is an added advantage. XI. Evaluation Criteria for Selecting the Consultant Relevant academic qualifications and professional experience in M&E systems, information systems, data management, or related fields. Demonstrated experience conducting M&E system assessments, gap analyses, requirements analysis, or digital system option appraisals, preferably in NGO or development contexts. Quality, clarity, and practicality of the proposed methodology, work plan, assessment tools, and analysis framework. Capacity to provide partner-specific, realistic, affordable, and sustainable recommendations for M&E system strengthening. Value for money based on the financial proposal and the quality of the technical offer. XII. Application procedures Applicants should su bmit a technical proposal, financial proposal, CV or company profile, tax clearance certificate, three references, and relevant work completion certificates by 22nd October 2026 to inforwanda@trocaire.org.

title: Terms of Reference (ToR) for the Consultancy to Develop Adolescent Health Audio-Visual Materials for the National ASRH Programme
raw_text: CALL FOR PROPOSALS PLAN/ FY27/10/001 Terms of Reference (ToR) for the Consultancy to Develop Adolescent Health Audio-Visual Materials for the National ASRH Programme 1. Background The National Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health (ASRH) Programme aims to improve adolescents’ knowledge, access to quality services, and adoption of positive health behaviors. To support national training, awareness creation, and behavior change communication, there is a need for high-quality, youth-friendly, culturally appropriate, and inclusive Adolescent Health (AH) audio-visual materials. These materials will be aligned with national policies and guidelines and used by the Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC), implementing partners, and other stakeholders. 2. Purpose of the Consultancy The purpose of this consultancy is to develop technically accurate, engaging, and validated adolescent health audio-visual materials to support national ASRH training, communication, and community engagement activities. 3. Scope of Work Under the overall coordination of the Rwanda Biomedical Center and with procurement and financial management by Plan International Rwanda, the consultant will undertake the following tasks: A. Script Development Develop clear, youth-friendly, and gender-responsive scripts covering priority adolescent health and Sexual Reproductive Health Rights (SRHR) topics. Ensure alignment with national Adolescent Sexual Reproductive Health (ASRH) policies, standards, and cultural context. B. Script Review and Validation Workshop Organize and facilitate a script review workshop with approximately 15 ASRH/SRHR experts, including youth representatives, for 3 days. Revise and finalise scripts based on consolidated feedback. C. Production of Audio-Visual Materials Produce audio-visual sketches based on validated scripts, including casting, filming, voice recording, editing, and post-production. Ensure professional quality suitable for training, community outreach, and digital dissemination. D. Validation of Final Materials Organize a One-day validation meeting to review produced materials for 20 people, including ASRH technical working group and the communication team. Integrate final comments and submit approved materials to RBC. 4. Key Deliverables The quality, accuracy, age appropriateness, cultural sensitivity, language suitability, and inclusiveness of the materials will be reviewed and validated by RBC in collaboration with ASRH TWG members and communication team. The content package should comprehensively address adolescent SRHR topics relevant to adolescents and young people in all their diversity, including: - Relationships - Values, rights, and sexuality - Gender and power - Violence prevention and staying safe - Human body and adolescent development - Sexuality and sexual behavior - Sexual and reproductive health Content should be illustrated through short sketches and role plays. Expected Deliverables: Deliverable Format Details Draft scripts MS Word Scripts divided into short sketches/role plays, including topic, objective, target audience, and key messages. Submitted to RBC for review. Script review workshop report and final scripts MS Word Report of technical inputs from ASRH TWG and revised, validated scripts. Draft audio-visual materials Video files Draft videos produced from validated scripts and submitted to RBC for review. Final audio-visual materials Video files (soft copy + 2 CDs) Finalized videos incorporating RBC feedback. One copy for Plan International and one for RBC. Final consultancy report MS Word Summary of process, outputs, lessons learned, and final deliverables. 5. Duration and Timeline The consultancy will be implemented within 45 working days from the date of contract signature, based on an agreed work plan. Activity Timeline Working Days Responsible Key Participants Tendering process 15–28 October 2026 14 days Plan International Rwanda Plan International Rwanda Background checks and contracting 29/09–04 November 2026 5 days Plan International Rwanda Plan International Rwanda, RBC, Consultant Inception meeting (shared understanding of scope, roles, and expectations) 05 November 2026 1 day Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC) RBC, Plan International Rwanda, Consultant Script development and submission 06–16 November 2026 10 days Consultant Consultant, RBC Collection and incorporation of feedback; final script submission 17–30 November 2026 12 days Consultant Consultant, RBC Video preparation, production, and submission of draft materials 01–18 December 2026 15 days Consultant Consultant, RBC Addressing RBC comments and submission of final audio-visual materials 21–31 December 2026 8 days Consultant Consultant 7. Payment Schedule Payments will be made by Plan International Rwanda in two instalments, subject to RBC approval of key milestones: 30% Inception report (details on how the assignment will be done) 40% upon approval of the final scripts 30% upon the approval audio visual materials and submission of the final report The total contract amount is inclusive of all taxes and costs. The consultant is responsible for all statutory obligations, production costs, travel, workshops, and any other related expenses. 8. Consultant Qualifications The consultant or firm should demonstrate: At least 5 years of demonstrated experience in developing and writing scripts for films, videos, or audio-visual content targeting adolescents and young people. Demonstrated experience in casting, directing, and working with adolescent and/or youth actors in the production of films or video content for young audiences. Submission of at least 3 relevant, high-quality video/film productions previously developed, preferably on adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), or related youth issues, for assessment of the quality and relevance of the work. Experience facilitating technical review and validation workshops. 9. Proposal Submission Requirements Interested applicants should submit the following documents: Provision of three recent completion certificates of similar assignments with video links attached. Experience of 5 years. Copy of RDB and VAT certificates Valid RRA Tax clearance and RSSB contribution clearance Cover letter expressing interest, Understanding of the ToR (maximum 2 pages) Proposed methodology and work plan (including timeline/Gantt chart) , Profile of the consultant/firm and key personnel - At least three certificates of similar assignments with links attached. Itemized consultant fees - Itemized workshop costs - Itemized production costs Experience of 5 years. Interested and qualified consultants should submit their offers in a sealed envelope, clearly marked “Consultancy to Develop Adolescent Health Audio-Visual Materials for the National ASRH Programme” in two hard copies (one original and 1 copy) at the reception of Plan International Rwanda – Kigali Country Office (Kacyiru), no later than 2:00 p.m. on 28th October 2026. Submissions should be addressed to: The Chairperson -Tender Panel Plan International Inc. Rwanda Golden Plaza Building, Floor # 4, KG 456 St P.O. Box 6211, Kigali, Rwanda. Done at Kigali on 15th October 2026

title: Request for Proposal for Consultancy for Agri-Enterprise Commercialization and Market Access Advisor
company: Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
raw_text: REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL RFP AGRA-RW-1092 CONSULTANCY FOR AGRI-ENTERPRISE COMMERCIALIZATION AND MARKET ACCESS ADVISOR Disclaimer |AGRA reserves the right to determine the structure of the process, number of short-listed participants, the right to withdraw from the proposal process, the right to change this timetable at any time without notice and reserves the right to withdraw this tender at any time, without prior notice and without liability to compensate and/or reimburse any party.Section 1: Synopsis of the Request for Proposal Solicitation Reference No. RFP AGRA-RW-1092 Title of Consultancy Consultancy for Agri-Enterprise Commercialization and Market Access Advisor Eligibility Open to all eligible Firms Issuing Office & Address AGRA Nairobi Point of contact for clarifications and questions AGRA, General ProcurementEmail: Procurement@agra.org Location of the assignment Rwanda Bid Submission Electronically via the AGRA Oracle SCM System. Refer to the Advertisement on our Website Solicitation Issue Date As per Open Date in AGRA’s Oracle SCM system Deadline for submission of questions and clarifications 20th October,2026 at 4pm Deadline for Answering questions and clarifications 12th October,2026 Deadline for Submission of Proposals As per Close Date in AGRA’s Oracle SCM system Type of Consultant Consultancy Firm Selection method Quality and Cost Based Selection method. 1. Introduction AGRA invites qualified consulting firms to submit proposals to bid for aConsultancy for Agri-Enterprise Commercialization and Market Access Advisor. This document outlines the requirements and guidelines for the submission of proposals. 2. Background AGRA is a not-for-profit organization working with African governments, other donors, NGOs, the private sector, and farmers to improve the productivity and incomes of resource-poor smallholder farmers in Africa. AGRA aims to catalyze an inclusive agricultural transformation in Africa by increasing incomes and improving food security for millions of smallholder farmers in Africa. For more information about AGRA, please visit www.agra.org. YEFFA supports young people to participate in agriculture as viable entrepreneurs across Rwanda. Phase 1 interventions, delivered through implementing partners, have equipped youth with production skills, value addition capabilities, business development services (BDS), financial literacy, and linkages to VSLAs and financial institutions. As enterprises mature, the principal constraint shifts from production capacity to commercialization. Youth-led and women-led enterprises continue to face challenges in securing reliable buyers, meeting market requirements, negotiating commercial agreements, accessing growth capital and integrating into competitive value chains. Women-led enterprises constitute a core target group; YEFFA commits to a minimum 70% participation rate. A defining feature of the YEFFA target population is that participants are predominantly underserved and economically excluded rural youth with limited formal education and business management experience. Many enterprises are not legally registered and operate informally. For the purposes of credit access, financial inclusion and collective marketing, enterprises are typically organized into cooperatives or youth groups. Any service provider engaged under this ToR must demonstrate a deep understanding of the peculiarities and complexities of working with such market actors, including their literacy levels, geographic dispersion, limited digital access and the trust dynamics that govern group-based economic activity. AGRA therefore seeks to engage a suitably qualified consulting firm to act as the strategic Commercialization and Market Systems Advisor for the entire YEFFA programme portfolio, facilitating the transition of youth-led and women-led enterprises from capability-building interventions into commercially viable and scalable agribusinesses. YEFFA Rwanda Commercialization Pathway The diagram below maps the structured progression from foundational capacity-building to sustainable commercial income for YEFFA-supported enterprises. The Commercialization and Market Systems Advisor will operate primarily across stages 5–8, while reinforcing upstream stages through feedback loops with implementing partners. Shaded cells (stages 5–8) indicate the primary mandate of the Commercialization and Market Systems Advisor. Stages 1–4 remain the responsibility of implementing partners, with the Advisor providing demand-side feedback to strengthen upstream programming. At stage 4, youths are expected to transition from subsistence to commercially oriented enterprises that will be sustainable long after the YEFFA programme. 3. Objectives General Objective To serve as the strategic commercialization instrument for the YEFFA programme, facilitating the transition of youth-led and women-led agribusiness enterprises from production-oriented activities into commercially viable and scalable businesses through structured market access, private sector engagement, enterprise readiness development and market-driven financing mechanisms. Specific Objectives Develop a national commercialization strategy for the YEFFA enterprise portfolio. Assess commercial readiness and develop structured enterprise readiness pathways for 16 anchor firms working with AGRA’s Implementing partners across Rwandan country Establish and manage a dynamic buyer engagement platform connecting youth enterprises to domestic, regional and export markets. Facilitate deal-making, contract negotiations and off-take arrangements in shared responsibility with implementing partners. Develop and implement an enterprise readiness framework aligning quality, compliance and packaging standards to market requirements. Leverage commercial market linkages to improve youth enterprise access to growth capital. Ensure inclusive commercialization with a minimum 70% participation by women-led enterprises. Convene a national YEFFA commercialization showcase event to demonstrate outcomes and attract investor and buyer interest. 4. Scope of Work and Workstreams The Advisor shall deliver four primary outputs that together constitute the strategic commercialization architecture for YEFFA. Actual transaction facilitation is a shared responsibility between the Advisor and implementing partners, with the Advisor providing frameworks, platforms and deal support, while implementing partners manage enterprise-level relationships on the ground. Scope of Work 1: Commercialization Strategy A national-level strategy defining the commercial positioning of the YEFFA portfolio, target value chains (chili, avocado, French beans, poultry, passion fruits, and maize )and market segments, competitive entry strategies for youth enterprises, aggregation and collective marketing models, and a phased commercialization roadmap. The strategy shall be context-sensitive to the realities of rural youth operating in group-based enterprise models. For the sake of helping AGRA Rwanda to achieve its intended results, the consultant will work closely with 19,651 who are identified as youth in work and 84,504 identified as work enabling outreach by connecting them with buyers, suppliers, aggregators, processors, and anchor firms, and track their sustainable social economic status throughout the journey. At the end of the day, the consultant will indicate the graduation levels in market facilitation as follows: Youth will be outreached through being given training, information about market access and awareness of local and internal market standards requirements Market-Readiness: The beneficiaries will be given the capacity to get local and international market certification. Market linkage: Youths will be connected to the buyers, aggregators, suppliers, through contract farming and job placement due to market facilitation. Youth in Work: Youth will be earning significant income through sales which might be increasing at the rate of 10%. (Employment, self-employment, entrepreneurship, or agricultural value-chain activities). Scope of work 2: Buyer Engagement Platform A structured, living market platform comprising: a buyer and market actor database; an active supplier/buyer engagement log; a framework for business-to-business (B2B) facilitation; and documented off-take arrangements and memoranda of understanding. The platform shall track the progression of enterprises from initial buyer introduction through to concluded commercial agreements, and shall be designed for handover and ongoing management by AGRA or implementing partners beyond the assignment period. Scope of Work 3: Enterprise Readiness Framework A practical framework enabling youth enterprises — including those organized as cooperatives and youth groups — to meet the quality, grading, packaging, traceability and compliance requirements of target markets. The framework shall include differentiated pathways for cooperatives versus individually operated enterprises and shall be operationally accessible to enterprises with limited formal education and administrative capacity. It shall also include a commercial finance readiness component facilitating access to growth capital. Scope of work 4: Deal Facilitation Support Structured support for the negotiation and conclusion of commercial agreements between youth enterprises and buyers, aggregators, processors, exporters and institutional purchasers. The Advisor shall lead deal structuring and documentation while implementing partners provide ground-level enterprise support. The Advisor shall maintain a deal pipeline tracker and report on transaction value, number of agreements concluded and finance mobilized. Workstream 5: Women’s Economic Empowerment All outputs shall be designed with an explicit gender lens. The Advisor shall identify barriers facing women-led enterprises in accessing commercial markets, design targeted commercialization solutions, and track and report gender disaggregated outcomes throughout the assignment. Workstream 6: YEFFA Commercialization Showcase Event Towards the close of the assignment, the Advisor shall plan and convene a national YEFFA Commercialization Showcase Event. The event shall bring together youth and women entrepreneurs, buyers, financial institutions, government representatives and development partners to demonstrate the commercial outcomes of the YEFFA portfolio, facilitate business matching, attract investment and generate evidence for programme scale-up and replication. The Advisor shall be responsible for event design, participant mobilization, facilitation and post-event reporting. The consultant will be responsible for tracking the event outcome such as participation target, buyer engagement, and clear guidance on YEFFA Commercialization pathways. Workstream 7: Financing Strategy For the sake of improving the aspect of access to finance, the financing pathway for at least 16 anchor firms will be performed, including bankability assessments and tailored financing solutions such as working-capital loans, asset finance, guarantees, and blended finance. The Advisor should engage at least 4 commercial banks, 3 SACCOs/MFIs, and 2 investors or guarantee providers, while maintaining a pipeline of at least 30 enterprises from assessment and application through approval and disbursement. To strengthen accountability, the TOR could target at least 20 enterprises receiving actual financing and USD 1 million in finance mobilized, measured through the existing growth-capital and finance-mobilization KPIs. Workstream8: The consultant will establish the digital commercialization platform by leveraging existing e-commerce, digital trading, traceability, and market intelligence platforms relevant to the targeted enterprises and value chains. The Advisor should also facilitate the use of these existing tools to support buyer identification, market information, product promotion, traceability, and commercial transactions, without developing new digital systems that can capture the progress of market facilitation mechanisms through the number of enterprises using existing digital platforms and the buyer linkages or transactions facilitated through them 5. Methodology The Advisor shall adopt a participatory and market-systems-based methodology. Recognizing the specific context of working with underserved rural youth organized in cooperatives and informal youth groups, the methodology should prioritize trust-based engagement, simplified business communication tools, community validation processes and gender-responsive facilitation approaches. Core methodological elements include: Desk review of programme data, enterprise profiles, enterprise-viability models for the target value chains/agri-enterprises and market intelligence. Stakeholder consultations with enterprises, buyers, financial institutions, government and development partners. Enterprise diagnostics and commercial readiness assessments adapted for low-literacy and cooperative contexts. Market systems analysis to identify systemic barriers and leverage points. B2B facilitation events, trade fairs and structured buyer engagements. Pilot testing of enterprise readiness tools and frameworks. Validation workshops with implementing partners and youth enterprise representatives. Continuous learning reviews and adaptive management. 6. Deliverables The four primary outputs are embedded within the following deliverables schedule. Payment milestones are tied to accepted deliverables. No Deliverable Description of the deliverable Expected delivery time (days/months) 1. Inception Report & Detailed Workplan Day 14 10% 2. Commercial Readiness Assessment Report Day 45 30% 3. Market Intelligence and Opportunity Mapping Report Day 75 4. Buyer and Market Actor Engagement Platform (database + engagement log) Day 90 5. Commercialization Strategy (national scope) Day 120 15% 6. Enterprise Readiness Framework (quality, compliance, packaging standards) Day 150 7.
